children.translated_text: Now, the first chapter.
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of all worlds, the sovereign who performs the eight [acts] beginning with creation —

children.text: yathā sasarja nikhilaṃ tanme brūhi jagadguro // PS_1,1.1 //
children.translated_text: tell me, O teacher of the universe, how he created everything. (PS 1.1.1)
<s>Śrī Haṃsa</s> said:
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, of infinite power, full of bliss, imperishable, self-sovereign —
his body is of infinite nature, consisting of knowledge and bliss — thus says the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture). (PS 1.1.2)
Of that independent, great-souled <s>Hari</s>, in his entirety —

children.text: svarūpaṃ naiva jānanti ramābrahmādayopi tu // PS_1,1.3 //
children.translated_text: even <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), <s>Brahmā</s>, and the others do not know his true form. (PS 1.1.3)

children.text: tathāpi te pravakṣyāmi yathā jānāsi tatvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, I shall declare to you so that you may know the truth.
For him whose desires are fulfilled, there is no purpose in creation and the rest. (PS 1.1.4)
Such is his nature — for that purpose, the unborn one performs it.
He alone is the Lord, the self, the controller of the moving and the unmoving. (PS 1.1.5)
The Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), in the form of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, as <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>,
the sovereign Lord, consumed the cosmic egg along with all its coverings made of <s>Prakṛti</s>. (PS 1.1.6)
Then, all the conscious beings — both those liberated in the previous <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle) and those bound —
the Lord, self-luminous, placed them within his own belly and rested happily without sleeping. (PS 1.1.7)
The extent of the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>) endowed with ten coverings is the measure;
of equal extent is <s>Śrī</s>, who has the form of the Lord. (PS 1.1.8)
To that extent, the earth had form, like a banyan leaf, as it was before;
<s>Durgā</s> was of that limited extent, having the form of darkness. (PS 1.1.9)
At that time, apart from <s>Ramā</s>, nothing else existed in the external realm;
all souls dwelt then in the womb of the child named <s>Śūnya</s> (the Void). (PS 1.1.10)
The liberated ones, situated above the navel in his belly, manifest in the great abode;
those fit for liberation are in the middle of the belly; the eternally bound are below the navel. (PS 1.1.11)
The lower gods are at the region of the hip; those who have attained suffering are above that;

children.text: vasanti kḷptānandaste muktā bhuñjanti netarāḥ // PS_1,1.12 //
children.translated_text: those [with] assigned bliss dwell — the liberated ones enjoy, not the others. (PS 1.1.12)
Those who are to be attained through dissolution alone — <s>Mādhava</s> shall give to them;
setting aside the bliss to be attained, for those who enjoy only assigned bliss. (PS 1.1.13)
<s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and other sport [realms] having been set aside, <s>Hari</s>'s dwelling is in the womb;
during dissolution, the 'destruction' of all liberated ones is thus described, O lotus-born one. (PS 1.1.14)
Worthy of experiencing pleasure and pain and the like, having the nature of desire and knowledge,
the multitudes of souls are engaged in aversion, <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>adharma</s> (vice), and effort. (PS 1.1.15)
All souls, bound by the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>), move about during creation;
having attained a state of equilibrium, endowed with the subtle body. (PS 1.1.16)
During dissolution, they dwell in the Lord's womb; the former power then —
at that time, all such beings enter deep sleep. (PS 1.1.17)

children.text: laya ityucyate sadbhiḥ na layosti svarūpataḥ /
children.translated_text: By the wise, it is called dissolution (<s>laya</s>), but dissolution does not truly exist in essence;
the powers of knowledge and expression abide in the essential nature of all souls. (PS 1.1.18)
The power of bestowing knowledge through the activity of mind, as held by <s>Śruti</s> —

children.text: layejīvādyabhāvena sā śaktiḥ kuṇṭhitā bhavet // PS_1,1.19 //
children.translated_text: during dissolution, due to the absence of souls and the rest, that power becomes dormant. (PS 1.1.19)
For the <s>Śrutis</s> (scriptures), which stand at the place of the all-pervading Lord's cognition, such is dissolution;
for the insentient [matter] of the cosmic egg and the souls, it is designated as the unmanifest sky (<s>avyākṛta</s>). (PS 1.1.20)
That which is the substratum at the time of creation becomes dormant during dissolution;
the destruction of this unmanifest realm is what is called dissolution. (PS 1.1.21)
Of all subtle bodies, in accordance with their respective <s>karmas</s>,

children.text: nānāyoni prāpikāsti śaktiḥ sṛṣṭau laye na tu // PS_1,1.22 //
children.translated_text: there is a power that leads to various wombs during creation, but not during dissolution. (PS 1.1.22)
The power that bestows pleasure and pain upon all who have performed actions

children.text: sṛṣṭau laye na sā viṣṇorājñayā kuṇṭhitā bhavet // PS_1,1.23 //
children.translated_text: exists during creation; during dissolution, it becomes dormant by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s command. (PS 1.1.23)
Such indeed is his dissolution — it is not regarded as dissolution of essential nature;
in phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>), the power of expressing all languages is acknowledged. (PS 1.1.24)

children.text: sṛṣṭau na sāsti pralaye teṣāṃ nāśo hi tādṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: During creation that [power] does not exist [independently]; during dissolution, their destruction is of such a nature;

children.text: tamaḥ sthānāṃ pūrvakḷptaduḥkhabhogo layaḥ smṛtaḥ // PS_1,1.25 //
children.translated_text: for those stationed in darkness (<s>tamas</s>), the experience of previously assigned suffering is regarded as dissolution. (PS 1.1.25)
Of the subtle body made of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), and of insentient <s>Prakṛti</s> itself,
of the subtle and gross [elements], and of the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) in their entirety — (PS 1.1.26)

children.text: sraṣṭṛtvaśaktiḥ sṛṣṭau hi na laye syattato layaḥ /
children.translated_text: the creative power exists during creation, not during dissolution; therefore dissolution [means]:

children.text: hitvā jagatsarjanādyaṃ sarvadā śrīpatau ratiḥ // PS_1,1.27 //
children.translated_text: setting aside the creation of the world and the rest, there is always delight in the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>. (PS 1.1.27)
The extremely close attendance [upon <s>Hari</s>] is declared to be the dissolution of <s>Lakṣmī</s>;
of the non-eternal and non-conscious, whether inside or outside the cosmic egg — (PS 1.1.28)
the burning by the fire of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, gradually, is called destruction;

children.text: deśataḥ kālato vyāptā varṇāsarvepi śāśvatāḥ // PS_1,1.29 //
children.translated_text: pervading in space and time, all phonemes are eternal. (PS 1.1.29)
Insentient <s>Prakṛti</s> is eternal; the insentient atom (<s>aṇu</s>) too
pervades in space and time; [all are] of non-conscious nature, always [dependent on] <s>Śrī Hari</s>. (PS 1.1.30)
Infinitely lower in qualities [than the Lord], yet infinite in qualities relative to the Lord —
during dissolution, all dwell having taken refuge, with their powers diminished. (PS 1.1.31)
In the Lord of complete power, infinite in space and time,
<s>Hari</s> always has infinite forms of atomic measure. (PS 1.1.32)
Non-different from that, <s>Hari</s> the supreme has infinite subtle and gross forms;
having the form of all souls, with subtle and gross natures. (PS 1.1.33)
Having the form of all insentient [matter], with infinite forms upon forms, the teacher of the universe;
<s>Hari</s>, non-different from infinite [forms] within infinite [forms], is without [material] qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>). (PS 1.1.34)
With hands and feet everywhere, the Self, with eyes, heads, and faces everywhere,
possessing all sense organs everywhere, he stands pervading everything. (PS 1.1.35)
With infinite non-material sense organs and forms, supremely wondrous,
unattached yet omniscient, without [material] qualities yet filled with [divine] qualities. (PS 1.1.36)
Outside and inside all beings, both unmoving and moving,
unmanifest yet having manifest form, the good one, witnessed by the righteous. (PS 1.1.37)
Though one, he appears as many, eternally real, of great bliss,
knowable through infinite <s>Vedas</s>, the sovereign Lord who performs the eight [acts] beginning with creation. (PS 1.1.38)
Independent, greatly describable, of infinite forms, having a consciousness-body;
situated in one place within his own infinite body of pure consciousness. (PS 1.1.39)
Having entered <s>yoganidrā</s> (yogic sleep), yet sleepless, the Lord in his own state;
<s>Hari</s>, during dissolution, having burned the accumulation of the cosmic egg and its coverings — (PS 1.1.40)
having made the material cause one with <s>Prakṛti</s>, the Man-Lion (<s>Nṛkesarin</s>),
from <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>-<s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, [the forms] headed by <s>Aniruddha</s> [enter] through the mouth — (PS 1.1.41)
having burned the accumulation of all subtle bodies, the Lord of all,
the unborn one merges into the subtle bodies the elements that served as their material cause. (PS 1.1.42)
Then <s>Śrī</s>, the supreme consort, became the form of a bed;
<s>Durgā</s> became the form of a covering for <s>Hari</s> of immeasurable brilliance. (PS 1.1.43)
Enjoying only his own good qualities, he remained unwake yet as if deeply asleep;
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, with the liberated ones having enjoyed [bliss] in his belly, of infinite radiance. (PS 1.1.44)
Self-luminous, in his own state, through <s>yoganidrā</s>, he rested upon the banyan leaf;
at the time of creation, all souls, afflicted by various sufferings, (PS 1.1.45)
wander about; for the cessation of the respective toil of all souls,

children.text: laye svāpaṃ prāpayati liṅgabaddhān svadehagān // PS_1,1.46 //
children.translated_text: during dissolution, he causes the subtle-body-bound ones dwelling in his own body to sleep. (PS 1.1.46)
The many [souls], confused by beginningless ignorance, <s>karma</s>, and dispositions,
those to be created, of diverse kinds, situated in a hierarchy, of three types — (PS 1.1.47)
those of light sleep, those of great sleep, and those endowed with deep sleep;
the liberated who enjoy consciousness-bliss, and the <s>asuras</s> (demons) who always experience suffering — (PS 1.1.48)

children.text: tamaḥsaṃsthān sadā baddhān jaṭhare sthāpya keśavaḥ /
children.translated_text: the eternally bound ones stationed in darkness — having placed them in his belly, <s>Keśava</s>
rested upon the banyan leaf, the Lord, as if performing sleep. (PS 1.1.49)

children.text: teṣu sṛjyān svayaṃ sṛṣṭvā yathāyogyaphalaṃ vibhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Among those to be created, having himself created them, the all-pervading Lord,

children.text: sukhaṃ miśraṃ tathā duḥkhaṃ dātumaicchallayāntime // PS_1,1.50 //
children.translated_text: desired to give appropriate fruit — happiness, mixed, and suffering — at the end of dissolution. (PS 1.1.50)
The eighth part of dissolution is called the end of dissolution;

children.text: laye samāliṅya hariṃ vinidrā parameśvarī // PS_1,1.51 //
children.translated_text: during dissolution, having embraced <s>Hari</s>, the supreme sovereign goddess, sleepless — (PS 1.1.51)
or when [he] sleeps, she rests near the ocean of eternal bliss;
in the eighth part of dissolution, the goddess <s>Śrī</s>, dependent yet independently — (PS 1.1.52)
being awakened by the command of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, she began to praise [him].
Infinite in space and time, yet devoid of infinite [material] qualities, (PS 1.1.53)
she, the beloved of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, surpasses <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> by tens of millions of qualities;
during dissolution and creation, she presides over all eternal substances. (PS 1.1.54)
Performing the eight [acts] beginning with creation by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s command, of infinite forms,

children.text: chāyeva sūkṣmasthūloru rūpaṃ viṣṇuṃ samāśritā // PS_1,1.55 //
children.translated_text: like a shadow, she rests upon <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of great subtle and gross forms. (PS 1.1.55)
Knowing directly the qualities of <s>Viṣṇu</s> proclaimed in infinite <s>Vedas</s>, and even those beyond them,
she who presides over all the <s>Vedas</s> [knows them all]. (PS 1.1.56)
Of indescribable beauty, presiding over all souls,
<s>Śrī</s>, the liberated one, shining, presides over the pure ones fit for liberation. (PS 1.1.57)
Red among all the bound ones who are red, she presides over them;
dark blue among the unfit souls, she is <s>Durgā</s>, presiding [over them]. (PS 1.1.58)
<s>Prakṛti</s> — in <s>Prakṛti</s>, she instigates equilibrium, disequilibrium, and the like;
unbroken in devotion to the Lord, among the insentient she takes insentient form. (PS 1.1.59)
Of conscious form among conscious beings, among women she instigates feminine activities and the like;
of masculine form, supreme, yet devoid of male nature. (PS 1.1.60)
Devoid of a body made of the unmanifest and its effects, being of such nature,

children.text: svayaṃ śrīḥ viṣṇubhāvajñā vedaistuṣṭāva vedavit // PS_1,1.61 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> herself, knowing the nature of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, praised him through the <s>Vedas</s>, she who knows the <s>Vedas</s>. (PS 1.1.61)
Those <s>Vedas</s> — the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Atharva</s> — are under <s>Śrī Hari</s>'s control;
even the four, separately by kind, are infinite and free from defects. (PS 1.1.62)
With <s>udātta</s> and other accents, meanings of words, and the arrangement of phonemes,
with <s>visarga</s>, <s>bindu</s>, and other preceding [elements], with collections of qualities fit for sound — (PS 1.1.63)
from beginningless time, free from the words 'iṣat' ('slightly') [i.e., free from deficiency],

children.text: sāṃśā samastadeśeṣu vyāptāḥ śuddhajaḍāḥ sadā // PS_1,1.64 //
children.translated_text: partial, pervading all regions, always purely insentient. (PS 1.1.64)
Devoted to declaring the qualities of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, free from defects of word,
the capacity of being known and making known — in them, the expression of contrary meanings (PS 1.1.65)
and obscurity and the like — these faults of discourse do not exist in them at all;
having the form of sound (<s>dhvani</s>), at the time of creation, abiding in speech, under the control of the deity of speech. (PS 1.1.66)
During dissolution, they are under <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s control; during creation, by <s>Brahmā</s> and other presiding [deities],

children.text: rakṣitāḥ pralaye sṛṣṭāvekarūpā bhavanti hi // PS_1,1.67 //
children.translated_text: they are protected; in dissolution and creation, they exist in one form. (PS 1.1.67)
Infinite in infinite number, and conducive to the knowledge of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
infinite and pervading all regions, they abide in the throat of that bow-bearer (<s>Śārṅgin</s>). (PS 1.1.68)
Being sung forth from the throat, according to the fitness of the souls,
they reveal the knowledge of their respective true natures, by the will of <s>Śrī Hari</s>. (PS 1.1.69)
Eager to produce cognitive knowledge, and [for] the unfit, they indicate non-knowledge;
having the form of sound, they are the object of the witness-endowed mind and ear alone. (PS 1.1.70)
They are reflections of the archetype (<s>bimba</s>) of <s>Hari</s>, who is the essence of all sounds;
<s>Durgā</s>, having the form of sound, present in the <s>Vedas</s>, is of infinite forms. (PS 1.1.71)
Knowing the person to be awakened, she praised the Supreme Person;
of infinite self and infinite power, manifesting the eternal hosts of <s>Śrutis</s> beginning with <s>Oṃkāra</s>, (PS 1.1.72)
at the time of creation, she instructed <s>Durgā</s> regarding them.
In the eighth part of dissolution, of the creator of the <s>Vedas</s>, the Lord of the universe — (PS 1.1.73)
<s>Oṃkāra</s> first became manifest, filled with the Lord;
au, ma, <s>nāda</s> (resonance), and <s>bindu</s> (dot) — of voiced, voiceless, and extra-voiceless nature. (PS 1.1.74)
Those whose nature is <s>Viśva</s> and the rest, those who are denoted [by it], those who abide in it, the supreme ones —
<s>Oṃkāra</s> denotes the Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>); its constituents are eternally of pure consciousness. (PS 1.1.75)
They are the denoters of the forms of <s>Hari</s>: <s>Viśva</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, <s>Prājña</s>, <s>Turya</s>,
the inner self, the supreme self, and those of the nature of knowledge-self. (PS 1.1.76)
By the words <s>tāra</s> (the syllable 'a') and <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), the one denoted is called <s>Oṃkāra</s>;
called the eight-syllabled [mantra] of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, it arose from the syllables within <s>tāra</s>. (PS 1.1.77)
Then became manifest <s>Viśva</s> and the rest; all the manifest [forms] of <s>Viśva</s> and the others —
The deities proclaimed are those expressible by <s>Nārāyaṇa's</s> <s>manus</s> (sacred formulas). // PS_1,1.78 //
From the first four syllables of the <s>tāragarbha</s> (seed of the praṇava) arose the <s>manu</s>;
called <s>vyāhṛti</s> (sacred utterance), <s>Aniruddha</s> and others are those arisen from <s>Viśva</s> and the rest — thus they are declared. // PS_1,1.79 //
Manifested by the <s>tāragarbha</s> syllables, the fifty <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) are declared;
a, ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa — likewise ya and śa — eight are enumerated. // PS_1,1.80 //
The eight <s>varṇas</s> arising from a-kāra are the sixteen vowels, as recognized;
the five <s>varṇas</s> of the ka-group are proclaimed as arising from u-kāra. // PS_1,1.81 //
The five <s>varṇas</s> of the ca-group are proclaimed as arising from ma-kāra;
the five <s>varṇas</s> of the ṭa-group are recognized as arising from <s>nāda</s> (resonance). // PS_1,1.82 //
The five <s>varṇas</s> of the ta-group are enumerated as manifested by <s>bindu</s> (dot);
the five <s>varṇas</s> of the pa-group arise from <s>ghoṣa</s> (voiced sound). // PS_1,1.83 //
The four <s>varṇas</s> of the ya-group become manifest from <s>śānti</s> (peace);
from <s>atiśānta</s> (supreme peace), the five <s>varṇas</s> of the śa-group have arisen. // PS_1,1.84 //
By the combination of ka and ṣa, kṣa is manifested — it is also called another syllable;
of the fifty <s>varṇas</s>, the eight <s>tāra</s>-syllables, with their deities — // PS_1,1.85 //
beginning with <s>Viśva</s> and the rest, in order, are manifested; the deities beginning with <s>Aja</s> are recognized;

children.text: aja ānanda indreśa ugra ūrja ṛtambharaḥ // PS_1,1.86 //
children.translated_text: <s>Aja</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Indreśa</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Ūrja</s>, <s>Ṛtambhara</s>, // PS_1,1.86 //
<s>Ṝgha</s>, <s>Ḷśa</s>, <s>Lṝjira</s>, <s>Ekātma</s>, <s>Airojobhṛt</s>, <s>Aurasa</s>,
<s>Antordhagarbha</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Khapati</s>, <s>Garuḍāsana</s>, // PS_1,1.87 //
<s>Gharma</s>, <s>Aṅgasāra</s>, <s>Cārvaṅga</s>, <s>Chandogamya</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>,
<s>Jhaḍitāri</s>, <s>Ñamaṣṭaṅkī</s>, <s>Ṭhalaka</s>, <s>Ḍaraka</s>, <s>Ḍharī</s>, // PS_1,1.88 //
<s>Ṇātmā</s>, <s>Tārastha</s>, <s>Podaṇḍī</s>, <s>Dhanvī</s>, <s>Namya</s>, <s>Para</s>, <s>Phalī</s>,
<s>Bali</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Manu</s>, <s>Yajña</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣīpati</s>, <s>Vara</s>, // PS_1,1.89 //
<s>Śāntasaṃvit</s>, <s>Ṣaḍguṇa</s>, <s>Sārātmā</s>, <s>Haṃsa</s>, and <s>Lāluka</s>;
these are proclaimed as expressible by all the <s>varṇas</s> beginning with a-kāra. // PS_1,1.90 //
<s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, expressible by kṣa, is the controller of all beings;
the <s>mātṛkā-mantra</s> (matrix-mantra), consisting of fifty-one <s>varṇas</s>, is thus declared. // PS_1,1.91 //
The eight <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> syllables, with the four <s>vyāhṛtis</s> in order,
[produced] the great twelve-syllabled <s>Vāsudeva</s> <s>mantra</s>, of the nature of the supreme self. // PS_1,1.92 //
The twelve beginning with <s>Keśava</s> are the deities of the syllables of that <s>mantra</s>;
the <s>mantras</s> uttered thrice by <s>Viṣṇu</s> arose from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. // PS_1,1.93 //
The <s>Gāyatrī</s>, with <s>Brahmā</s> as its seer, [arose] from doubling the twelve syllables;
the twenty-four deities of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> syllables begin with <s>Keśava</s>. // PS_1,1.94 //
From the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [arose] the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> (Hymn of the Cosmic Man); from the <s>sūkta</s>, the <s>Vaiṣṇava mantras</s>;
the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Cosmic Man) set forth by the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> is declared to be <s>Hari</s>. // PS_1,1.95 //
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, set forth by the <s>Viṣṇu-mantra</s>, is proclaimed as the Self of all;
the <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ), the eight <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, the <s>mātṛkā</s>, the twelve-syllabled [mantra], // PS_1,1.96 //
the <s>Gāyatrī</s> with <s>Brahmā</s> as its seer, and the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, and the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> [mantras] —
these eight are the great <s>mantras</s>, Vedic, bestowing all <s>siddhis</s> (perfections). // PS_1,1.97 //
From the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, the manifestation of all the <s>Vedas</s> arose — thus the <s>śruti</s> (scripture);
through <s>Durgā</s> of infinite forms, <s>Hari</s> as proclaimed by infinite <s>Vedas</s>, // PS_1,1.98 //
being entreated by her, the lord of all, fashioned the creation of his own self. // PS_1,1.99 //

children.text: iti śrī paratattavanirṇaye prakāśasaṃhitāyāṃ prathamaparicchede prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, in the determination of the supreme reality, the first chapter of the first section.
<s>Śrī Haṃsa</s> said:
The Blessed <s>Keśava</s>, being praised thus, rising up at that very moment,

children.text: śūnyanāmātha jagṛhe paruṣākhyāṃ tanuṃ hariḥ // PS_1,2.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> assumed the form called <s>Paruṣa</s> (Puruṣa), [which is] named <s>Śūnya</s> (Void). // PS_1,2.1 //
The <s>Puruṣa</s> (Cosmic Man) stood as the unmanifest seed of all forms;
he, of infinite self, with a pervading body, is called <s>Viśvakukṣi</s> (Womb of the Universe). // PS_1,2.2 //
From the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the four beginning with <s>Vāsudeva</s> came into being;
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, and <s>Aniruddha</s>. // PS_1,2.3 //
White, red, yellow, and blue are <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the others, in order;

children.text: muktyaihṛtyai tathā guptai sṛṣṭyai svecchātanurhariḥ // PS_1,2.4 //
children.translated_text: for liberation, for play, for protection, and for creation — <s>Hari</s> assumes forms by his own will. // PS_1,2.4 //
The goddess <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), named <s>Śūnya</s>, becoming <s>Śrī</s>, resorted to the <s>Puruṣa</s>;
she, becoming <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Ajayā</s>, <s>Kṛti</s>, and <s>Śānti</s> — thus she is declared. // PS_1,2.5 //
She was the wife of <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the others, always inseparable;
four-faced <s>Vāsudeva</s> is the image-form of <s>Brahmā</s>. // PS_1,2.6 //
<s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, thousand-faced, is the image-form of the serpent-king;
<s>Pradyumna</s>, of the nature of the image of <s>Māra</s> (Love), is of exceedingly beautiful form. // PS_1,2.7 //
<s>Aniruddha</s>, of the nature of the image of <s>Kāma's</s> son, is the face of <s>Aniruddha</s>;
beginning with the singular <s>dholkā</s>, the five-fold self, <s>Hari</s> has eight forms beginning with <s>Viśva</s>. // PS_1,2.8 //
He became of the nature of <s>Vimala</s> and others, having ten forms beginning with <s>Matsya</s> (Fish);
he became of twelve-fold self beginning with <s>Śakti</s>, having sixteen forms beginning with <s>Dvārakā</s>. // PS_1,2.9 //
He was of twenty-three forms beginning with <s>Ānanda</s>, the supreme beyond the supreme;
<s>Hari</s> became of twenty-four forms beginning with <s>Keśava</s>. // PS_1,2.10 //
Then the Supreme Person became of fifty forms beginning with <s>Aja</s>;
he became the sixty-first form called <s>Kāla</s> (Time), the controller of the year. // PS_1,2.11 //
He is of a hundred [forms] beginning with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, of a thousand beginning with <s>Viśva</s>;
he became of infinite forms beginning with <s>Para</s>, devoid of division of self. // PS_1,2.12 //
By his command alone, that goddess <s>Ramā</s> too [became] of many forms;
with her of infinite forms, the lord of <s>Ramā</s> is of infinite forms. // PS_1,2.13 //
Even of his own accord, with that goddess, for the sake of her delight, the treasure-house of compassion,
the supreme among men, having passed one-eighth of the time of dissolution, // PS_1,2.14 //
at the beginning of the time of creation, began to create <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā) and the others. // PS_1,2.15 //

children.text: iti śrī paratatvanirṇaye prakāśasaṃhitāyāṃ prathamaparicchede dvitīyodhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, in the determination of the supreme reality, the second chapter of the first section.
<s>Śrī Haṃsa</s> said:
When the radiance of sunrays, entering through the openings of a lattice as if seized by the planets, falls on the earth,

children.text: yadā bhavanti tasyāḥ samīpe tirgāsthitaḥ // PS_1,3.1 //
children.translated_text: one standing obliquely near it — // PS_1,3.1 //
the time during which a hair is raised from it — that is the <s>paramāṇu</s> (atomic unit of time) for mortals;
the foremost among mortals, through the ripening of devotion, is established among the great ones and above. // PS_1,3.2 //

children.text: yaṃ kālaṃ sūkṣmadṛgveda sa kālaḥ paramāṇukaḥ /
children.translated_text: The time-unit which the subtle-sighted perceives — that time-unit is the <s>paramāṇu</s>;

children.text: tacchatāṃśo hi devānāṃ tacchatāṃśobjajasya tu // PS_1,3.3 //
children.translated_text: its hundredth part is [the paramāṇu] of the gods; its hundredth part is that of <s>Brahmā</s> (the Lotus-born). // PS_1,3.3 //

children.text: bhūmau sthitānāṃ martyānāṃ yaḥ kālaḥ paramāṇukaḥ /
children.translated_text: That which is the <s>paramāṇu</s> for mortals dwelling on earth,
its hundredth part is the <s>paramāṇu</s> of one dwelling in the divine realm. // PS_1,3.4 //
Its ten-millionth part is [the paramāṇu] of <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), and its infinitesimal fraction is that of <s>Hari</s>;
this is called the <s>paramāṇu</s> — it is not perceived by others. // PS_1,3.5 //
The time-unit consisting of two <s>paramāṇus</s> is called <s>dvyaṇuka</s> (two-atomic);
that consisting of three <s>paramāṇus</s> is proclaimed as <s>tryaṇuka</s> (three-atomic). // PS_1,3.6 //

children.text: truṭiḥ tribhiśca tryaṇukaiḥ vedhaḥ syāttatrayeṇa tu /
children.translated_text: A <s>truṭi</s> is three <s>tryaṇukas</s>; a <s>vedha</s> would be three of those;
a <s>lava</s> is three <s>vedhas</s>; a <s>nimeṣa</s> (eye-blink) is three <s>lavas</s>. // PS_1,3.7 //
A <s>kṣaṇa</s> (moment) is said to be three <s>nimeṣas</s>; a <s>kāṣṭhā</s> is five <s>kṣaṇas</s>;
fifteen <s>kāṣṭhās</s> are proclaimed as a <s>laghu</s> (short unit of time). // PS_1,3.8 //
Fifteen <s>laghus</s> are proclaimed as a <s>vināḍikā</s>;
sixty <s>vināḍikās</s> constitute one <s>nāḍikā</s>. // PS_1,3.9 //
Thirty <s>muhūrtas</s> consisting of two of those are declared as one day-and-night (<s>ahorātra</s>);
seven <s>ghaṭikās</s> less one-eighth, plus seven, // PS_1,3.10 //
or seven-and-a-quarter, or seven-and-a-half,
a <s>yāma</s> (watch) is a time-unit of eight [ghaṭikās] also, as stated according to the variations of time. // PS_1,3.11 //
Four <s>yāmas</s> constitute the day; the same number constitute the night;
thirty day-and-nights make a <s>māsa</s> (month), consisting of two <s>pakṣas</s> (fortnights). // PS_1,3.12 //
Two of those make a <s>ṛtu</s> (season); three of those are proclaimed as an <s>ayana</s> (solstice-period);

children.text: karkādi kārmukānteṣu yadā carati bhaskaraḥ // PS_1,3.13 //
children.translated_text: when the sun moves through [the signs] from <s>Karka</s> (Cancer) to <s>Kārmuka</s> (Sagittarius), // PS_1,3.13 //
that is designated the <s>dakṣiṇāyana</s> (southern course), known as the night of the gods;
as long as the sun remains from <s>Nakra</s> (Capricorn) to the end of <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini), // PS_1,3.14 //
that period is designated by the wise as the <s>uttarāyaṇa</s> (northern course);
the year (<s>vatsara</s>), consisting of two <s>ayanas</s>, is known as consisting of twelve months. // PS_1,3.15 //
The year consists of three hundred and sixty day-and-nights;
by twenty-eight thousand and seventeen <s>lakṣas</s> (hundred thousands) of years, // PS_1,3.16 //
the <s>Kṛtayuga</s> (Golden Age) is reckoned; from that, the <s>Tretā</s> is said to be less by one-quarter —
amounting to twelve <s>lakṣas</s> and ninety-six thousand [years]. // PS_1,3.17 //
The <s>Tretāyuga</s>; then, less by one-quarter, the <s>Dvāpara</s> is declared —
amounting to eight <s>lakṣas</s> and sixty-four thousand [years]. // PS_1,3.18 //
From the <s>Dvāpara</s>, the <s>Kali</s> [is measured] as half-a-quarter;
the <s>Kali</s> consists of four <s>lakṣas</s> and thirty-two thousand [years]. // PS_1,3.19 //
<s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Dvāpara</s>, and <s>Kali</s> — these are the four <s>yugas</s>;
the time-unit consisting of four <s>yugas</s> is called a <s>mahāyuga</s> (great age). // PS_1,3.20 //
With forty-three <s>lakṣas</s> and twenty thousand years,

children.text: kḷptaḥ kālaḥ kāladṛgbhiḥ mahāyuga itīryate // PS_1,3.21 //
children.translated_text: this time-unit is reckoned by the knowers of time as a <s>mahāyuga</s>. // PS_1,3.21 //
Three hundred and sixty [human] years are declared as one year of the gods;
four thousand such years constitute [the yuga] called <s>Kṛta</s>. // PS_1,3.22 //
The <s>Tretā</s> is three thousand years; the <s>Dvāpara</s> is measured as two thousand years;
then the <s>Kali</s>, less [by a thousand], is measured as one thousand years. // PS_1,3.23 //
At the beginning and at the end of the <s>Kṛta</s>, separately, four hundred years each;
the junction-period at the beginning and end of the <s>Tretāyuga</s>, separately, three hundred years each. // PS_1,3.24 //
The junction-period at the beginning and end of the <s>Dvāpara</s>, separately, two hundred years each;
the junction-period at the beginning and end of the <s>Kali</s> is measured as one hundred years. // PS_1,3.25 //
Thus, by divine measure, twelve thousand years —

children.text: kḷptaḥ kālaḥ kālavidbhiḥ mahāyuga itīryate // PS_1,3.26 //
children.translated_text: this time-unit is reckoned by the knowers of time as a <s>mahāyuga</s>. // PS_1,3.26 //
In eighteen-and-a-half <s>lakṣa</s> years, seventy-one <s>yugas</s>
combined constitute the period of enjoyment of a <s>Manu</s> with his junction-periods — thus it is declared. // PS_1,3.27 //
The dissolution after <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [Manu] is measured as twelve hundred years;
for the six beginning with <s>Svārociṣa</s> and the others, the dissolution in between // PS_1,3.28 //
is a dissolution-period declared as consisting of fifteen hundred years;
a dissolution-period enumerated as consisting of fourteen hundred years. // PS_1,3.29 //
In the other <s>manvantaras</s> (Manu-periods), by rule, always in every case,
a thousand sets of four <s>yugas</s> is called a day of <s>Brahmā</s>. // PS_1,3.30 //

children.text: rītriśca tāvatī tasya ahorātrā tu tādṛśā /
children.translated_text: His night is of the same duration; such are his day-and-nights;
three hundred and sixty [such day-and-nights] are declared as one year of <s>Brahmā</s>. // PS_1,3.31 //
A period of one hundred such years is regarded as the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>;
from <s>Vāsudeva</s>, [Brahmā] received a subtle body — at this moment, within his hundred-year [lifespan], // PS_1,3.32 //
he who obtained a lifespan of one hundred years — forms other than his
arose from the previous [creation], after six years and three months. // PS_1,3.33 //
The subtle creation of the subtle portions of those to be created is by the four-formed one;
of those created first in subtle form, the gross body came thereafter. // PS_1,3.34 //
From <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, from <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā), from <s>Rudra</s>, in order, following the course of time,

children.text: yāvatāṃ sūkṣmataḥ sṛṣṭiḥ sthūlasṛṣṭistu tāvatā // PS_1,3.35 //
children.translated_text: for as many as there is subtle creation, for that many there is gross creation. // PS_1,3.35 //
Above the cosmic egg, the coverings, and the gross bodies are made of that [substance];

children.text: ādyasya brahmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ pañcāśadvatsarānti me // PS_1,3.36 //
children.translated_text: of the first <s>Brahmā</s>, at the end of the fiftieth year — // PS_1,3.36 //
when the day had passed, during his night, the creation of the cosmic egg took place;
within it, of <s>Viṣṇu</s> sleeping in the midst of the waters, // PS_1,3.37 //
from the world-containing <s>prākṛta</s> (primordial) lotus-bud arisen from the navel,
<s>Pādma</s> <s>Brahmā</s> arose together with thirty-seven [principles] in that. // PS_1,3.38 //
At the end of the day and during the night, the destruction of the cosmic egg of the lord of the world [occurs];
by the reverse order of the previous measure, the destruction of both gross and subtle [takes place]. // PS_1,3.39 //
Thus, when the full hundred-year lifespan is complete, [Brahmā's] lifespan consisting of two <s>parārdhas</s> (half-periods) —
And the unborn one himself brings about the unification of the self-forms.
For as long a time as the self-creation [endures], the unification lasts that long;
even when unified, he delights, and thus [delights in] the unified <s>māyā</s> (illusion).
For that same duration, thereafter the unborn one puts [all] to sleep, as if sleeping;
two and a half times six <s>Brahma</s>-years — thus is the rest [period] according to my [teaching].
In the [next] portion, as before, the Lord performs the self-creation and the like;
for that <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Being), no measure of lifespan is prescribed.
Thus, in time that is of such a nature — unlimited, infinite, with infinite supreme selves —

children.text: kāle bhāvinyapi hariḥ sṛṣṭyādīśaḥ kariṣyati // PS_1,3.44 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, even in the time yet to come, will perform creation and the like as Lord.
The boundary of this independent one cannot

children.text: laṅghituṃ pūrṇaśakterhi vaśe sarvaṃ carācaram // PS_1,3.45 //
children.translated_text: be transgressed by those who are dependent; for all that moves and does not move is under the control of the one of full power.
Those who, from infinite time, [experience] his death, birth, old age, and the like,
preceded by toil, suffering, misfortune, worry, and torment,
ignorance, envy, malice, affliction, desire, anger, fear, and the like,
emaciation, disease, sin, and the stain of merit and the like,
loss and gain of hope, hunger, thirst, trembling, and the like —
these faults did not exist [in him] nor will they ever exist in the Lord of all.
Whatever accumulations of faults are imagined by the various groups of wicked people —
opposite to those, [he possesses] infinite, full, auspicious qualities, the one who closes his eyes [in cosmic sleep].
Even the slightest trace of those faults does not [belong to] <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this is certain.
That which is time — from the atomic particle to the end of two <s>parārdhas</s> —
in all those times, the Lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), bearing the respective names,
and manifesting the respective capacities, the unborn Lord abides and protects.
This flow of time is eternal, but the moments and the like are non-eternal;

children.text: naṣṭeṣu satsukāleṣu vartamāneṣu vai kramāt // PS_1,3.52 //
children.translated_text: when the good times have passed and the present ones proceed in sequence,
he, whose essential nature is indestructible, is the protector of that flow.
The time measured as a hundred years of <s>Brahmā</s> is designated as '<s>para</s>' (supreme);
that same time is called a 'blink' and a 'day' of the Supreme Lord —
thus it is figuratively described for the purification of the intellects of the ignorant.
Therefore the greatly wise call the Lord infinite in terms of time.
Moreover, at the end of the supreme time, the all-pervading one, generating <s>Brahmā</s>,
accepts that time — this is [the nature of] the Lord of all.
Though devoid even of the measure of night, the Lord for that much time
conducts [the period] as night; thus the unborn one puts <s>Brahmā</s> and others to sleep.
At the last portion of the night, the Lord performs the self-creation and the like;
for that <s>Puruṣa</s>, the measure of lifespan is prescribed.
Thus, of such a nature — unlimited, infinite, with infinite supreme selves —
the creation and the like of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Supreme Self, the creator, are beyond time.
Like the essential senses, he who is time is devoid of form and the like.
When the earlier times have perished, others come into being
in subsequent [periods], from the flow of atomic particles that are yet to come.
Combining <s>ghaṭikās</s> (time-units) and the like, time should be known as uniform;
<s>ghaṭikās</s>, hours, months, and the like do not arise simultaneously.
For the one devoid of lifespan-measure, with infinite, infinite supreme selves —
the infinity of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s time is immeasurable; knowledge of time is its purpose.
Of the <s>Vedas</s>, of the syllables, of the unmanifest spatial [dimension],
of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), of all <s>jīvas</s> (souls), of the liberated ones, of those endowed with subtle bodies,
of all the subtle and gross bodies, of insentient <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) —
of these dependent ones, subject to the control of the independent one,
the infinity of time is always immeasurable; knowledge of time is its purpose.
For the non-eternal, insentient ones with subtle and gross bodies,
knowledge of time is the purpose regarding the lifespan-measure of bodies.

children.text: evaṃ kālagatiṃ jānan kālabhītiṃ tariṣyati // PS_1,3.66 //
children.translated_text: Thus, one who knows the course of time will cross over the fear of time.
In one supreme time-cycle, the teacher of the world [creates] one cosmic egg,
endowed with ten coverings — the unborn one creates, protects, and destroys.
<s>Keśava</s> does not desire to create many cosmic eggs at once.

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ garuḍaṃ śeṣam idraṃ prāṇaṃ raviṃ surān // PS_1,3.68 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Garuḍa</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Prāṇa</s> (Vāyu), <s>Ravi</s> (the Sun), the gods —
each one <s>Hari</s> makes liberated in the supreme time-cycle, [being] unborn.
Nevertheless, [as] the controller of the infinite cosmic eggs, he has the form of the cosmic egg.
<s>Hari</s> — in the infinite hair-pores of <s>Hari</s>,
infinite [cosmic eggs] of such great forms dwell — thus says the <s>śruti</s> (scripture).
Of those infinite forms, through the conjunction of infinities of infinities,
below, above, and in the eight directions, combined infinitely,
<s>Hari</s>, of full body, [fills] the space unfilled by the infinities of forms,
undivided, of a body of auspicious qualities — bliss, strength, and the like.
Without distinction, omnipresent, of subtle, gross, and other forms,
of equal power, of equal knowledge, strength, and other auspicious good qualities,
devoid of anything equal or superior, with <s>Ramā</s> of infinite form,
together with her who is under his own control, <s>Hari</s>, true, bears all sentient and insentient [beings].
Different from <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), who is different from himself; different from the liberated and bound ones by their qualities of sentience;
different from the eternal insentient real [entities]; different from the soul-lords always —

children.text: vibhinno viśvato viṣṇuḥ deśato guṇato vibhuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> is universally different in place and in qualities, [being] all-pervading.
With infinite, infinite forms, he is undivided though appearing divided, [being] <s>Hari</s>.
Though full, the unborn one creates, protects, and destroys the sentient and insentient.

children.text: iti śrī paratattavanarṇaye prakāśasaṃhitāyāṃ prathamaparicchede tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, the determination of the supreme reality — in the first section, the third chapter.
<s>Śrī Haṃsa</s> said:

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ sarvajagadbījaṃ mitaṃ trātaṃ ca viṣṇunā /
children.translated_text: "The subtle seed of the entire world, measured, protected by <s>Viṣṇu</s> —
that which the wise call <s>pradhāna</s> (primary matter), <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest),
<s>Mahāmāyā</s> (great illusion), <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature), <s>Mohinī</s> (enchantress) —
the unmanifest, of three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), of three forms, endowed with three powers,
is known also as the seed of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>kāma</s> (desire), <s>karma</s> (action), and the like;
protected at dissolution, the one of infinite form creates it [again] at creation.
It is called the beginningless knot of <s>karma</s>, the bond, and the binder;
unborn, not under the control of any other, endowed with sixteen <s>kalās</s> (parts),
of the nature of intense suffering, [it is] declared to be the cause of obtaining various wombs.
Shaped like a coconut, consisting of three divisions,
with an opening at the top, divine, always shining like a jewel —
covered by <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Ramā</s>, like [the illumination within] a cavity covered [by a shell].

children.text: sṛṣṭau laye ramā tasya māninī ca nirantaram /
children.translated_text: In creation and dissolution, <s>Ramā</s> is its <s>Māninī</s> (presiding deity) continuously;
in creation itself, <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, together with their consorts, are the presiding deities.
Endowed with three portions called <s>rajas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, and <s>tamas</s>;
the <s>sattva</s> portion is white in color; the <s>rājasa</s> is red in color;
the <s>tamas</s> portion is blue in color — thus it is of three portions.
The <s>kalās</s> (faculties) of the knowledge-senses and action-senses are established in the <s>rajas</s> portion;
the five <s>kalās</s> called <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) belong to the <s>tamas</s> portion;
the <s>kalā</s> of the mind belongs to the <s>sattva</s> portion — it is the chief of all in <s>pradhāna</s>.
Mind (<s>manas</s>), intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), and consciousness (<s>citta</s>) — thus it is fourfold.
Desire, anger, great greed, intoxication, envy, and delusion;
hatred, ego, possessiveness, jealousy, malice, fear, and the like —
these are the faults of the mind; that which is devoid of them, the mind, is the instrument for knowledge.
The mind, fourfold, is always considered to belong to insentient <s>Prakṛti</s>;

children.text: tajjanyamapyanityaṃ syāttatra cittaṃ na doṣayuk // PS_1,4.13 //
children.translated_text: what is born of it is also non-eternal; therein, <s>citta</s> (consciousness-faculty) is not faulty.
The mind (<s>manas</s>) will generate desire for gold and many other objects;
the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) will always resolve toward desire for prohibited enjoyments;
<s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) is the destroyer of the goals of a person, along with the base [qualities];
it imagines rivalry, and hatred toward <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the gods, in every way.
<s>Citta</s> (consciousness) always makes a person oriented toward true spiritual practice;
true spiritual practice mixed with ego is indeed sinful.
That <s>citta</s> devoid of ego is the instrument of [true] knowledge.

children.text: racite bhārate varṣe yathā mānuṣasattanum // PS_1,4.17 //
children.translated_text: Having obtained, in the created <s>Bhārata</s>-land, a human body,
having dwelt in the abode of a teacher through many good births,
having performed self-appropriate good deeds, having obtained the service of a true teacher,
by those who are pleased, through the hearing of excellent scriptures and the like —
that [<s>citta</s>] grants knowledge of [proper] conduct, and is the means for devotion and conduct.
Through both of those, the essential knowledge and devotion will become manifest.

children.text: svārūpikaṃ mano nityaṃ tataḥ svārūpikī matiḥ // PS_1,4.20 //
children.translated_text: The essential mind is eternal; thence the essential intellect

children.text: vyaktā bhavati nityā sā bhaktiḥ svārūpikī tathā /
children.translated_text: becomes manifest — it is eternal; so too is essential devotion.
That very [devotion], in the form of bliss, abides eternally in the liberated ones.
The globes of the senses are called visible, collectively;
the senses [themselves] are supersensory, consisting of knowledge and action.
Hearing, skin, eye, tongue, and nose — these are the knowledge-faculties;
speech, hands, feet, anus, and reproductive organ — all these are the action-faculties.
Hearing grasps sound; sound is declared to be of two kinds:
sound that is of the nature of resonance, and sound that is of the nature of phonemes — the first of these
arises from ego and is the cause of the production of space;
the sound that is of the nature of resonance is declared to be the primary [sound].
The knowledge-senses, action-senses, mind, and <s>tanmātras</s> are subtle and beginningless;
they are eternal [in their essential form]; at dissolution and creation they are declared non-eternal.
But the sound that is of the nature of phonemes is eternal, omnipresent, all-pervading;

children.text: dravyamityeva sarveṣāṃ na guṇaḥ kasyacinmate // PS_1,4.27 //
children.translated_text: it is a substance — according to all [authorities], it is not a quality of anything.
The <s>Vedas</s> — from their words, phonemes, sounds, and accents —
are all beginningless and eternal, of excellent qualities, not made by any person.
For conveying the greatness of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and as valid means of true knowledge —
the <s>śāstras</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s> are entirely of human authorship.
They are composed truthfully by <s>Hari</s> and then by the divine sages;
they are eternal in their meaning, but non-eternal in the arrangement of their phonemes.
The <s>sāttvika</s> (goodness-mode) <s>Purāṇas</s> and the <s>smṛtis</s> (law-codes) such as those of <s>Manu</s> and others —

children.text: yathārtha eva tatroktaṃ grāhyaṃ śrīharitatparaiḥ // PS_1,4.31 //
children.translated_text: what is stated therein as truthful should be accepted by those devoted to <s>Śrī Hari</s>.

children.text: vārāhaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ pādmaṃ vāyuproktaṃ ca gāruḍam /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vārāha</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, <s>Pādma</s>, <s>Vāyuproktam</s>, and <s>Gāruḍa</s>,

children.text: śrīmadbhāgavataṃ caiva sātvikānīti hi śrutiḥ // PS_1,4.32 //
children.translated_text: and the glorious <s>Bhāgavata</s> — these are the <s>sāttvika</s> [Purāṇas], according to <s>śruti</s>.
The <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>, <s>Brahmavaivarta</s>, <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>,

children.text: bhaviṣyaṃ nārasiṃhaṃ ca rājasāni ṣaḍaiva hi // PS_1,4.33 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaviṣya</s>, and <s>Nārasiṃha</s> — these six are the <s>rājasa</s> (passion-mode) [Purāṇas].

children.text: mātsyaṃ kaurmyaṃ tathā laiṅgyaṃ śaivaṃ skāndaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>Mātsya</s>, <s>Kaurma</s>, <s>Laiṅga</s>, <s>Śaiva</s>, <s>Skānda</s>,

children.text: pāśupatasaṃjñikaṃ ceti tāmasāni vido viduḥ // PS_1,4.34 //
children.translated_text: and that called <s>Pāśupata</s> — the knowers know these as the <s>tāmasa</s> (darkness-mode) [Purāṇas].
All that is stated in the <s>sāttvika</s> [Purāṇas] should be accepted; or [resolved] through different interpretation;
in the followers of the <s>Veda</s>, when there is contradiction, a different meaning should be construed.
The other [Purāṇas] are contradictory, born of deception and confusion;
even all the <s>sāttvika</s> <s>Purāṇas</s> stated by <s>Vyāsa</s>
in some places, some <s>Purāṇas</s> produce mostly erroneous knowledge;
due to the influence of demonic possession, [passages] stated by others are infinite [in number].
They are indeed inaudible [to the spiritual hearing]; those are not valid authorities — enough!
Those stated by the three supreme white [teachers] are always, by the very command of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
supremely authoritative, through the avoidance of demonic possession, ignorance, and the like.
Deafness and the like are faults of the hearing-faculty; by those with faultless senses,
these are called sense-objects — they are to be heard thousands of times.
Those free from defects of language should be grasped together with the mind.
Therein, the Lord to be known is described as having infinite good qualities, who is beyond description,

children.text: gamyaṃ satyaṃ ca sukhacinmayaṃ viṣṇuṃ sanātanam // PS_1,4.41 //
children.translated_text: who is attainable, true, and composed of bliss and consciousness—<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the eternal.
Those who worship <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), the Supreme Lord of the Self, with devotion, become liberated; the wrong path described in false scriptures is to be rejected, being connected with intellect.
Thus, in the <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, the fourth chapter of the first section.
<s>Śrī Haṃsa</s> (the Divine Swan) spoke:
The five organs of knowledge and the five organs of action—
belonging to the domain of <s>rajas</s> (passion)—among these, the ear is distinguished as foremost.
Due to its being the instrument of hearing, worship, and devotion, it is superior in qualities;
the skin, [present in] the orb of the skin-covering, pervading the entire body, is established [as the next].
Leprosy, brittleness, blisters, and others are declared as defects of the skin;
beginning with the unmanifest, the touches that are devoid of defects, beginning with cold and heat—
those are declared as its objects—air, fire, water, and earth;
certain substances and qualities are within the range of the skin organ.
The skin and touch, the two, are established in <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature); the eternal ones are subtle, and the non-eternal ones are gross;

children.text: tajjanyau prākṛtau vāyusaṃśrayau naśvarau matau // PS_1,5.5 //
children.translated_text: those produced [from them], natural, depending on air, are considered perishable.
The objects of the sense organs are declared to be qualities only;

children.text: jñānātmakānāṃ te sarve dvividhāḥ parikīrtitāḥ // PS_1,5.6 //
children.translated_text: of those that are of the nature of knowledge, all are declared to be of two kinds.
Those favorable to the service of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and his devotees are considered auspicious;

children.text: aśubhāḥ pratikūlāśca punaste trividhā matāḥ // PS_1,5.7 //
children.translated_text: the inauspicious are those that are contrary; and again, they are considered to be of three kinds.
Those who are fit for liberation, who are eternal; those in eternal transmigration are middling;
those who are fit for darkness are the lowest—each attaining [their state] through means appropriate to their fitness.
They lead to the lowest, middle, and highest stations, in due order;
the mind and the sense organs, which are mere [instruments], are part of the essential nature of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul).
Their essential natures are eternal; in the highest [souls], they are also auspicious;
the highest are fit for liberation, while those eternally bound are middling.
The lowest are fit for darkness; the mind and other [faculties] likewise—
those that are of one's own essential nature and situated in the subtle body are eternal; those in the gross body are non-eternal.
For <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), <s>Brahmā</s>, and others—for the liberated, in due order—
the mind, sense organs, knowledge, bliss, steadfastness, strength, and others—
are <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s own essential attributes, eternally pervading all;
they are independent, belonging to the independent, great-souled <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person).
He whose knowledge and action are clearly established in his own essential nature,

children.text: sarvasvarūpaceṣṭāsu parāpekṣā na yasya hi // PS_1,5.14 //
children.translated_text: who has no dependence on another in any of his essential activities—

children.text: sa svantantra iti proktaḥ sa viṣṇurnetaraḥ kvacit /
children.translated_text: he is declared to be independent; he is <s>Viṣṇu</s> and no other, anywhere.
Even <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), who is devoid of a body made of <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest matter) and its effects,
whose consciousness, sense organs, and mere [faculties] are eternal, pervading, and of her own essential nature—
she is under the sole control of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; her dependence on <s>Hari</s> always exists.
Because she is endowed with dependence on another, she is declared to be not independent;
the non-independence of <s>Brahmā</s> and other liberated and unliberated beings is beginningless.

children.text: siddhameva svarūpe ca jñāne karmaṇyapi sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: This is established regarding their essential nature, knowledge, and action, clearly—
the essential natures of the lowest among the low, and the minds of the highest among the highest—
their activity arises from [the Lord's] grace, as does all knowledge and devotion;
knowledge, ignorance, darkness, and liberation; of the eternal, non-eternal, and insentient—
there is neither origination nor destruction of the three kinds of <s>jīvas</s> (souls) in their entirety.
Suffering, hatred, jealousy, worry, and anguish pertaining to one's own essential nature—
these do not exist for the liberated; for as long as they have bodily connection, there is no fear or the like for them;

children.text: bhayādīni ca yogyebhyaḥ uttameṣvalpameva ca // PS_1,5.21 //
children.translated_text: fear and such exist for the fit [for liberation], but only slightly in the highest.

children.text: jñānaṃ muktirayogyasya na ca svapnepi dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Knowledge [of the nature leading to] liberation is not seen even in a dream for the unfit;
the darkness of ignorance regarding one's own essential nature never [exists] for the fit.

children.text: sṛṣṭiṃ sthitiṃ saṃhṛtiṃ ca niyatiṃ jagatosya tu /
children.translated_text: Creation, maintenance, dissolution, and the regulation of this world,

children.text: jñānājñāne tamomokṣau viṣṇunaiva vido viduḥ // PS_1,5.23 //
children.translated_text: knowledge and ignorance, darkness and liberation—the wise know [these are done] by <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone.
The essential nature of <s>Brahmā</s> and others is considered exceedingly minute;

children.text: tadindriyāṇi sūkṣmāṇi sūkṣmāṇyeva sthirāṇi tu // PS_1,5.24 //
children.translated_text: their sense organs are subtle, indeed subtle and stable.
The eye, situated in the eyeball, is the supreme organ for grasping form;
it is eternal and located in the unmanifest; the gross eye is non-eternal and produced.
Connected with the essential eye, both the eternal and non-eternal eyes
are givers of knowledge, called the witness—the essential sense organ of all.
Of the sense organs mentioned and those to be mentioned, in their entirety,
without the assistance of the essential sense organ, there is no power.

children.text: vṛddhiṃ hāniṃ ca labhate guṇairdeṣaiḥ svarūpataḥ /
children.translated_text: It gains increase and diminution through virtues and faults, by its essential nature;
the witness-organ of the fit [souls], except for hostility toward their own superiors—
even therein, due to some [obstruction], all that may become impeded.

children.text: paṭalaṃ kāmilā kācaḥ pratidīdhiti saṅgatiḥ // PS_1,5.29 //
children.translated_text: A film, jaundice, cataract, counter-reflection, and conjunction—
these and wounds etc. are the diseases of the eye; those caused by bile and similar;
wandering of the eye, cold, and the like are declared as defects of the eye.
Being too near, being too far, subtlety, and obstruction,
stability, and equal impact—these are declared as defects of the objects.
Those that are objects of description and within the range of descriptive sight—
white, red, bright, yellow, green, and all others—
multicolored and other forms are the objects of the eye;
those connected with manifest form, consisting of fire, water, and earth—
are declared as the objects of the eye; some [say] the sun, the gods [are also objects]. The tongue, situated in its orb, is declared to be the supreme organ of taste.
Supersensory [tastes like] sweetness and others; its defects are eruptions and the like;
astringent, pungent, bitter, salty, sweet, and sour—
and also mixed taste—these are the objects of the organ of taste;

children.text: doṣahīnasya ca rasajñānaṃ janayati sphuṭam // PS_1,5.36 //
children.translated_text: for one whose [organ] is free from defects, it produces clear knowledge of taste.
It quickly produces natural knowledge, established in <s>prakṛti</s> (nature);

children.text: duṣṭā paryuṣitā yāmahīnā pūtiyutā rasāḥ // PS_1,5.37 //
children.translated_text: spoiled, stale, diminished by time, and mixed with putrid [substances]—

children.text: sadoṣā rasasambandhe rasanā jñānadā na hi /
children.translated_text: when connected with such defective tastes, the tongue does not give knowledge.
Substances consisting of earth are the objects of the organ of taste.
The nose, situated in its orb, is declared to be the powerful sense organ;
nasal congestion and the like are defects of the nose; it is considered the organ for grasping smell.
Mixed and other classes of defects are declared as defects of smell.
The [organ of] speech, situated in the orb of the mouth, is declared to be the supersensory organ of speech.
Its words are eternal and non-eternal, true and false,
proper and improper, in the divine and common languages—
free from great defects such as muteness, these are within the range of speech;
stammering, indistinctness, and the like are declared as defects of speech.
The hand, situated in its orb, is declared to be the supersensory organ of the hand;
deformity and the like are its defects; it is an organ beyond description.
It grasps what is beneficial for oneself, both in this world and the next, always;
earth, jewels, gold, and other manifold objects are considered the objects [of the hands].
Stones and likewise non-entities are also considered objects of the hands;
thorns, leftovers, rocks, scorpions, and the like give what is undesirable—

children.text: heyā arthāśca hastābhyāṃ parityājyāḥ sadā matāḥ /
children.translated_text: undesirable objects are to be rejected by the hands, always, it is considered;
what is beneficial along with the undesirable, what is helpful—that is considered the beneficial [object] of the hands.
The foot, situated in its orb, is declared by the wise to be the capable organ of the foot;
lameness and the like are defects of the foot; it is the instrument for movement beyond description.
Belonging to one's own essential nature, belonging to <s>prakṛti</s>, and material—it is considered threefold;
whatever action is performed by whatever organ, always by the virtuous—
that is declared to be its object, within the range of that organ by name.

children.text: pakvāpakvaṃ ca bhuktaṃ ca vātaṃ jīrṇaṃ ca kukṣigam // PS_1,5.49 //
children.translated_text: Cooked and uncooked, eaten, flatulence, digested, and what enters the belly—
what in time becomes contrary is called excrement by the wise;
the object called discharge of such substance is declared to be the domain of the organ of excretion.
Fistula and other [diseases], wounds and the like situated in the excretory organ—

children.text: doṣāḥ nirodhātisārāḥ pāyorna yadi kāryakṛt // PS_1,5.51 //
children.translated_text: these are its defects; constipation and diarrhea—when the excretory organ does not function properly.
In women and men, the genitals and phallus, situated in their orbs, are supersensory;
the two organs called <s>upastha</s> and <s>śiśna</s>, when free from defects—
are capable of sexual pleasure and emission; they are considered to depend on blood and semen;
urinary diseases, wounds, and the like are their defects; the indescribable organ accomplishes its own purpose.
Natural, material, and connected with the essential sense organ—

children.text: arthakriyākāri taddhi nānyathā bhavati dhruvam // PS_1,5.54 //
children.translated_text: it is indeed productive of action; it cannot be otherwise, certainly.
The five organs of knowledge and the five organs of action—
belonging to the division of <s>rajas</s> (passion), possessing distinct powers—
the objects of the organs of knowledge are, in order, considered to be sound and the rest;
sound, touch, form, taste, and smell—these are considered qualities.
The subtle elements (<s>mātrā</s>), darkness, and their divisions are considered to be within the five great elements;
the wise declare that the elements are dissolved within the subtle elements in their seed-forms.
The fivefold [group], consisting of real ignorance, containing the seed of qualities,
is established as the fivefold [set] of [mental] states, within the subtle elements where the elements are dissolved.
<s>Tamas</s> (darkness), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), <s>tāmiśra</s> (gloom), and <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness)—

children.text: tamaḥ śabdagataṃ prāhuḥ mohaḥ sparśagato mataḥ // PS_1,5.59 //
children.translated_text: <s>tamas</s> is declared to relate to sound; <s>moha</s> is considered to relate to touch;
<s>mahāmoha</s> relates to form; <s>tāmiśra</s> is considered to relate to taste;
<s>andhatāmisra</s> relates to smell—these are of the nature of real states.
These, situated in <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), are eternal and exceedingly subtle;
the gross, manifest elements are considered non-eternal.
The essential nature of the <s>jīva</s> (soul) is not those; distinct from them, situated in the subtle body,
it is declared to be the concealer of the <s>jīva</s>'s essential knowledge.
Through its operation, it obstructs the essential knowledge that manifests;
<s>tamas</s> (darkness) causes the opposite of essential knowledge to function.
<s>Moha</s> (delusion) is that which, even with instruction, does not turn away; <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion) is that which cannot be reversed;
<s>tāmiśra</s> (gloom) is declared to be the cause of hatred toward instructors;
through false reasoning and inaccessible [pseudo-]scriptures, it is the sole means of deep ignorance—
the beginningless ignorance called <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness) is declared.
From beginningless time, infinitely and infinitely minute—
of essential natures as small as a ten-thousandth of a hair-tip—and within the range of the self—
protected by <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) in the form of a reflection, having the shape of each one's essential nature,

children.text: rakṣitāḥ pralaye sṛṣṭā nityaṃ tadanapāyinā // PS_1,5.67 //
children.translated_text: they are sustained during dissolution, created [again], and are eternally inseparable from Him.
Of those who come into being at the beginning of each <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age),
to be created in their respective <s>kalpas</s> in due order—dissimilar yet equal, unequal and of three kinds—
all <s>jīvas</s> (souls), from beginningless time, are not independent, subject to <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī);
bound by the subtle body consisting of <s>prakṛti</s>, they are within the womb of <s>Śrī Hari</s>.
At dissolution and creation, <s>Hari</s> creates them—from the cosmic egg, both outside and inside;
the <s>sāttvika</s> (virtuous), the low, and the middling [are created] within; the non-<s>tāttvika</s> (those not in accordance with truth) [are also created].
The partless—mortals, <s>gandharvas</s>, and those prior [to them]—all down to the grass;

children.text: yogyā nityasṛtisthāśca tamo yogyāśca kṛtsnaśaḥ // PS_1,5.71 //
children.translated_text: the fit, those in eternal transmigration, and those fit for darkness—all without exception.

children.text: sarvepi liṅgasambaddhā ye te jīvā na cānyathā /
children.translated_text: All those <s>jīvas</s> that are connected with the subtle body, and no otherwise—
they too, in the infinitely past <s>kalpas</s>, by means appropriate to themselves—
the liberated, the middling who attained darkness, exist within the womb of <s>Śrī Hari</s>;
there is no complete fulfillment for them anywhere, at any time, by the rule of <s>Hari</s>.
Thus, in the glorious <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, in the first section, the fifth chapter.
The glorious <s>Haṃsa</s> said:
When the night-measure had completely elapsed and the first day had arrived, at that moment the Lord of all (<s>Akhilasvayaṃprabhu</s>) formed the desire to create the universe.

Then the Lord (<s>Vineśvara</s>), [taking] the souls dwelling in his own womb — those released from the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) — covered them threefold with bodies made of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature).
The Lord, separating the <s>tāmasic</s> (dark), pure <s>rājasic</s> (passionate), and <s>sāttvic</s> (pure) [souls] dwelling in his belly, lifting them out, the one called <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person),
gave forth — he called <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Lord of the universe, gave all the souls.
There is no creation of the liberated ones; nor of the bound ones in every respect.

children.text: naiva sṛṣṭistu muktānāṃ baddhānāṃ na hi sarvaśaḥ // PS_1,6.4 //
children.translated_text: Creation is properly said [to occur] because of the fixed number; creation is said [to be] by fixed enumeration, both among the real (<s>tāttvika</s>) and the non-real (<s>atāttvika</s>).

children.text: sṛṣṭiḥ saṃkhyā niyamataḥ tātvikātātvikeṣu ca // PS_1,6.5 //
children.translated_text: Among the partless (<s>niraṃśa</s>), there is no enumeration; because of their multiplicity, it is manifold. Those fit for the status of <s>Brahmā</s>, the upright (<s>ṛju</s>) ones, are groups infinite in number.
Among them, those liberated by infinitely prior <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) are infinite; those bound by the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) too are infinite — infinite are those dwelling in the womb.
Of <s>Hari</s>, among all those — some among them are to be created. The upright and other real (<s>tāttvika</s>) ones — all have direct perception (<s>aparokṣa</s>) from beginningless time.

In general and in particular, each having direct perception according to their own respective fitness, they come to have it through the great practice (<s>sādhana</s>) appropriate to the appointed time.
The upright (<s>ṛju</s>) ones, limited to a hundred [kalpas], strive for direct perception; and those who already possess direct perception are always measured by the number of a hundred.
Always striving in the worship of the qualities of <s>Hari</s> proclaimed in infinite <s>Vedas</s>, they too gradually accumulate the worshipped qualities.
Those <s>Brahmās</s> who possess the full worship of perfect good qualities — at the [appointed] time, one becomes liberated indeed; one is not liberated all at once.

children.text: kāle mukto bhavatyeva mucyate naikadaiva hi // PS_1,6.12 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by <s>Brahmā</s>'s measure, through twenty <s>kalpas</s>, one of full power and full worship of qualities becomes fully liberated.
At the moment prior to liberation, even when the enjoyable <s>prārabdha</s> (commenced karma) is exhausted — likewise in the higher [realms] too, O gods, by fixed enumeration
the real (<s>tāttvika</s>) ones are liberated through the <s>kalpas</s> that will be stated — of the unborn (<s>Aja</s>, i.e., <s>Brahmā</s>) indeed:
Those beginning with <s>Śeṣa</s>, together with their consorts, are measured by fifty-two <s>kalpas</s>.

The <s>Indra</s>-souls are measured by twenty <s>kalpas</s>; the ordinary born (<s>dvijanma</s>) by two times nine <s>kalpas</s>. The one worthy of the position of <s>Ahaṃprāṇa</s> (ego-breath), and those beginning with the guru — by twice eight <s>kalpas</s>.
<s>Pravāha</s> by twice six <s>kalpas</s>; those beginning with <s>Sūrya</s> by ten <s>kalpas</s>; for those beginning with <s>Mitra</s> by nine; and for the remaining group,

children.text: mitrādīnāṃ ca navabhistūkta śeṣagaṇasya tu // PS_1,6.17 //
children.translated_text: by eight; for the group of <s>Sanaka</s> and others by seven <s>kalpas</s>; beginning from <s>Parjanya</s> up to the group ending with <s>Puṣkara</s>, by six.

children.text: aṣṭabhiḥ saptabhiḥ kalpaiḥ sanakādi gaṇasya tu /

children.translated_text: From direct perception onward, the <s>karmadevās</s> (gods by action) attain direct perception in five <s>kalpas</s>; by four for the naturally-born (<s>ājānaja</s>); and by three and a half <s>kalpas</s>
for the <s>gopīs</s> associated with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s limbs; by three for the group of ancestors (<s>pitṛs</s>); for the <s>Gandharvas</s> by two <s>kalpas</s>; and for mortals by one.

children.text: gandharvāṇāntu kalpābhyāṃ martyānāṃ tu tathaikataḥ // PS_1,6.20 //
children.translated_text: Half a <s>kalpa</s> for those ending with grass (<s>tṛṇa</s>) who are fit for the vision of <s>Hari</s>. This rule applies in all <s>kalpas</s> in just this way, and not otherwise.

The <s>kalpa</s>-enumeration should be known by the wise from <s>Brahmā</s>'s measure. The attainment of darkness (<s>tamas</s>) for the <s>asuras</s> (demons) is by the day-<s>kalpa</s> of <s>Brahmā</s>.
It is ever thus by the command of the Creator of the universe. For those from <s>Indra</s> up to <s>Puṣkara</s>, by the <s>kalpas</s> appropriate to the worship of qualities
as stated, they are liberated; and the practice (<s>sādhana</s>) must be done for that many <s>kalpas</s>. Prior to that, direct perception must be attained — this is the certainty.
Within the cosmic egg (<s>aṇḍa</s>), as long as <s>Brahmā</s> born from the lotus endures, for that long — in each day within the cycle of years —

all those with parts (<s>sāṃśa</s>), the non-real (<s>atāttvika</s>), measured by the number to be stated, in each <s>kalpa</s> too, are those with direct perception who are established in their positions.
The <s>Apsarases</s> beginning with <s>Urvaśī</s>, measured by the number eight up to a hundred, are equal to the naturally-born; the others are equal to the <s>karmadevās</s>.

children.text: mitā ājānajaistulyāḥ karmadevaiḥ samāḥ parāḥ // PS_1,6.27 //
children.translated_text: Among the ancestors, there are a hundred — seven of them are equal to <s>Urvaśī</s> and the rest; the others are less than the naturally-born, and inferior to them in order.

The <s>Gandharvas</s> are a hundred; among them, eight are equal to the action-born (<s>karmaja</s>). All the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages), measured by a hundred <s>koṭis</s> (ten million) — twenty are the highest.

children.text: gandharvāstu śataṃ teṣu aṣṭau tulyāstu karmajaiḥ /

children.translated_text: Among the <s>ṛṣis</s>, a hundred are declared equal to the <s>karmadevās</s>. And among them, those possessed by <s>Hari</s> (<s>haryāveśa</s>) — twenty are slightly superior in qualities.
Among those very ones, eight are real (<s>tāttvika</s>); a hundred are equal to the action-born. The others are equal to the naturally-born; and so too the sons of <s>Agni</s>.
Sixteen thousand, one hundred and thirty are of the <s>Cāraṇas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>; the <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, and others — seventy in all classes.

The naturally-born among them, with an amount less than that, combined with ancestors and <s>Gandharvas</s> — those with parts (<s>sāṃśa</s>) depend on images (<s>pratīka</s>); and the partless are inferior to them.
Among those who depend on images, the foremost are the human singers (<s>mānuṣagāyaka</s>); less than them are kings; and lower than the highest mortals are the lowest.

children.text: tato nyūnāstu rājāno martyoccāstu tato 'dhamāḥ // PS_1,6.34 //
children.translated_text: Among all groups of souls — mortal <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and others — those who are fit for liberation all depend on images (<s>pratīka</s>).
The partless (<s>niraṃśa</s>) ones, prior to direct perception and even afterwards, remain within the cosmic egg indeed. Those to be created — as above, those with parts, lacking direct perception —
for the direct-perceivers among those with parts, and for those of different minds from the real ones — for the non-real <s>karmadevās</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and humans —

to this extent, the subtle attainment of all souls [comes] from <s>Aniruddha</s>; prior to the birth of the unborn (<s>Aja</s>), within the cosmic egg — [their] gross attainment: this is the certainty.
For the real (<s>tāttvika</s>) ones, the subtle and gross attainment is from outside the cosmic egg. They have unmixed bodies — those gods [exist] prior to the production of the egg.
Within the cosmic egg, all are mixed, having gross bodies. During dissolution, all those bound by the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) dwell in the empty womb.

children.text: laye sarve liṅgabaddhāḥ śūnyakukṣā vasanti hi // PS_1,6.40 //
children.translated_text: Among them, those other than the liberated, by fixed enumeration, are agreed to be created; and all of those — <s>Vāsudeva</s> undertook to create them.

<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), called the insentient (<s>jaḍa</s>), is the <s>liṅga</s>-form of all souls. The souls dwelling in the womb of <s>Prakṛti</s> are understood to be endowed with <s>liṅga</s>-bodies.
From beginningless time, souls are subject to the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). Therein, in the infinitely prior <s>kalpa</s>, souls — through correct practice (<s>satsādhana</s>),

children.text: tatra pūrvānantakalpe jīvāḥ satsādhanena ca // PS_1,6.43 //
children.translated_text: through mixed practice, and through contrary knowledge — having unrelinquished bondage, the souls were of three kinds, in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of thousands.
Among those to be created, who are bound by the <s>liṅga</s>, the four-faced one (<s>Brahmā</s>) is created first. But not all are created at one time — creation differs by temporal sequence.

children.text: na caikakāle sarveṣāṃ sṛṣṭiḥ sā kālabhedataḥ // PS_1,6.45 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, those born first are superior; the others born later are inferior. When the time called dissolution (<s>laya</s>), the supreme time, has elapsed, at the beginning of the supreme time,

the creation of the unborn (<s>Aja</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>) [occurs]; the creation of others [occurs] over time. After the creation of <s>Brahmā</s>, the creation of <s>Vāyu</s> [occurs] after a hundred years.

children.text: brahmaṇaḥ sṛṣṭitaḥ paścādvāyoḥ sṛṣṭiḥ śatābdataḥ // PS_1,6.47 //
children.translated_text: Then after a hundred years, [the creation] of <s>Vāṇī</s> (Speech/<s>Sarasvatī</s>); of <s>Bhāratī</s> after another hundred years; then after a thousand years, the creation of the two <s>Vipaś</s> (forms).
Of <s>Nīlā</s> and others after a thousand years; after the same period again, of <s>Vāruṇī</s> and others after ten thousand years; then after that,
the creation of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Kāma</s>; after ten thousand years, the others too were created by <s>Hari</s>; and those who are lower — by the highest of the highest:
those ending with <s>Puṣkara</s>, who are real (<s>tāttvika</s>); and likewise the non-real others; the partless, the eternally bound, the <s>tamas</s>-destined, and the <s>Rākṣasas</s>.
From ten thousand years by divine measure, according to the arrangement of each preceding one, creation occurs — that is understood to be of two kinds, by the distinction of subtle and gross.
For all the real (<s>tāttvika</s>) ones who are established in their positions and possess direct perception, [creation occurs] from outside the egg itself; for the others, within it.
For beings born outside and within the egg, creation should be known in due order according to the time-regulation previously stated.
When the subtle body attainment of one bound by the <s>liṅga</s> is to occur, at the moment prior to that, a disequilibrium of qualities in the <s>liṅga</s> is posited.

The <s>rajas</s> (passion) portion, situated in the middle of the <s>liṅga</s>-body, is proclaimed. The one called <s>Bhū</s> (<s>Indirā</s>/<s>Lakṣmī</s>) is the instigator therein; its presiding deity is <s>Māninī</s>.

children.text: bhūrnāmakendirā tatra ceṣṭakā tasya māninī // PS_1,6.56 //
children.translated_text: The <s>rajas</s> touched by the <s>sattva</s> portion — the <s>rājasic</s> atoms are on the side. During the ten-fold dissolution, the atoms on the side of the <s>sattva</s> of <s>Bhūmi</s> (Earth)

children.text: daśapralayakāle tu bhūmyā satvasya pārśvagāḥ // PS_1,6.57 //
children.translated_text: come to be; at the end of the dissolution period, they remain there in every way. A <s>rājasic</s> atom, gone to the <s>sāttvic</s> portion, individually and separately —
ten such [atoms] — these, combined, are twelve atoms. Among the <s>sāttvic</s> ones, it makes a hundred measured ones of red color.
By nature, the <s>sattva</s> portions are white; those established in <s>sattva</s> — the red ones, numbering a thousand, by ten <s>rājasic</s> atoms,
come to be; and those touched by <s>rajas</s>, situated on the side of <s>sattva</s> during dissolution — thus one <s>rājasic</s> atom [takes] the <s>rājasic</s> portion on the left side,

children.text: bhavanti ca rajaḥ spṛṣṭāḥ satvapārśvagatā laye /

children.translated_text: having brought the <s>tāmasic</s> portion from <s>Bhū</s> (earth), makes its hundredth part <s>tāmasic</s> — very minute, blue-colored — making them more and more red.

children.text: atyalpaṃ nīlavarṇaṃ te raktoraktī karotyalam // PS_1,6.62 //
children.translated_text: One pure <s>rājasic</s> portion, in the <s>rājasic</s> section, remains in the middle even during dissolution; these are equal to <s>rājasic</s> atoms.

children.text: ekaḥ śuddho rājasāṃśaḥ paricchede tu rājase /
madhye tiṣṭhantyapi laye rājasāṇu samā ime // PS_1,6.63 //
children.translated_text: Those situated in the <s>tamas</s> section — the <s>tāmasic</s> atoms of such a kind — during dissolution, the <s>rājasic</s> atoms on the side of the <s>sattva</s> section,
the <s>tāmasic</s> ones of such a kind — these twelve combined atoms; the <s>rājasic</s>-<s>tāmasic</s> are very minute, by the measure of a <s>paramāṇu</s> (ultimate atom).
When multiplied there, they amount to twelve hundred; ten <s>rājasic</s> combined with a thousand <s>sāttvic</s> atoms,
they become a <s>lakṣa</s> (hundred thousand); these are the ones useful for effects. From the <s>tāmasic</s> section, the <s>rājasic</s> is remembered as double.
From the <s>rājasic</s> section, the <s>sāttvic</s> is remembered as double. In each section, infinite are the <s>paramāṇus</s> (ultimate atoms).
There exist the controllers — the unborn (<s>Aja</s>), of the nature of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-<s>Brahmā</s>-<s>Śiva</s>. <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, of infinite qualities; <s>Śrī</s>, the feminine presiding deity —
in the insentient <s>Prakṛti</s> also, and in the <s>liṅga</s>-body likewise, there are infinite atoms — those previously described — which accomplish effects.

children.text: jaḍāyāṃ prakṛtau cāpi liṅgadehe tathaiva ca /

children.translated_text: The <s>rājasic</s> portions gone to <s>sattva</s>, during dissolution, they call them <s>rājasa-sāttvika</s>; the <s>rajas</s> gone to <s>tamas</s>, they call <s>rājasa-tāmasa</s>.
The <s>rajas</s> situated in the <s>rajas</s> section — the noble ones call it <s>rājasa-tāmasa</s> even during dissolution; the union occurs by the will of <s>Śrī Hari</s>.

children.text: vadantyeva laye yogo bhavati śrīharīcchayā // PS_1,6.72 //
children.translated_text: The wise call this the state of equilibrium (<s>sāmyāvasthā</s>) of <s>Prakṛti</s> and the <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: sāmyāvasthāṃ budhāḥ prāhuḥ etāṃ prakṛtiliṅgayoḥ // PS_1,6.73 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, in the first section, the sixth chapter.
The glorious <s>Haṃsa</s> said:
The <s>liṅga</s>-body (subtle body) is shaped like a coconut, understood as threefold; having an opening at the crown, always endowed with interior space like a womb.
The souls bound within it are of three kinds; yet in liberation they are unable [to escape on their own]; nor can <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) — they dwell in the opening at the crown.
Those bound by the <s>liṅga</s> are touched by suffering; only <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) is untouched by suffering.
