Those bound by the <s>liṅga</s> are touched by suffering; only <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) is untouched by suffering.

children.text: yasmannakāle yasya sūkṣmaḥ nāśo bhavati viṣṇunā // PS_1,7.3 //
children.translated_text: since the subtle destruction of a particular [being] does not occur at the [appointed] time by <s>Viṣṇu</s> — (PS 1.7.3)
by <s>Aniruddha</s>, that lowly one [is expelled] gradually from within the cosmic egg to outside;
at the very next moment, in the subtle body, there occurs an equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities). (PS 1.7.4)
That [equilibrium], having the form of the earth, which has the nature of essential knowledge, obstructs the knowledge of the souls;
the efforts and desires for the bliss of essential knowledge [that belong to] the virtuous during dissolution (PS 1.7.5)

children.text: ruddhā bhavanti sāmye tu vaiṣamye vyaktimañjasā /
children.translated_text: become obstructed in [the state of] equilibrium; in [the state of] disequilibrium, they readily attain manifestation;

children.text: yāntyavasthādvayaṃ liṅge laye sṛṣṭau kramātkila // PS_1,7.6 //
children.translated_text: the two states in the subtle body — during dissolution and creation — occur in sequence. (PS 1.7.6)

children.text: kṣaṇakṣaṇena bhramatāṃ sa tāṃ savyena cānyathā /
children.translated_text: Moment by moment, for those who revolve [in the cycle], in one direction and otherwise,
for those revolving, from the proper combination of the three <s>guṇas</s> residing in the subtle body — (PS 1.7.7)
at the time of creation, the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) of souls is acknowledged to be threefold:

children.text: sātvikī rājasī ceti tāmasīti samastaśaḥ // PS_1,7.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>sāttvikī</s> (of <s>sattva</s>), <s>rājasī</s> (of <s>rajas</s>), and <s>tāmasī</s> (of <s>tamas</s>), altogether. (PS 1.7.8)
For the fit ones, <s>sāttvika</s> intellect is abundant; for the others, it is held to be slight;

children.text: madhyamānāntu jīvānāṃ rājasī tāmasī matiḥ // PS_1,7.9 //
children.translated_text: for the middling souls, the intellect is <s>rājasī</s> and <s>tāmasī</s>. (PS 1.7.9)
Gradually, the others become more abundant and will become very small in measure;
the fivefold ignorance pertaining to the five [elements], residing in the subtle body — (PS 1.7.10)
is declared to be beginningless ignorance, external and not of one's essential nature;
when the witness-sense-organs are conjoined with a mind [dominated by] <s>tamas</s>, then indeed it arises. (PS 1.7.11)
If the witness-sense-organs are conjoined with a mind established in <s>sattva</s>,
then external and essential knowledge [arises] for the three kinds of conscious beings here. (PS 1.7.12)
If the witness-sense-organs are conjoined with a mind [dominated by] <s>rajas</s>,

children.text: bāhyamasvārūpikaṃ ca kāmakrodhādikaṃ ca yat // PS_1,7.13 //
children.translated_text: then external and non-essential [qualities arise], as well as desire, anger, and the like. (PS 1.7.13)
Beginningless desire of the three kinds of souls will arise;
if the faculties of the sense-organs of knowledge are situated within the scope of <s>rajas</s>, (PS 1.7.14)
then the desire for external sounds and the like, endowed with witness-sense-organs, will arise;
that is declared to be beginningless desire, for the three kinds of conscious beings here. (PS 1.7.15)
If the faculties of the organs of action are situated within the scope of <s>rajas</s>,
then, endowed with witness-sense-organs, they generate <s>karma</s> (action), which is also beginningless. (PS 1.7.16)

children.text: bāhyaliṅgagataṃ karma na tu svārūpikaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: The <s>karma</s> residing in the external subtle body is not considered to be of one's essential nature;

children.text: anādyavidyākāmau cānādi karma ca liṅgagam // PS_1,7.17 //
children.translated_text: beginningless ignorance, desire, and beginningless <s>karma</s>, all residing in the subtle body — (PS 1.7.17)
thinking 'this is mine,' the conscious being becomes bound;

children.text: kālena bhārate varṣe labdhajanmāpi mānuṣam // PS_1,7.18 //
children.translated_text: in the course of time, having obtained birth in <s>Bhārata</s> (India) as a human, (PS 1.7.18)
having attained <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> birth, association with a true teacher, devotion (<s>bhakti</s>), and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>),
by the grace of <s>Śrī Hari</s>, [the soul passes through] <s>karma</s> among the intermediate deities, (PS 1.7.19)
outside the cosmic egg, for the <s>sāttvika</s> ones, in the region enclosed by <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, during dissolution,
touching the shell of the cosmic egg, in [the realm of] <s>Śrī</s>, or by <s>Hari</s>'s will, (PS 1.7.20)
stationed in the surrounding region of the final state, or having plunged into the water,
for the virtuous ones whose essential natures are manifest, when the reversal of the subtle body [occurs] — (PS 1.7.21)
due to hatred of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Ramā</s>, and the <s>suras</s> (gods) in mortal birth in <s>Bhārata</s>,
when, due to the increase of bad association, the destruction of the subtle body within the cosmic egg [occurs], (PS 1.7.22)
for the unvirtuous, by the mace-blow of <s>Vāyu</s>, in the course of time,
beginningless ignorance, desire, and beginningless <s>karma</s> are also destroyed. (PS 1.7.23)

children.text: ato bāhyaṃ na svarūpā avidyādyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, ignorance and the rest are declared to be external, not of one's essential nature;

children.text: jñānājñāne svarūpasthe nitye naiva ca naśvare // PS_1,7.24 //
children.translated_text: knowledge and ignorance abide in one's essential nature, eternally, and are never perishable. (PS 1.7.24)

children.text: tadā jīvasya sarvasya na bhavanti kadācana // PS_1,7.25 //
children.translated_text: then they never exist for any soul whatsoever. (PS 1.7.25)
When beginningless ignorance, desire, and the rest attain the state of equilibrium,
The <s>tāmasic</s> atoms are [each] of the brilliance of a hundredth part of a <s>rājasic</s> [atom]; twelve <s>tāmasic</s> atoms [constitute one unit];
during dissolution, among them, one <s>rājasic</s> [atom] and ten situated on the side of <s>sattva</s> (PS 1.7.26)
exist; one <s>tāmasic</s> [atom] is situated in the middle, certainly;
from the <s>rājasic</s> atom, the <s>tāmasic</s> one, from the <s>sāttvic</s> one, becomes double in <s>rajas</s>. (PS 1.7.27)
The <s>tāmasic</s> atoms [each] of the brilliance of a hundredth part of a <s>rājasic</s> [atom], situated in <s>sattva</s>,
even the ten, superior by tenfold — during dissolution, certainly, (PS 1.7.28)
they darken [them]; thus this is declared to be the state of equilibrium (<s>sāmyāvasthā</s>);

children.text: tāmasī rājasī ceti sāmyāvasthā dvidhā matā // PS_1,7.29 //
children.translated_text: the state of equilibrium is considered twofold: <s>tāmasic</s> and <s>rājasic</s>. (PS 1.7.29)

children.text: sāmyāvasthā sātvike tu na kvāpi kila vidyate /
children.translated_text: The state of equilibrium never exists in <s>sattva</s>;

children.text: dvābhyāntu sāmyavasthābhyāṃ liṅgastābhyāṃ janasya tu // PS_1,7.30 //
children.translated_text: from the two states of equilibrium, the subtle body [arises] from them, for the beings. (PS 1.7.30)

children.text: laye sarvasya tāṃ nidrāṃ nāśaṃ prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: During dissolution, for all, the sages call that sleep 'destruction';

children.text: yadā yogecchoparamaḥ tadā jñāpayati prabhuḥ // PS_1,7.31 //
children.translated_text: when the cessation of the Lord's desire [for creation occurs], then the Lord makes it known. (PS 1.7.31)
The unfit one's desire, effort, and the like — [the Lord] cuts off the doer's expectation;

children.text: vaiṣamye sati liṅge tu jananecchā hi jāyate // PS_1,7.32 //
children.translated_text: when disequilibrium exists in the subtle body, the desire for birth indeed arises. (PS 1.7.32)

children.text: yadecchā jāyate jantostadā sṛjati taṃ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: When desire arises in a being, then the Lord creates it;
of all the souls to be created, outside the cosmic egg and within it — (PS 1.7.33)
the state of disequilibrium does not occur all at once for <s>Aja</s> (the unborn, <s>Brahmā</s>) and the rest, but gradually;
in reverse order, by the former measure, both within and outside the cosmic egg — (PS 1.7.34)
the state of equilibrium of the lowly ones [occurs] first, and that of the supreme [occurs] afterward;

children.text: laye satvapraviṣṭā ye daśate rājasāṇavaḥ // PS_1,7.35 //
children.translated_text: during dissolution, those ten <s>rājasic</s> atoms that have entered <s>sattva</s> — (PS 1.7.35)
endowed with more than a hundred <s>sāttvic</s> atoms in the region of <s>sattva</s>,

children.text: sṛṣṭikāle śriyānunnā rajo bhāgaṃ viśanti hi // PS_1,7.36 //
children.translated_text: at the time of creation, impelled by <s>Śrī</s>, they enter the <s>rajas</s> portion. (PS 1.7.36)
The <s>rājasic</s> atom that during dissolution is situated within the domain of <s>tamas</s>,
having taken with it a <s>tāmasic</s> atom of its own hundredth part, impelled by <s>Durgā</s> — (PS 1.7.37)
they enter the <s>rajas</s> portion when the time of creation arrives;
during dissolution, the atom of <s>rajas</s> situated in the middle of the <s>rajas</s> portion — (PS 1.7.38)
it attains manifestation in the middle of <s>rajas</s> when the time of creation approaches;

children.text: prakṛtau liṅgadeho 'pi evaṃ yadi guṇasthitiḥ // PS_1,7.39 //
children.translated_text: in <s>Prakṛti</s>, even in the subtle body, if such is the state of the <s>guṇas</s> — (PS 1.7.39)
the wise call it the state of equilibrium; from it, creation will proceed;
during dissolution, those ten <s>tāmasic</s> atoms that have entered <s>sattva</s> — (PS 1.7.40)
[each] of the brilliance of a hundredth part of a <s>rājasic</s> atom — joined with their own equal <s>sāttvic</s> atoms,

children.text: yuktāstāmasa bhāgaṃ hi viśanti śrīsamīritāḥ // PS_1,7.41 //
children.translated_text: they enter the <s>tamas</s> portion indeed, impelled by <s>Śrī</s>. (PS 1.7.41)
The <s>tāmasic</s> atom that has entered <s>rajas</s>, balanced with the prior atom [of <s>sattva</s>],
joined with a <s>rājasic</s> atom double of itself and of <s>sattva</s> — (PS 1.7.42)

children.text: tatra sthitvā laye bhūyaḥ sṛṣṭikāla upāgate /
children.translated_text: having stayed there during dissolution, again when the time of creation approaches,
impelled by the Earth (<s>Bhū</s>), they enter the <s>tamas</s> portion by the will of <s>Śrī Hari</s>. (PS 1.7.43)
One pure <s>tāmasic</s> atom, along with the former <s>tāmasic</s> and <s>sāttvic</s> ones —
the ten, plus one <s>tāmasic</s> and likewise the <s>rājasic</s>-<s>tāmasic</s> one — (PS 1.7.44)
having all assembled, they attain what is called the disequilibrium of <s>tamas</s>;
from a thousand <s>sāttvic</s> atoms, with ten <s>rājasic</s> atoms, (PS 1.7.45)
with one pure <s>rājasic</s> [atom], the <s>tāmasic</s> [atom] joined with <s>rajas</s> —
the atom that becomes unified — this is called the disequilibrium of <s>rajas</s>. (PS 1.7.46)

children.text: rajo vaiṣamyataḥ sṛṣṭiḥ tamo vaiṣamyato layaḥ // PS_1,7.47 //
children.translated_text: From the disequilibrium of <s>rajas</s> comes creation; from the disequilibrium of <s>tamas</s> comes dissolution. (PS 1.7.47)
Thus, in the <s>Śrī Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, in the first section, the seventh chapter.
<s>Śrī Haṃsa</s> said:
When the time of dissolution has passed and the time of creation has arrived,
at the beginning of the supreme time (<s>parakāla</s>), the Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>), [taking] all conscious beings — (PS 1.8.1)
offered to <s>Vāsudeva</s> the various souls bound by subtle bodies, to be created,
endowed with hierarchy, their respective fitness having been assessed. (PS 1.8.2)
Facing the great effort appropriate to each, by their respective <s>karmas</s>,
having looked upon and contemplated those situated in <s>Vāsudeva</s>, fit for obtaining birth — (PS 1.8.3)
at the very first moment of the time of creation, for the unborn (<s>Aja</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>) whose subtle body is fitting,
bound by the subtle body, connected with the disequilibrium of the preceding moment — (PS 1.8.4)
the all-pervading <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, having taken one, gave the other souls [to the next];

children.text: sa vāyumekaṃ liṅge taṃ gṛhītvānyān sucetanān // PS_1,8.5 //
children.translated_text: he, having taken <s>Vāyu</s> alone in the subtle body, [gave] the other well-conscious ones — (PS 1.8.5)
<s>Pradyumna</s> gave [them]; the wives of those two — having taken [them] along with their subtle bodies,
and all the other <s>sāttvic</s> ones situated in all [the higher] stations, the <s>sāttvic</s>-natured ones — (PS 1.8.6)
those of manifest direct perception, by a fixed number, through subtle connection,
to be created, [<s>Pradyumna</s>] gave [them] at the end; the Lord of all, <s>Aniruddha</s> — (PS 1.8.7)
<s>Vāsudeva</s> set in motion the subtle body of <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>);
from the three <s>guṇas</s> residing in that subtle body, three drops (<s>bindus</s>) [fell] — (PS 1.8.8)

children.text: nyapatan tatra yobinduḥ sātvikaḥ sa tu nirmalaḥ / /

children.translated_text: the <s>rājasic</s> drop, conjoined with the disequilibrium of <s>rajas</s>, likewise fell. (PS 1.8.9)
they fell there; the drop that was <s>sāttvic</s> was pure;
Mixed with the disequilibrium of <s>tamas</s>, the <s>tāmasic</s> drop arose; then,
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, [entering] the <s>rājasic</s> drop, the strengthened disequilibrium of <s>rajas</s> — (PS 1.8.10)
separating it, the teacher of the universe made the <s>rājasic</s> drop pure;
the Lord, [entering] the <s>tāmasic</s> drop, the intense disequilibrium of <s>tamas</s> — (PS 1.8.11)
extracting it and setting it aside, he made that drop pure and expanded it;

children.text: tato māyā prārthitaḥ san vāsudevastadādimaḥ // PS_1,8.12 //
children.translated_text: then, being entreated by <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the primordial one — (PS 1.8.12)
the unborn, all-pervading one, bound by the disequilibrium of <s>rajas</s>-<s>guṇa</s> in the subtle body,
for <s>Aja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) to obtain a subtle body, the strengthened disequilibrium of <s>rajas</s> — (PS 1.8.13)
having deposited it and having swallowed [it], the Lord, into <s>Māyā</s>, [deposited] what is called <s>Mahat</s> (the Great);

children.text: sūkṣmarūpaṃ tu tadvīryaṃ prākṛtaṃ prākṣipaddhariḥ // PS_1,8.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> cast that seed (<s>vīrya</s>), subtle in form, of material (<s>prākṛta</s>) nature. (PS 1.8.14)
There she gave birth to the unborn, all-pervading one endowed with a subtle body;

children.text: guṇatrayāṇavaḥ pūrvaṃ sāṃkhyā niyamataḥ sthitāḥ // PS_1,8.15 //
children.translated_text: the atoms of the three <s>guṇas</s>, as before, stood in fixed number. (PS 1.8.15)

children.text: yāvantaste sadā nityāḥ teṣāṃ nāśo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: However many they are, they are always eternal; their destruction does not exist;

children.text: tatra satvāṇavaḥ sarve daśadhopacitāḥ sadā // PS_1,8.16 //
children.translated_text: among them, all the <s>sāttvic</s> atoms, always increased tenfold, (PS 1.8.16)
exist; the <s>rājasic</s> and <s>tāmasic</s> atoms are increased only by a quarter;
they exist, increased, residing subtly in <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, and the rest. (PS 1.8.17)
<s>Sattva</s> and the rest are increased tenfold; they indeed arise;
for [beings] from grass and the like, those residing in the subtle [body] arise in greater measure. (PS 1.8.18)
The <s>sāttvic</s> atoms, <s>rājasic</s> atoms, and also <s>tāmasic</s> atoms —

children.text: ṛjūnāṃ sūkṣmagāḥ pādopacitāḥ prabhavanti hi // PS_1,8.19 //
children.translated_text: for the righteous ones, they arise in the subtle [body] increased by a quarter. (PS 1.8.19)
Partial [atoms] in all the partial subtle bodies entirely —
the <s>sāttvic</s> atoms attain a tenfold increase for the virtuous. (PS 1.8.20)
The <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> atoms are few in the superior ones and more in the inferior ones;
taking that disequilibrium of the <s>rajas</s>-<s>guṇa</s>, the first-born (<s>Aniruddha</s>) himself — (PS 1.8.21)
resides at the end of all subtle bodies, causing destruction;
<s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> were created, having the nature of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Śiva</s> [respectively]. (PS 1.8.22)
The lord of <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Bhū</s>, and <s>Durgā</s>, named <s>Viśva</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Prājña</s>,
white, red-natured, and dark blue — assuming infinite forms, (PS 1.8.23)
<s>Hari</s>, entering the three stations situated in each subtle body —

children.text: tadā hyavasthā tritayaṃ tadviśeṣādime sukham // PS_1,8.24 //
children.translated_text: then indeed [there are] three states; from the distinction of these, happiness [arises] for the first. (PS 1.8.24)
With nineteen faces each, named <s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s>,
going right and left — thus the faces of the Person, the middle-going one — (PS 1.8.25)
elephant-like indeed are the faces of those two; the function of the faces moreover —
<s>Viśva</s>, situated in the right eye, established in <s>sattva</s>, from the portion of <s>sattva</s>, (PS 1.8.26)
for the superior, middling, and inferior ones who identify with the principles —
through three faces situated in <s>sattva</s>, the state called waking (<s>jāgrat</s>) — (PS 1.8.27)

children.text: karotyayaṃ madhyagākhya tritayena sa eva hi /
children.translated_text: this one produces; by the triad called 'middle-going,'
for the high, middling, and low servants among mortals, the state called waking — (PS 1.8.28)
he produces, by three faces situated inwardly;

children.text: niraṃśānāṃ ca jīvānāṃ jāgratāṃ sampravartakaḥ // PS_1,8.29 //
children.translated_text: and for souls without parts, he is the activator while they are in the waking [state]. (PS 1.8.29)
For men, thus through the left-going faces; for women, he does likewise;
in infinitely many births, through mortal bodies, whatever was done — (PS 1.8.30)
in the waking state, by mind, by speech, or by the sense organs —
the <s>sāttvic</s> and other <s>karmas</s>, of high and low [character], that were performed — (PS 1.8.31)
whatever they all are, and all the intentions as well —
when destroyed, the unseen traces (<s>adṛṣṭas</s>) and marks (<s>liṅgas</s>) thereof continue to reside. (PS 1.8.32)

children.text: teṣu bhogāya dattāni bhuktvā nāśaṃ prayānti hi /
children.translated_text: Among them, those [karmas] given for enjoyment, having been experienced, go to destruction;

children.text: bhogāya ca pradattāni ardhabhuktāni sarvaśaḥ // PS_1,8.33 //
children.translated_text: and those assigned for enjoyment are in every case only half-experienced. // PS_1,8.33 //
And some among them, having begun to be experienced, go to exhaustion through enjoyment;
the remainder of those that have begun [to bear fruit] become clearly [manifest] at the time of <s>aparokṣa</s> (direct realization). // PS_1,8.34 //

children.text: na nayānti ca sarvāṇi bhogayogyānya saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: And not all of them that are fit for enjoyment [reach fruition] — there is no doubt;
therein, <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā) makes what has badly begun to bear fruit, whether much or little. // PS_1,8.35 //
Through <s>bhagavadbhakti-yoga</s> (devotion to the Lord) — for such is the will of <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: hariṇā jīvabhogāya na dattāni hyanantaśaḥ // PS_1,8.36 //
children.translated_text: those [karmas] not given by <s>Hari</s> for the enjoyment of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) are infinite in number, // PS_1,8.36 //
heaped up by the millions — the unseen <s>karmas</s> residing in the <s>liṅga-śarīra</s> (subtle body),

children.text: sañcitānyapi tānīha aparokṣe sati sphuṭam // PS_1,8.37 //
children.translated_text: the <s>sañcita</s> (accumulated) ones too — at the time of <s>aparokṣa</s> (direct realization), clearly, // PS_1,8.37 //
even if burnt, they are indeed destroyed — there is no doubt.
A mortal, living in this <s>Bhārata</s> (India), constantly, by the thousands of millions, // PS_1,8.38 //
performs [karmas] helplessly, bound by <s>prakṛti</s> (material nature), endlessly;
through infinite births, infinite, of infinite lifespan in measure, // PS_1,8.39 //
the dissolution of self-performed <s>karmas</s> that have not been experienced comes through enjoyment;
of the infinite and great <s>sañcita</s> (accumulated karmas), even in periods of <s>Brahmā's</s> time, // PS_1,8.40 //

children.text: kvāpi no ghaṭate bhoktuṃ kintu śrīviṣṇudarśane /
children.translated_text: it is not possible anywhere to experience [them all]; but upon the vision of <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: naiṣāṃ phalaṃ hi jīvānāṃ bhavedityājñayā hareḥ // PS_1,8.41 //
children.translated_text: by the command of <s>Hari</s>, [saying] 'the fruit of these shall not come to be for these <s>jīvas</s>' — // PS_1,8.41 //
even those written on the records by <s>Citragupta</s> (the celestial record-keeper), again and again —
<s>Ramā</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other gods, who preside over all <s>karmas</s>, // PS_1,8.42 //

children.text: yacchanti na phalaṃ puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ vā tasya karhicit /
children.translated_text: do not give their fruit, whether meritorious or sinful, to him at any time;
cutting the written records, <s>Hari</s>, through his beloved <s>Yama</s>-messengers, // PS_1,8.43 //

children.text: bodhayantyapi he jīva na te sañcitato bhayam /
children.translated_text: instructs: 'O <s>jīva</s>, you have no fear from the <s>sañcita</s> (accumulated karmas).'

children.text: iti kāraṇato nāśaṃ sañcitasya vadanti hi // PS_1,8.44 //
children.translated_text: For this reason, they declare the destruction of <s>sañcita</s>. // PS_1,8.44 //
Destruction of <s>karmas</s> like the destruction of a pot is not approved;
of all that has well-begun [its fruition], exhaustion comes only through enjoyment. // PS_1,8.45 //
But <s>karma</s>, whether auspicious or inauspicious, performed after <s>aparokṣa</s> (direct realization),
is called <s>āgāmi</s> (forthcoming) by the wise — it will not cease. // PS_1,8.46 //
The <s>Citraguptas</s> (celestial scribes), the best of gods, do not record those on their tablets;

children.text: yacchanti na phalaṃ teṣāmato na śliṣyate janaḥ // PS_1,8.47 //
children.translated_text: they do not grant their fruits — therefore it does not attach to a person. // PS_1,8.47 //
From those <s>āgāmi karmas</s>: the <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons) seize the undesirable and the desire-prompted;

children.text: gṛhṇantīṣṭaṃ kāmyapuṇyaṃ tadiṣṭāḥ prāpnuvanti hi // PS_1,8.48 //
children.translated_text: and those who are desired receive the desire-prompted meritorious [karmas] — they indeed obtain [their fruits]. // PS_1,8.48 //
<s>Kali</s> (the demon of strife) seizes the <s>āgāmi</s> [karma] of hatred toward <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the like — no other [does so];
one liberated from <s>āgāmi</s> [karma] through devotion enjoys the <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) that is to be attained. // PS_1,8.49 //
Whether prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s> or not prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s>, performed through knowledge or ignorance,
performed in childhood, youth, or old age, by speech, body, or mind, // PS_1,8.50 //

children.text: bhītyā prītyā āveśato vā kṛtaṃ karma śubhāśubham /
children.translated_text: whether performed out of fear, love, or possession — <s>karma</s>, auspicious or inauspicious,

children.text: jñāyanneva karotyeṣaḥ bhuṅkte jāgṛddhi tatphalam // PS_1,8.51 //
children.translated_text: that which one performs knowingly — one experiences its fruit while awake. // PS_1,8.51 //
On the entire surface of the earth, in the caverns, in the atmosphere,
<s>svarga</s> (heaven) and all the worlds, inside and outside the cosmic egg, // PS_1,8.52 //

children.text: niraye vā tamasi vā vaikuṇṭhādiṣu vā janaḥ /
children.translated_text: in hell or in darkness or in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and the like — a person

children.text: jāgradbhuṅkte karmaphalaṃ viśvādhīnaḥ sadaiva hi // PS_1,8.53 //
children.translated_text: experiences the fruit of <s>karma</s> while awake, being always dependent on <s>Viśva</s> (the waking deity). // PS_1,8.53 //
Those established in <s>Ānantāsana</s>, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, and <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>,
in the worlds from <s>Mahar</s> to <s>Satya</s>, and outside the cosmic egg, // PS_1,8.54 //
the <s>tātvikas</s> (genuine beings), fixed in their own domains — not other beings —

children.text: svaprārabdhaphalaṃ yānti te sarve hyaparokṣiṇaḥ // PS_1,8.55 //
children.translated_text: they all go to the fruit of their <s>prārabdha</s> (commenced karma), all being ones who have attained <s>aparokṣa</s>. // PS_1,8.55 //
The non-<s>tātvikas</s>, devoid of portions, fit [for liberation] — they have no authority anywhere at any time;
what need to speak of those unfit, who are experiencers of suffering? // PS_1,8.56 //

children.text: riyuḥ trīn karmaṇā lokān jñānenaiva taduttarān /
children.translated_text: They attain the three worlds through <s>karma</s>; through knowledge alone, those [worlds] above;

children.text: tatra makhyā hariṃ yānti tadanye vāyumeva tu // PS_1,8.57 //
children.translated_text: therein, the foremost go to <s>Hari</s>; the others go to <s>Vāyu</s> alone. // PS_1,8.57 //

children.text: apakvā ye na te yānti vāyuṃ vā harimeva vā /
children.translated_text: Those who are unripened do not go to <s>Vāyu</s> or to <s>Hari</s>;
they remain stationed in their place, but are free from rebirth. // PS_1,8.58 //
In the worlds attainable by knowledge, from <s>Mahar</s> and above within the cosmic egg,
the non-<s>tātvikas</s>, devoid of portions, up to the liberated — their progression is upward. // PS_1,8.59 //
Their dwelling, by the merit of <s>prārabdha</s> (commenced karma), will not be without desire;
of the non-<s>tātvikas</s>, devoid of portions — [who may be found] even among the lowest of created mortals — // PS_1,8.60 //
for <s>tātvikas</s>, from the <s>prārabdha</s> merit and from the <s>sañcita</s> sin,
and from the merit and sin assigned for enjoyment, happiness and suffering and so forth are sanctioned. // PS_1,8.61 //
Dwelling in animal wombs is ordained for those
who are the low and partially-portioned among the portionless; for them, dwelling in hell is accepted. // PS_1,8.62 //
For those who are fit, neither from <s>prārabdha</s> nor from <s>sañcita</s> is there the destination of darkness;
for those unfit, from the ripening of hatred, the attainment of darkness will come. // PS_1,8.63 //
Those from gods to <s>Gandharvas</s> are called by the word 'god' in order;

children.text: devānāṃ nirayo naiva tamaścāpi kathañcana // PS_1,8.64 //
children.translated_text: for gods, there is never hell, nor darkness in any way. // PS_1,8.64 //

children.text: nā surāṇāṃ tathā muktiḥ kadācit kenacit kvacit /
children.translated_text: Nor is there liberation for the <s>Asuras</s> (demons) — ever, by any means, anywhere;
in <s>Bhārata</s> and the other eight divisions, in the seven continents, and in the mountains, // PS_1,8.65 //
for all, by sins and merits, through the principal <s>prārabdha</s> and <s>sañcita</s>,

children.text: tamo mithyājñānayogāt jñānenaiva hareḥ padam // PS_1,8.66 //
children.translated_text: darkness [comes] through the conjunction of false knowledge; by knowledge alone, the abode of <s>Hari</s>. // PS_1,8.66 //

children.text: teṣāṃ prāgukta karmottha phalaṃ vai jāgratā bhavet /
children.translated_text: For them, the fruit arising from the previously stated <s>karmas</s> comes in the waking state;

children.text: jāgratpravartako viśvaḥ so 'ja dakṣākṣigo bhavet // PS_1,8.67 //
children.translated_text: the activator in the waking state is <s>Viśva</s> — he, [as] <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā), would be the one stationed in the right eye. // PS_1,8.67 //
Taking the <s>sattva</s> (purity) arising from the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), moving thus in the subtle [state],

children.text: na dhātuḥ sañcitaṃ kāmyaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ pātakādikam // PS_1,8.68 //
children.translated_text: there is no accumulated desire-prompted [karma] for the [liberated] soul, nor the seen sins and the like, // PS_1,8.68 //
nor desolation, possession, suffering, and the like, nor doubt and misapprehension,

children.text: na duricchānānyaratiḥ na bhogecchā kusaṅgatiḥ // PS_1,8.69 //
children.translated_text: nor evil desire, nor disinterest in other [goals], nor desire for enjoyment, nor bad company, // PS_1,8.69 //
nor identification with the body, nor the impulse of the body and senses toward the wrong path;
there is always delight in desireless <s>karma</s>, true knowledge, and genuine <s>bhakti</s> (devotion). // PS_1,8.70 //
By the grace of this Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, there is always happiness;
the suffering-fruit preceded by dream, sleep, and illness — that he abandons. // PS_1,8.71 //

children.text: sontaraṅgo hareḥ sākṣāt sarvotkṛṣṭa priyo mataḥ /
children.translated_text: That inner form of <s>Hari</s> is directly regarded as the most exalted and beloved;
through the ripened remainders and the like, by <s>aparokṣa</s> (direct vision), [one sees] <s>Keśava</s>. // PS_1,8.72 //
From beginningless time, the hosts of <s>jīvas</s> born of <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā), always
behold <s>Hari</s> appropriate to themselves, and through births strive toward <s>aparokṣa</s> (direct realization). // PS_1,8.73 //
They strive through hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons); having seen the Lord at the end of a hundred <s>kalpas</s>,
through the worship of infinite qualities spoken of in the <s>Vedas</s>, performed in the <s>Kṛta</s> age, they attain the abode. // PS_1,8.74 //
The subtle body of that one — from <s>Vāsudeva</s> it then arose;

children.text: taddhehaliṅgajaṃ śuddhaṃ raja ādāya tejasaḥ // PS_1,8.75 //
children.translated_text: taking the pure luminous substance born from that body's subtle form, // PS_1,8.75 //
the Blessed <s>Hari</s>, the creator of dreams, dwells in the throat of the subtle [body];
the impression that action is to be performed through the eleven senses // PS_1,8.76 //
arises in the mind — but [the liberated one] does not perform it through effort.
Sleep, unconsciousness, madness, fear, disease, and fatigue — [these], according to the wise, // PS_1,8.77 //
become favorable through births and rebirths also;
the dream of unperformed <s>karmas</s> is the granter of the Lord's fruit. // PS_1,8.78 //
Infinite objects seen in dreams bestow happiness and suffering at that time;

children.text: na jāgradṛṣṭipathagāḥ kintu tatkāla kalpitāḥ // PS_1,8.79 //
children.translated_text: they do not enter the path of waking vision, but are projected at that time [alone]. // PS_1,8.79 //
In the dream of a healthy <s>jīva</s>, the Lord, using the infinite impressions
as material cause, with the principal [forms] mentioned before, as <s>Taijasa</s> (the dream deity), // PS_1,8.80 //
having fashioned many objects, the Lord of all shows [them];
therefore dream is real, since it indicates future fruits. // PS_1,8.81 //
For all <s>jīvas</s> from <s>Śeṣa</s> onward, moving thus at the appropriate time,
<s>Taijasa</s> is the dream-creator — thus he becomes the dream-creator for beings. // PS_1,8.82 //
Taking that <s>tamoguṇa</s> (quality of darkness), <s>Prājña</s> (the deep-sleep deity), entered into the subtle heart;
to the <s>jīva</s> bound in the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), stationed at the feet of the world-teacher, // PS_1,8.83 //
the one-faced one, born of the body, gives the state of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation);
swallowing half of the [jīva] bound in the <s>liṅga</s>, he gives the state of unconsciousness. // PS_1,8.84 //
Placing the one bound in the <s>liṅga</s> within his mouth, <s>Prājña</s>, in a diminished form,

children.text: yadāśliṣyati taṃ devaḥ tadā nidrāṃ prayacchati // PS_1,8.85 //
children.translated_text: when the god embraces him, then he bestows sleep. // PS_1,8.85 //

children.text: prājño jīveśvarastaṃ vai vinā jīvokṣamaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s>, the lord of the <s>jīva</s> — without him, the <s>jīva</s> is said to be incapable;

children.text: prājñaḥ kaṇṭhasthitaṃ prāpya jīvānāṃ svapnado bhavet // PS_1,8.86 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s>, having reached the one stationed in the throat, becomes the bestower of dreams for <s>jīvas</s>. // PS_1,8.86 //
Having taken the <s>jīva</s>, the lord of waking (<s>Jāgrat-Īśvara</s>), stationed in the right eye,

children.text: na prājñatejasau dhātuḥ svapnanidrā pravartakau(kā ?) // PS_1,8.87 //
children.translated_text: [operates]; <s>Prājña</s> and <s>Taijasa</s> are not the source-entities — they are the activators of sleep and dream. // PS_1,8.87 //
Without the state of <s>dhyāna</s>, through the avoidance of various evil <s>karmas</s>,

children.text: prājñaṃ jīveśvaraṃ prāhuḥ sa sarvahṛdisaṅgataḥ // PS_1,8.88 //
children.translated_text: they call <s>Prājña</s> the lord of the <s>jīva</s> — he is present in all hearts. // PS_1,8.88 //

children.text: sāṃśajīvaṃ sa vai prājño rūpaiṇyaikena pādayoḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Prājña</s> indeed, having placed the portioned <s>jīva</s> at his feet with one subtle form,
and having taken the conscious [jīva] with another subtle form together with the <s>liṅga</s>, // PS_1,8.89 //

children.text: saliṅgaṃ sa yadā viśve naikībhūto bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: when he, with the <s>liṅga</s>, will not become unified in <s>Viśva</s> (the waking deity),
if [however] the subtle one becomes unified with <s>Prājña</s> stationed in the heart, // PS_1,8.90 //
then the lord of the <s>jīvas</s> brings about the state of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation);
<s>Viśva</s> and the others are the bestowers of the three states for those devoid of portions. // PS_1,8.91 //
Except for the righteous ones, the world-teacher, all gods and earthly beings,
are made endowed with the three states by those beginning with <s>Prājña</s>. // PS_1,8.92 //
For those stationed in the upper worlds, [Viśva] is always the activator of the waking state;
thus, the all-pervading one created <s>Brahmā</s> with a subtle body. // PS_1,8.93 //
Thus <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> was the creator of the subtle body for <s>Vāyu</s> [and] for <s>Jayā</s>;
<s>Vāsudeva</s> made <s>Brahmā</s> the husband of <s>Sarasvatī</s>. // PS_1,8.94 //
<s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> ordained <s>Mukhyaprāṇa</s> (the chief vital force) as the husband of <s>Bhāratī</s>;
and <s>Pradyumna</s> was the creator of the subtle bodies of <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Bhāratī</s>. // PS_1,8.95 //
From them, through those two [goddesses], the two subtle bodies of <s>Vipaśeṣa</s> (distinction) came into being;
then <s>Vāyu</s>, named <s>Sūtra</s> (Thread-soul), and <s>Brahmā</s>, named <s>Puruṣa</s>. // PS_1,8.96 //
Of all eternal objects such as the <s>Vedas</s>, of the lineage of <s>jīvas</s>,
even in the creation of eternal things — those two are the presiding deities. // PS_1,8.97 //
Without those two wives, no object whatsoever can exist;
<s>Brahmā</s>, being without [direct] identification, though embodied, is [as if] disembodied. // PS_1,8.98 //
<s>Vāyu</s>, disembodied, is [known] by the names cloud, lightning, and the like;
the supreme white triad is to be spoken of — through yoga they preside over all. // PS_1,8.99 //
Then <s>Aniruddha</s>, in the course of time, for <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> together with their wives,
created subtle bodies three [times], four [times], and twenty-one times. // PS_1,8.100 //
Three times and twenty-one times he bestowed subtle bodies;

children.text: aniruddho vipādīnāṃ nīlādīnāṃ tathaiva ca // PS_1,8.101 //
children.translated_text: <s>Aniruddha</s> [did so] for <s>Vipā</s> (Speech) and others, for <s>Nīla</s> and others, likewise, // PS_1,8.101 //
and for <s>Sauparṇī</s> and two others, according to the order of time and place,
for all the <s>tātvikas</s> from <s>Indra</s> to <s>Puṣkara</s>, without exception — // PS_1,8.102 //
<s>Aniruddha</s> was the creator of the subtle [bodies] twenty-one times.

children.text: yadā yasya ca sūkṣmāptistatpūrvakṣaṇa eva ca // PS_1,8.103 //
children.translated_text: At whatever [time] the subtle body is obtained by whomever — at that very prior moment, // PS_1,8.103 //
the diversity of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) of the respective group of <s>jīvas</s> [arises] — thus also;
within five to seven months, by external measure, in all cases, // PS_1,8.104 //
the subtle creation of the <s>tātvika</s> gods took place from <s>Hari</s>;
then he, the creator of the universe, properly set in motion // PS_1,8.105 //
<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial matter), called <s>jaḍā</s> (inert), endowed with the state of imbalance of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>;

children.text: tato bindutrayaṃ jātaṃ satvaṃ ceti rajastamaḥ // PS_1,8.106 //
children.translated_text: thence arose the three <s>bindus</s> (points): <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. // PS_1,8.106 //
The <s>sattva-bindu</s> in the upper region; the <s>rajo-bindu</s> below that;
below that arose the <s>tamo-bindu</s> — and the original three <s>bindus</s> are gross. // PS_1,8.107 //
In the forms of <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Bhū</s>, and <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Mā</s> (Lakṣmī) is in order the presider over the three <s>guṇas</s> —
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>—these are the regulators of the order of the <s>bindus</s> (drops/points). // PS 1.8.108 //
<s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, together with their consorts, the two who preside over the three forms,

children.text: satvādibinduṣu śrīśca śritā naśvareṣu vai // PS_1,8.109 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) resides in the <s>sattva</s> and other <s>bindus</s>, in the perishable ones indeed. // PS 1.8.109 //
When there is imbalance in the <s>bindus</s> of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, the Lord of the universe,

children.text: brahmā saṅkarṣaṇātmā tu samudhṛtya rarakṣatuḥ // PS_1,8.110 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, who is of the nature of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, having raised [them] up, protected [them]. // PS 1.8.110 //
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the unborn, having entered the <s>sattva-bindu</s>, causes [it] to increase;

children.text: satvāvaraṇamādyaṃ ca cakre tatra vṛtodyamam // PS_1,8.111 //
children.translated_text: He made the first covering of <s>sattva</s>, exerting effort for that purpose. // PS 1.8.111 //
The one called <s>Brahmā</s>, who entered the <s>rajo-bindu</s>, in the region below that,
created the second covering, named after <s>rajas</s> itself. // PS 1.8.112 //
<s>Rudra</s>, stationed in the <s>tamo-bindu</s>, made the <s>tāmasa</s> covering;
that second covering, indeed of <s>rajas</s>, is contained within [it]. // PS 1.8.113 //
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>—two by two—<s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> with their consorts,
<s>Śrī</s>, <s>Bhū</s>, and <s>Durgā</s> respectively, in the first, first, and third coverings. // PS 1.8.114 //
They preside over the three <s>guṇas</s> in the gross bodies of their respective natures;

children.text: ādyaṃ śuklaṃ dvitīyaṃ tu raktaṃ nīlaṃ tṛtīyakam // PS_1,8.115 //
children.translated_text: the first is white, the second is red, and the third is blue. // PS 1.8.115 //
Due to the imbalance of the quality of <s>rajas</s>, within the three <s>guṇa</s> coverings,

children.text: mahadāvaraṇaṃ cakre brahmanāmā sa bhūpatiḥ // PS_1,8.116 //
children.translated_text: the one called <s>Brahmā</s>, that sovereign, made the <s>mahat</s> covering. // PS 1.8.116 //
The fourth covering there, consisting of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>—

children.text: jātābhyāṃ brahmavāyubhyāṃ jatau dvau dvau trirūpakau // PS_1,8.117 //
children.translated_text: from the two born, <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, two pairs of three forms were born. // PS 1.8.117 //
<s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, together with their consorts, preside over the <s>mahat-tattva</s>;
the Lord who controls the <s>mahat-tattva</s> is <s>Hari</s> Himself, called <s>Ānanda</s> (Bliss). // PS 1.8.118 //
The sons of the one named <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, stationed in <s>mahat</s>,

children.text: rajoguṇasya vaiṣamyāt sarvāṃśena mataḥ kalāḥ // PS_1,8.119 //
children.translated_text: due to the imbalance of the <s>rajo-guṇa</s>, are considered <s>kalās</s> (phases) with all their parts. // PS 1.8.119 //
Through the portion of <s>rajas</s>, the <s>kalās</s> of the ten sense organs [arise],
and through the portion of <s>tamas</s>, the <s>kalās</s> of the five subtle elements (<s>tanmātrā</s>) within the great elements [arise]. // PS 1.8.120 //
The sixteen <s>kalās</s> that come into being are eternally present;
from the <s>mahat-tattva</s> undergoing transformation, [they emerge] from the gross body of <s>Brahmā</s>. // PS 1.8.121 //
Born under the control of <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle) is considered threefold;
<s>vaikārika</s> (modified), <s>taijasa</s> (luminous), and <s>tāmasa</s> (dark)—thus ego is threefold. // PS 1.8.122 //
Due to the power of the rising sun-like [creator], the great ego has three colors;
the <s>vaikārika</s>, born from the portion of <s>sattva</s>, is declared white. // PS 1.8.123 //
The <s>taijasa</s>, arising from the portion of <s>rajas</s>, is proclaimed to be of red color;

children.text: mano hṛṣīkāṇi mātrāḥ pūrvaṃ sūkṣmasvarūpataḥ // PS_1,8.124 //
children.translated_text: mind, sense organs, and subtle elements—previously in their subtle form— // PS 1.8.124 //
these, situated in the <s>mahat-tattva</s>, sequentially took refuge in <s>ahaṅkāra</s>;

children.text: gāyatrīśo vidhiḥ satve viriñcastu rajoguṇe // PS_1,8.125 //
children.translated_text: the lord of <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā), [presides] in <s>sattva</s>; <s>Viriñca</s> (Brahmā) in <s>rajo-guṇa</s>; // PS 1.8.125 //
the lord of <s>Sāvitrī</s> truly resides in <s>tamas</s>, called <s>Brahmā</s>;
the lord of <s>Sarasvatī</s> dwells [there]—from such a triad of forms arise // PS 1.8.126 //
the three-formed <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, bearing those names, stationed in <s>mahat</s>;
through <s>Vidyā</s> and the other three, in those three—<s>Gāyatrī</s> and the others— // PS 1.8.127 //
sequentially, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Śeṣa</s> came into being by the will of <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: vipaśeṣau sabhāryā ca mahadrāje rajotridhār // PS_1,8.128 //
children.translated_text: the two distinguished ones with their consorts, in the <s>rajas</s> of <s>mahat</s>, the threefold <s>rajas</s>— // PS 1.8.128 //
by the command of <s>Hari</s> alone, they preside over the threefold <s>ahaṅkāra</s>;
<s>Rudra</s>, three-formed, arising from <s>Vidyā</s> and others, preceded by <s>Brahmā</s>, through three [forms]— // PS 1.8.129 //
with consort, three-formed, presiding over <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, possessed of a gross body;
the covering of <s>mahat</s> is considered to be situated within the womb of the <s>mahat-tattva</s>. // PS 1.8.130 //
<s>Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> accompanied by their consorts,
in all the <s>tattvas</s> mentioned and to be mentioned, at all times, // PS 1.8.131 //
they dwell; without them, <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Vīśa</s> and others are incapable anywhere.
From the <s>vaikārika</s> [ego] undergoing transformation, the <s>manas-tattva</s> (mind-principle)—the world-teacher // PS 1.8.132 //
created it, situated within the womb of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, that best of beings;

children.text: taijasāttu vikurvāṇāt hariṇā cendriyāṇi ca // PS_1,8.133 //
children.translated_text: and from the <s>taijasa</s> [ego] undergoing transformation, by <s>Hari</s>, the sense organs [were created]— // PS 1.8.133 //
five organs of knowledge and five organs of action;

children.text: sṛṣṭā bhāvīni kāle tu sṛjyaṃ vai bhūtapañcakam // PS_1,8.134 //
children.translated_text: these were created as future [potentials]; in due time, the five elements are to be created. // PS 1.8.134 //
Wherever the Lord was to place them, He arranged those sequentially;
from <s>ākāśa</s> (space) undergoing transformation, the subtle element of touch arose, by <s>Hari</s>'s [will]; // PS 1.8.135 //
then, having produced <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), He extended the wind-covering;
from <s>Vāyu</s> undergoing transformation, the subtle element of form arose; // PS 1.8.136 //
then, having produced fire, He extended the fire-covering;
from fire undergoing transformation, <s>Hari</s> produced the subtle element of water; // PS 1.8.137 //
then, having produced water, He made the water-covering;
from the water-enclosed [region] undergoing transformation, the subtle element of smell arose, of the all-pervading Lord; // PS 1.8.138 //

children.text: tataḥ pṛthvīṃ sanirmāya cakre bhūmyāvṛtiṃ hariḥ // PS_1,8.139 //
children.translated_text: then, having fashioned the earth, <s>Hari</s> made the earth-covering. // PS 1.8.139 //
Thus ends the eighth chapter of the first section of the glorious <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>.
The Blessed Lord said:
Within the earth-covering, suitable for the production of the cosmic egg,
a region measuring twice twenty-five <s>koṭi</s> (250 million) <s>yojanas</s> // PS 1.9.1 //
was made as open space by the Blessed Lord, the knower of place and time;
the <s>tattvas</s> that are unmixed are situated above the cosmic egg; // PS 1.9.2 //
the egg and everything within it is declared to be mixed (<s>saṃsṛṣṭa</s>);
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, named <s>Vijñāna</s> (Consciousness), is the protector of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>; // PS 1.9.3 //
in mind, sense organs, and subtle elements, the Lord of <s>Ramā</s> bears each respective name;
in space, wind, and fire, the Lord of all is named <s>Prāṇa</s> (Life-breath); // PS 1.9.4 //
in earth, He is named <s>Anna</s> (Food); He is also the protector of the water-covering;
the special earth, which is the double covering of the egg, // PS 1.9.5 //
water, fire, wind, space, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, <s>mahat-tattva</s>, and the <s>guṇas</s>—
the coverings of <s>sattva</s> and the rest, above the egg, are stationed sequentially from the earth-covering. // PS 1.9.6 //
Each succeeding one is ten times greater; <s>rajas</s> is double <s>tamas</s>,

children.text: rajaso dviguṇaṃ satvaṃ tato na prākṛtaṃ kvacit // PS_1,9.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>sattva</s> is double <s>rajas</s>; beyond that, nothing belongs to <s>Prakṛti</s>. // PS 1.9.7 //
In the region beyond and above, <s>Hari</s>, of the nature of <s>Aniruddha</s>,
who is ten times greater than that, also has the form of a covering. // PS 1.9.8 //
Then, ten times greater, are the ones named <s>Pradyumna</s> and <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>;
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, stationed above them, is considered ten parts greater than that. // PS 1.9.9 //
Beyond even that, in the infinitely multiplied, infinite, infinite expanse,

children.text: lakṣmīnārāyaṇau vyāptau maryādā na tayoḥ kvacit // PS_1,9.10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa</s> pervade; there is no boundary for them anywhere. // PS 1.9.10 //
<s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) is infinite in space, time, and qualities—never limited anywhere;
from <s>Aniruddha</s> first, through the <s>ṛjus</s> (straightforward ones) who have direct perception, // PS 1.9.11 //
together with the previously mentioned time, two were born, accompanied by consorts,
the three-formed <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, sequentially entering the three <s>guṇa</s> coverings; // PS 1.9.12 //
their coverings of <s>sattva</s> and the rest are declared to be their gross bodies;
from the subtle body of <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā) and <s>Iraṇa</s> (Vāyu) were born; // PS 1.9.13 //
those straightforward ones, four times [manifested], are considered stationed in the <s>mahat-tattva</s>;

children.text: teṣāṃ mahattatvameva sthūladehaṃ vadanti hi // PS_1,9.14 //
children.translated_text: their <s>mahat-tattva</s> itself is declared to be their gross body. // PS 1.9.14 //

children.text: tata strirūpau sa ṛjū tau dvau śāntīśajau kramāt /
children.translated_text: Then, three-formed and straightforward, those two, born sequentially from <s>Śāntīśa</s>,

children.text: trividhāhaṅkṛtigatau sa bhāryau sa ṛjū ubhau // PS_1,9.15 //
children.translated_text: entered the threefold <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, with consorts, straightforward, both; // PS 1.9.15 //
born through twenty-one doorways, they entered the <s>manas-tattva</s> and other <s>tattvas</s>;
the birth of the directly perceiving <s>ṛjus</s> and [others] of the hundred is outside the cosmic egg. // PS 1.9.16 //
Thus, the lords of <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>Rudra</s>, fit for their respective numbers,

children.text: aṇḍādbahiḥ sṛṣṭiyogyāḥ dṛṣṭeśāḥ netare kvacit // PS_1,9.17 //
children.translated_text: are fit for creation outside the egg; the seen lords, not others anywhere. // PS 1.9.17 //
Thus, from the three-formed [Brahmā], born previously by <s>Śāntīśa</s> in due time,
immediately after the birth of the straightforward <s>ṛjus</s> through the subtle [body], <s>Śeṣa</s> and the other three; // PS 1.9.18 //
the six beginning with <s>Nīla</s>, through the conjunction of time, then <s>Sāparṇī</s> and others in sequence;
by the unborn lord's [consorts] and the unborn's <s>Śeṣa</s>-consorts, with three consorts each, // PS 1.9.19 //
having gross bodies of the nature of the <s>ahaṅkāra-tattva</s>,
the directly perceiving ones fit for [higher] stations came into being; // PS 1.9.20 //
those very ones, in the twenty-one <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>mahat</s>,
with corresponding forms, born from the subtle <s>tattva</s> previously by <s>Aniruddha</s>— // PS 1.9.21 //
mind and the other <s>tattvas</s> became [their] gross bodies;
<s>Indra</s> and others down to <s>Puṣkara</s>, born from <s>Aniruddha</s>'s subtle [body], // PS 1.9.22 //

children.text: ekaviṃśadvārataste āsan cittādi tatvagāḥ (āsa śritādita tatvagāḥ)/
tāni sthūlādi tatvāni(dehāni) teṣām āsan krameṇa hi // PS_1,9.23 //
children.translated_text: those gross <s>tattvas</s> (bodies) became theirs sequentially. // PS 1.9.23 //
through twenty-one doorways, they were stationed in the <s>citta</s> and other <s>tattvas</s>;
Those born previously from <s>Śāntīśa</s>, beginning with <s>Indra</s>, with mind as [their] gross body,
born through two, three, five, six doorways, entered the <s>śrotra</s> (hearing) and other <s>tattvas</s>; // PS 1.9.24 //
born sequentially through seven, eight, nine, and ten doorways,
<s>Indra</s> and others down to <s>Puṣkara</s> [took] speech and other [faculties] as gross bodies. // PS 1.9.25 //
Then, those born through five doorways, previously by <s>Śāntīśa</s> through conjunction of time,

children.text: śabdādi sthūladehetāḥ tato jātāstu dvādigāḥ // PS_1,9.26 //
children.translated_text: [took] sound and other [subtle elements] as gross bodies; then those entering through two and more doorways were born. // PS 1.9.26 //
For the deities mentioned here, from whatever gross body [they arose],

children.text: bhāvīnāṃ ca padasthānāṃ tadvaśe sthitiriṣyate // PS_1,9.27 //
children.translated_text: and for those in future stations, their position is considered to depend on that. // PS 1.9.27 //
<s>Aniruddha</s>, the subtle creator, first [reaching] the appropriate place for these,
made creation, being the knower of place, time, purpose, and <s>tattva</s>. // PS 1.9.28 //
For the straightforward <s>ṛjus</s> stationed in all <s>tattvas</s>, within their subtle bodies,

children.text: satvāṇavo daśaguṇādhikā yānti ca sarvaśaḥ // PS_1,9.29 //
children.translated_text: the atoms of <s>sattva</s> increase tenfold and pervade everywhere; // PS 1.9.29 //
the atoms of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> increase by only a quarter;
for <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and others born through many doorways, within [their] subtle bodies, // PS 1.9.30 //
the atoms of <s>sattva</s> are equal, slightly increased, and fully increased;
the atoms of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, within the subtle [bodies] of <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), and other deities, // PS 1.9.31 //
by portions of two, three, five, six, seven, eight—[those of] <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Arka</s> (Sun)—
ending with twentieths, will increase sequentially. // PS 1.9.32 //
For that very reason and due to the previously mentioned causes,
in successively higher forms, dullness of intellect and the like are to be expected. // PS 1.9.33 //
In <s>mahat</s> and other [tattvas] above the cosmic egg, possession by <s>daityas</s> (demons) and the like is not accepted;
just as <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> increase in the subtle bodies, // PS 1.9.34 //
so too it is declared to be manifest in their gross bodies;

children.text: rajastamoṇavo vyaktiṃ yāsyantyeva tataḥ kramāt // PS_1,9.35 //
children.translated_text: the atoms of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> will become manifest sequentially. // PS 1.9.35 //
The <s>tattvas</s> in their prior forms exist as infinite;
the straightforward <s>ṛjus</s>, in all <s>tattvas</s>, shine in gradations of higher and lower. // PS 1.9.36 //
With consorts, stationed in all <s>tattvas</s> from low to high,
due to the predominance of the increase of atoms of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, [there is] intellectual distortion; // PS 1.9.37 //

children.text: naiva yāsyanti te sarve hareḥ priyatamāḥsadā /
children.translated_text: but they will never undergo that—all of them are ever most dear to <s>Hari</s>;
<s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s> arise from all the limbs of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // PS 1.9.38 //
<s>Śeṣa</s> and <s>Vipa</s> arose from the left channel (<s>vāma-nāḍī</s>) of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; <s>Śiva</s> likewise;
<s>Nīlā</s> and the others, <s>Vāruṇī</s> and the former; <s>Indra</s> and <s>Kāma</s> were born from the mind. // PS 1.9.39 //
With consorts, the preceptor [arose] from the intellect; <s>Manu</s>, the first, from the generative organ;
<s>Dakṣa</s> from the thumb; <s>Kāma</s>'s son; the <s>Manus</s> [arose] preceded by <s>Kāma</s>. // PS 1.9.40 //

children.text: marutaḥ śvāsataḥ sūryaḥ cakṣuṣaḥ candramā śruteḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Maruts</s> from the breath; <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun) from the eyes; <s>Candra</s> (Moon) from the ears;

children.text: dharmo hṛdaḥ sabhāryaśca varuṇo rasanotthitaḥ // PS_1,9.41 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s>, with consort, from the heart; <s>Varuṇa</s> arose from the tongue. // PS 1.9.41 //
<s>Bhṛgu</s> from the skin; <s>Agni</s> (Fire) from the mouth; born from the phallus, <s>Manu</s> went forth;
<s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Marīci</s> and others, <s>Mitra</s> from drinking; <s>Nairṛta</s> from [another source]; // PS 1.9.42 //
from <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Bhava-Gaṇapati</s>; <s>Śambhu</s> and <s>Jayanta</s> from the navel and feet;
the two <s>Nāsatyas</s> (Aśvins) from the two nostrils; and <s>Viśvaksena</s> arose from the mouth. // PS 1.9.43 //
The <s>Ṛbhus</s> (<s>Rutavas</s>/<s>Rubhavas</s>) from the feet; from the throat, the <s>Digdevas</s>, born of <s>karma</s>;
the <s>Rudras</s> from the cheeks; from the forehead, and the <s>Vasus</s> by the will of the all-pervading Lord. // PS 1.9.44 //
The <s>Ādityas</s> (solar deities) arise from radiance and are situated in the row of teeth;
<s>Sanaka</s> and others are born from the mind; <s>Jaya</s> and others [arise] from the sides.
The <s>Gaṅgā</s> and other rivers [arise] from the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels), from the great toes and other [parts] of the Lord;
all the unmentioned <s>tāttvika</s> (essential) beings are considered by the wise to arise from His sidelong glance.
<s>Śani</s> (Saturn) [arises] from the body; <s>Puṣkara</s> and others arise from the organs of action;
the unmentioned wives of deities arise together with their husbands.
These, in all the categories of reality, situated in the categories, abiding as the presiding deities of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Ramā</s>'s
declared limbs, born in sequence—they dwell as the presiding entities.
Thus in creation, outside the cosmic egg; and in liberation, thus under <s>Hari</s>'s control;

children.text: jātau jātau hi yastasmāt kāmastudgatiḥsutaḥ // PS_1,9.49 //
children.translated_text: in each birth, from that [source], <s>Kāma</s> (Desire) is the son who leads upward.
<s>Caṇḍa</s>, <s>Jaya</s>, and others are door-keepers; <s>Śaśāṅka</s> (Moon) and <s>Dhanapati</s> (Kubera) likewise;
all the lords of <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), even in their births, are <s>tāttvika</s> (essential beings).
Those higher than <s>Puṣkara</s>, higher than <s>Budha</s> (Mercury)—those unmentioned are declared;
thus, all those arisen from portions of <s>Śeṣa</s> (the cosmic serpent), from outside the cosmic egg entirely.
Indeed, nine <s>koṭis</s> (ninety million) of gods are presiding deities of the <s>sattva</s> (goodness) principle;
<s>Aja</s> (Brahmā), then <s>Vipas</s> (Sarasvatī), then from <s>Nīla</s>—the six wives of <s>Vipas</s>.
Then <s>Indra</s>, then the Moon; from that, <s>Prāṇa</s> (Vital Breath) and all the others born of <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind);
from <s>Indra</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>; then the divine sages—<s>Nārada</s> and others.
From <s>Indra</s>, <s>Guru</s> (Bṛhaspati); then the Sun; then the two <s>Jayas</s>, then <s>Vighnaprabhū</s> (Gaṇeśa);
and the <s>Abhavas</s> are remembered [as born] from the Sun; <s>Agni</s> (Fire); and from <s>Agni</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>.
The <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s>, the lord of <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
<s>Parjanya</s> (Rain-god), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), and others up to <s>Puṣkara</s>—all have arisen.
<s>Garutmān</s> (Garuḍa) dwells in all the categories; the deities of the path;

children.text: uttamānāṃ ca guravaḥ nīcā uttamasevakāḥ // PS_1,9.56 //
children.translated_text: the teachers of the highest, and the lowest who are servants of the highest.
Thus, in the <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, the ninth chapter of the first section.
<s>Śrī Haṃsa</s> (the Divine Swan) spoke:
Everywhere, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s and <s>Vāyu</s>'s <s>ṛjus</s> (upright beings) exist indeed;

children.text: aṇḍāntarbahisthā vā nānairjanma labhanti te // PS_1,10.1 //
children.translated_text: whether situated inside or outside the cosmic egg, they do not obtain birth by various [wombs].
For the delusion of the <s>asuras</s> (demons), they appear as if born from others;
all of them, from <s>Rudra</s> and others, are those who have direct perception of <s>Brahmā</s>—inherently <s>tāttvika</s> (essential).
Born of the lords of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle) who are born of <s>Vāyu</s>, they come into being indeed;
the creation of all the lower [beings] is by the highest, from the upper region of the [Lord's] limbs.
Thus creation is described in sequence; dissolution is remembered in reverse order;
the lords of the principles in the upper region of the cosmic egg—here, in the manner previously described.
Well-commenced, of many kinds, free from the connection of faults—

children.text: ye ye yathā yathā jātāḥ sṛṣṭikāle bhavanti hi // PS_1,10.5 //
children.translated_text: whoever is born in whatever manner at the time of creation, they come into being.
After the creation of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), all those born become possessed of gross bodies;
portions, bliss, strength, knowledge, place, time, direct perception—
dissolution, creation, entry into a station, qualities, characteristics, and beauty—
thus the fourteen great gradations of hierarchy are declared.
In the <s>Vedas</s>, in space and time, in the subtle and gross bodies, and in the imperishable,
in <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), of all <s>jīvas</s>, in the <s>mahat-tattva</s> (great principle) and the three <s>guṇas</s>—

children.text: aṃśā ṛjūnāṃ santyeva vipādyaṃśā na teṣu hi /
children.translated_text: portions of the <s>ṛjus</s> (upright beings) exist, but the portions of <s>Vipas</s> (Sarasvatī) and others do not exist in them;
in <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle), the portions of <s>Vipas</s> and others exist, but not the portions of <s>Indra</s> and others.
In the lowest [realms]—the immortals' minds, bodies, etc.—the highest gods
dwell through their portions; but the lowest do not enter into their own superiors.
Thus, both inside and outside the cosmic egg, the understanding of hierarchy arises from portions;
<s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā) has <s>sāyujya</s> (union) with all limbs [of Viṣṇu]; <s>Vāṇī</s> (Sarasvatī) with speech and mind as well.
The Lord grants <s>sāyujya</s> to the gods in the limbs from which they originate;
the highest have great bliss; connected with the lowest of the low—
the bliss of the lowest is less than a hundredth of the highest; that [bliss] leads upward from the highest.
In liberation, more than a hundredth above the highest—clearly in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island) and other [realms].
In the three stations, in the portion of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), the bliss is pure consciousness-made and powerful;
the bliss to be attained in the portions of <s>Bhū</s> and <s>Durgā</s> [is for those] who are purely <s>sāttvika</s>.
With bodies, infinite pure <s>sāttvika</s> substances fit for enjoyment—
fashioned by <s>Bhū</s> and <s>Durgā</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed Lord), to the succession of devotees—
gives abundantly to the highest, and only a little to the lowest;

children.text: tattadyogya nijānandaṃ dadāti puruṣaḥ svarāṭ // PS_1,10.16 //
children.translated_text: the self-sovereign <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) gives to each their own bliss appropriate to their fitness.
In liberation, for one whose desire for the great enjoyment of his own superior is slight,

children.text: na vidyate hi svānandapūrṇasya na punarjaniḥ // PS_1,10.17 //
children.translated_text: there is no rebirth, for one who is full of his own bliss.
Suffering, ignorance, and the like are not desired again for one whose subtle body is destroyed;

children.text: śataśabdo daśasahasraparaṃ prāptaṃ vadanti hi // PS_1,10.18 //
children.translated_text: they declare that the word "hundred" means ten thousand as its ultimate meaning.
The strength of the highest is abundant; of the lowest, only slight.
<s>Śeṣa</s> (the cosmic serpent), situated in the waters of the cosmic womb, bears the entire earth upon a single head;
he supports the continents, oceans, rivers, and mountains, always as if [they were] a mustard seed;

children.text: taṃ vai śeṣaṃ sahasrāsyaṃ vāyukūrmo mahābalaḥ // PS_1,10.20 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Śeṣa</s>, of a thousand mouths, is borne by the immensely powerful <s>Vāyukūrma</s> (Wind-Tortoise)
at the tip of his tail. <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) and the preceding [gods] are inferior in strength to <s>Śeṣa</s>;

children.text: bahavo gomahiṣyādyā eka kuñjara bhojane // PS_1,10.21 //
children.translated_text: many cows and buffaloes [are needed for] the food of a single elephant.
However many tortoise-elephants there may be—even in their <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions),

children.text: militā api nāgena yoddhumarhati na kvacitu // PS_1,10.22 //
children.translated_text: even assembled together, they are nowhere capable of fighting with the great serpent.
Similarly, the lower gods, even assembled in thousands of <s>koṭis</s>, by the highest gods
are unable to [contend]—how much less mortals and <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons)?
Therefore, the hierarchy of all is determined by strength;
having contemplated across infinite <s>kalpas</s>, situated inside and outside the cosmic egg—
past, present, and future—the aggregate of entities—
[<s>Vāyu</s>] always knows, like a fruit in the palm of one's hand, by the grace of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Beginningless, eternal, unsurpassed, without distinction, immediately following—
even he, having contemplated the qualities of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> beyond time—
of Him who is full of infinite auspicious qualities, from His infinite portions,

children.text: vibhaktānantabhāgaikabhāga jñaptau na hi kṣamaḥ // PS_1,10.27 //
children.translated_text: is not capable of comprehending even a single portion of the divided infinite portions.
Without the knowledge of the Lord's qualities, the knowledge of the <s>ṛjus</s> (upright beings)
is indeed capable of encompassing the past and future worlds.
Even contemplating Vaiṣṇava knowledge, it is greater than that of all <s>jīvas</s>;
the knowledge of <s>Vipas</s> (Sarasvatī) and others, even through contemplation of everything—
is capable of encompassing the world that is distinct from their own superiors;

children.text: na bhavedekadeśena jānantyete na cānyathā // PS_1,10.30 //
children.translated_text: it cannot [encompass it] in its entirety—they know [only] partially, and not otherwise.
The inert and the unconscious also—from <s>Śiva</s> and others down to <s>Puṣkara</s>—
bound by the subtle body, stationed in their positions, destined and having direct perception—
both inside and outside the cosmic egg, the <s>tāttvika</s> beings in their many forms,

children.text: sthitā api na jānanti sākalyena jagadgatam // PS_1,10.32 //
children.translated_text: even though situated, do not know in totality what exists in the world.
The knowledge of all <s>jīvas</s> from beginningless time is considered to be of two kinds:

children.text: svārūpikaṃ ca bāhyañca nityaṃ svārūpikaṃ matam // PS_1,10.33 //
children.translated_text: essential and external; the essential is considered eternal.

children.text: ajanyaṃ śāśvataṃ viṣṇoḥ bandhasya vaśagaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: [Viṣṇu's knowledge is] uncreated and everlasting; it is always subject to [His] control over bondage;
the <s>jīva</s>'s [knowledge is] subordinate to the lords of the limbs, subject to <s>māyā</s> (illusion) in due order.
Manifested through practice, up to the end of liberation; thereafter,
of one form, free from ignorance, dependent upon one's own superior—
the knowledge is a hundredfold less, whether regarding the Lord or the world;
<s>Padmabhū</s> (Brahmā, the lotus-born) knows the infinite <s>Veda</s>-declared qualities of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: padastho vā vimukto vā tadanye tadguṇasthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether stationed [in his position] or liberated, others, established in His qualities—
the worshippers of <s>Viṣṇu</s> have knowledge progressively a hundredfold less.
For the upright being, always situated in the material and immaterial bodies,

children.text: manasyanityaṃ yajjanyaṃ punaḥ punarapi sphuṭam // PS_1,10.38 //
children.translated_text: in the mind, the non-eternal [knowledge] that is produced, again and again, clearly—
that is called external, in the form of a mental modification, and always corresponding to reality.

children.text: teṣāṃ pañcavidhajñānaṃ kvacideva na sarvadā // PS_1,10.39 //
children.translated_text: Their fivefold knowledge [occurs] only sometimes, not always.
Free from possession by <s>daityas</s> (demons) and the like, always devoid of evil objects—
together with the witness-organs, covered by the subtle organs of the subtle body,
with gross organs well-connected to their proper objects—thus perceptual cognition [arises].

children.text: yadārthaiva tayā doṣaśūnyā sadyuktijā matiḥ // PS_1,10.41 //
children.translated_text: When it corresponds to reality and is produced from proper reasoning, free from defects—that is valid cognition.
The knowledge produced by reasoning is declared to be inferential;
perception, inference, and scripture are its means of valid knowledge.
Corresponding to reality, likewise [knowledge] arising from hearing the meaning of <s>Vedic</s> scriptures—
that which arises in the mind, born from one's own scripture, is indeed valid knowledge.
From a higher station to a lower station, situated in the categories in sequence—
at the time of the operation of the categories, [they have] powers appropriate to their essential nature.
That which arises from scripture is declared to be threefold;
knowledge born from the mind is declared to be external and active.
Perception and inference—scripture is their means of validation;
the <s>jīva</s> is the knower, and the objects are considered the causes.
The knowledge of <s>Rudra</s> and others that is external, born in the mind,
though supported by the three valid means such as perception—is also non-eternal.
Sometimes that knowledge corresponds to reality; sometimes it may not.
<s>Karmadevāja</s> and others, servants of the gods, are progressively lower;
all from the gods down to the <s>gandharvas</s> are declared to possess portions;
those without portions are the mortals, <s>gandharvas</s>, and others, always, down to the grass.

children.text: jīvā eṣāṃ svarūpantu jñanaṃ nityaṃ yathārthakam /
children.translated_text: The essential nature and knowledge of these <s>jīvas</s> is eternal and corresponds to reality;
less than the highest of the highest, and progressively [including] what does not correspond to reality.

children.text: bāhyaṃ janyamanityaṃ ca yathārthaṃ prāyaśaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: External [knowledge] is produced, non-eternal, and mostly corresponds to reality always;

children.text: riśvare vā jagati vā kramādalpāvagāhi ca // PS_1,10.51 //
children.translated_text: regarding the Lord or the world, it comprehends progressively less.
Thus the hierarchy of knowledge among gods, high and low, is established;
portions of the <s>ṛjus</s> (upright beings) exist in the three great groups, and not in the higher
regions—therein, the portions of <s>Rudra</s> and other gods do not [exist]; in the region below that,
the portions of <s>Rudra</s> of the <s>ahaṅkṛti</s> (ego-principle) and other gods always exist.
Therein, <s>Indra</s> and others do not abide; those residing in even lower regions—
the boundary of those who have not passed beyond the elements—in whatever region, whatever [limit] is declared.
The sixteen <s>kalās</s> (arts/digits), residing therein, are pervaded by their respective activities;
the <s>kalās</s> of mind, sound, hearing, and speech are pervaded by <s>ākāśa</s> (ether);
the <s>kalās</s> called skin, touch, and hand depend on <s>vāyu</s> (air);
the <s>kalās</s> called eye, form, and foot reside in the body of <s>tejas</s> (fire);
the <s>kalās</s> of tongue, taste, and the generative organ depend on <s>vāri</s> (water);
the <s>kalās</s> of smell, nose, and the excretory organ depend on the covering of <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth).
The <s>kalās</s> of the mind, the subtle elements, and the sense organs [are distributed] among the elements in due order;
those having authority over them, appointed by <s>Hari</s>, are <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) and others, down to <s>Puṣkara</s>.
At the time of the subtle and gross creation, the highest are in the upper regions;
the lowest of the low, by depending on the gods situated in the highest regions—
from higher to lower regions, they are established in the categories in sequence;
at the time of the operation of the categories, [they have] powers appropriate to their essential nature.
Thus the great hierarchy appropriate to station is declared.
By divine reckoning, in a century of years, in the arrangement of succession—
the births of the <s>ṛjus</s> (upright beings) are declared; they are considered to be within intervals of a thousand years;
<s>Vipas</s> (Sarasvatī) and others, and likewise <s>Indra</s> and others, [are born] at intervals of ten thousand years.
Born successively in due order, from time [manifesting as] low and high—
Now the hierarchy of direct perception of all is examined.
When the time comes for the recovery of the essential nature of all <s>jīvas</s>, from grass onward,
at the time appropriate for the practice of each <s>jīva</s> according to its fitness—
<s>Hari</s>, together with <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Vāyu</s> with their consorts, by his command,
in other continents (<s>dvīpas</s>) and regions (<s>varṣas</s>) — all those who are born everywhere,
those subject to their own <s>karma</s>, those dwelling in heaven, the atmosphere, and the earth,
those souls gone to various wombs, those situated in the lower realms beginning with <s>Atala</s> —
the Blessed Lord, desiring to uplift them, will cause them to be born in <s>Bhārata</s> (India);
there, among those born in human wombs, and among them the best of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> —
there, through actions that bring about the manifestation of all true forms,
joining them with the best of gurus who bestow all true knowledge fit for the worthy —
<s>Hari</s> arranges everything in different lands and at different times.
From those [as low as] grass up to mortals, and the <s>Gandharvas</s> — they are infinite.
Those without parts (<s>niraṃśa</s>), who depend on images (<s>pratīka</s>), are <s>karmayogins</s> (practitioners of action).
Those beginning with gods and <s>Gandharvas</s>, up to the naturally-born (<s>ājānaja</s>), are all together
not depending on images, those with parts (<s>sāṃśa</s>), progressively higher <s>jñānayogins</s> (practitioners of knowledge).
Those who see [<s>Hari</s>] situated in an image or situated in the body are called by those names.
From seeing the Lord outside the image, [they become] <s>karmadevās</s> (gods by action);
and those not depending on images are mostly <s>vijñānayogins</s> (practitioners of discernment).
For these, birth within the cosmic egg, direct perception (<s>aparokṣa</s>), and so forth are praised.

children.text: niraṃśāḥ pakvakāle tu utkrāmyaiva maharādigāḥ // PS_1,10.73 //
children.translated_text: The partless ones, when their time has ripened, departing upward, go to <s>Mahar</s> [<s>loka</s>] and beyond.

children.text: eṣāṃ laye svottameṣu praveśo naiva vidyate /
children.translated_text: For these, during dissolution, there is no entry into their immediate superiors.
For those beginning with gods and <s>Gandharvas</s>, dissolution [comes] by departing from the earth.
During the great dissolution, entry into one's immediate superiors occurs through the subtle body.
Those ascending and not ascending — the yogins proclaim them to be under the control of the lords who are not of the real (<s>tattva</s>) [category].
The real (<s>tāttvika</s>) ones ending with <s>Puṣkara</s> never undergo dissolution by departure;

children.text: yānti sthūlaśarīraiste svottameṣu viśanti hi // PS_1,10.76 //
children.translated_text: they go with their gross bodies and enter into their immediate superiors.
The yogins, who are <s>bhaktiyogins</s> (devotion-practitioners), call those sequential entries.

children.text: satkarmajñānabhaktī ca sarveṣāṃ sarvadāpi hi // PS_1,10.77 //
children.translated_text: Righteous action (<s>satkarma</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), and devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) — for all, at all times,
are indispensable; all [souls] likewise [distinguish themselves] by the predominance of each respectively.
The partless ones, through thousands of births appropriate to correct practice,

children.text: jñānantu daśabhiḥ prāpya sadbhaktiṃ tribhirāpya ca /
children.translated_text: attaining knowledge in ten [births], attaining true devotion in three —

children.text: dṛṣṭvā hṛdisthaṃ mucyante hyataste karmayoginaḥ // PS_1,10.79 //
children.translated_text: seeing [<s>Hari</s>] situated in the heart, they are liberated. Below them are the <s>karmayogins</s>.
Having performed righteous action without desire, they obtain the lineage of gurus.
The non-real (<s>atāttvika</s>) <s>devadāsas</s> (servants of gods), through a hundred births of righteous action,
having performed [that], through ten thousand great births attaining knowledge,
attaining devotion through three hundred [births], are liberated — these are the <s>jñānayogins</s>.
Below them are the <s>karmadevās</s>; above them are the <s>bhaktiyogins</s>.
Those from grass onward see him situated in their own hearts through appropriate births —
[seeing] the Lord distinguished by lamplight radiance, not the gods, not the mortal-born one.

children.text: ghaṭikārdhaṃ śarīre vā muktau śaktistu tādṛśī // PS_1,10.83 //
children.translated_text: For half a <s>ghaṭikā</s> (12 minutes), in the body, such is the power at the time of liberation;
the power of worship of pure consciousness alone — not superior to those of higher qualities.

children.text: teṣārm idṛśa evaṃ syāt apararokṣo hi nādhikaḥ // PS_1,10.84 //
children.translated_text: For them, direct perception (<s>aparokṣa</s>) would be of precisely this kind — not more;
they see the forms of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and others externally sometimes,
but see them as human; this is remembered as direct perception.
Those whose direct perception is in the gross heart — externally, those who have direct perception;
[they see] the soul-reflection situated in its own true form, and the vision of the independent one.
Direct perception through one's own true form — this is the same for all indeed.
For slightly less than a quarter-<s>ghaṭikā</s>, in the <s>Prākṛtic</s> (material) heart, in their own true form,
worms, insects, and the like see <s>Hari</s> by lamplight radiance;
sight through the eye of one's own true form is called direct perception (<s>aparokṣa</s>).
<s>Veda</s>, space, syllable, time — soul and Lord through material (<s>Prākṛta</s>) senses

children.text: na vedyā hi svarūpeṇa vedyā eva prakīrtitāḥ // PS_1,10.89 //
children.translated_text: are not to be known; but through one's own true form they are indeed to be known — thus it is proclaimed.
Through devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) and <s>Hari</s>'s grace, when the fivefold ignorance is destroyed,
when the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) shines like a jewel — for the soul situated in the subtle body,

children.text: jīvasya cakṣuṣī vyakto bhavataḥ svena paśyati /
children.translated_text: the two eyes of the soul become manifest; with its own [eyes] it sees
him situated in his own radiant true form, situated in the gross heart, gradually.
Those from insects see [<s>Hari</s>] barley-grain-sized; insects and the like, berry-sized (<s>badarī</s>);
bulls, thumb-tip-sized, resembling ten lamps —
they see <s>Hari</s>, the Lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), for a <s>ghaṭikā</s>-measured time,

children.text: samaṃ dīpaṃ cidānandaṃ cidānandātmakaṃ mṛgāḥ // PS_1,10.93 //
children.translated_text: as an equal lamp, consciousness-bliss, of the nature of consciousness-bliss. Deer,

children.text: khagāśca paśavo gāvaḥ hṛdgaṃ jīvagataṃ harim /
children.translated_text: birds, cattle, and cows — [they see] <s>Hari</s> situated in the heart, entered into the soul,
endowed with the radiance of a hundred lamps, for half a <s>ghaṭikā</s> and half of that.
As <s>saccidānanda</s> (being-consciousness-bliss) and self — by humans, the Lord is to be meditated upon;
humans [see him] like lightning; kings [see him] measured as ten lightnings.
Royal rulers [see him] with double that radiance; gods [see him] like the solar disk.
<s>Gandharvas</s> and ancestors — [they see] the Lord resembling a hundred suns.
The <s>gopīs</s> worthy of contact with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s limbs — [they see him] with the radiance of five thousand suns.
The naturally-born [see him] with the radiance of ten thousand suns; and so too the sons of <s>Agni</s>.
Among the groups of souls numbering four <s>lakṣas</s> (400,000) plus eighty <s>lakṣas</s> (8,000,000) [= 8,400,000 species],

children.text: daśaiva puruṣāḥ proktāstātvikāsteṣu pañca ca // PS_1,10.98 //
children.translated_text: only ten persons are proclaimed; among them, five are real (<s>tāttvika</s>),
five are inferior beginning from <s>Parjanya</s>, regarded as superior to <s>Puṣkara</s> —
with their wives, without <s>Soma</s>, situated both inside and outside the cosmic egg.
Thirty of the <s>Cāraṇas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>; seventy in all classes.
In the interval, as long as the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s> endures,
for that long — in each day within the cycle of years —
all those with parts, the non-real, all measured by the number to be stated,
in each <s>kalpa</s> too, are those with direct perception who are established in their positions.
The <s>Apsarases</s> beginning with <s>Urvaśī</s>, a hundred, with portions measured by the number eight,
are equal to the naturally-born; the others are equal to the <s>karmadevās</s>.

children.text: śataṃ pitṝṇāṃ saptaiva teṣūrvaśyādibhiḥ samāḥ // PS_1,10.103 //
