children.translated_text: Among the ancestors, there are a hundred — seven of them are equal to <s>Urvaśī</s> and the rest.
The others are less than the naturally-born, and inferior to them in order.

children.text: gandharvāstu śataṃ teṣu aṣṭau tulyāśca karmajaiḥ // PS_1,10.104 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Gandharvas</s> are a hundred; among them, eight are equal to the action-born.
All the <s>ṛṣis</s>, measured by a hundred <s>koṭis</s> — twenty are the highest.

children.text: teṣveva tāvatviṣṭābhiḥ śatakaṃ karmajaiḥ samam // PS_1,10.105 //
children.translated_text: Among those very ones, with that many excellent worship — a hundred are equal to the action-born.
The others are equal to the naturally-born; and so too the sons of <s>Agni</s>.
Sixteen thousand, a hundred and thirty are of the <s>Cāraṇas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>.
The <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, and others — seventy in all classes.

children.text: śataṃ siddhājānajākhyā paśyanti hṛdi jīvagam // PS_1,10.107 //
children.translated_text: A hundred <s>Siddhas</s>, called naturally-born — they see in the heart, entered into the soul,
<s>Hari</s> with the radiance of a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) suns; the <s>karmadevās</s> [see him] situated in the gross heart, externally,
measured as the fourteen worlds — those depend on images (<s>pratīka</s>).
Mortals [see him] for only two <s>ghaṭikās</s>; the best of kings for up to three <s>nāḍīs</s>;
likewise the mortal <s>Gandharvas</s> — [they see] the Lord for up to four <s>nāḍīs</s>.
The divine <s>Gandharvas</s> for up to six <s>nāḍīs</s>; the <s>gopīs</s> for up to one <s>yāma</s> (watch, 3 hours).
The <s>ṛṣis</s> and the sons of <s>Agni</s>, numbering a hundred minus one <s>koṭi</s> —
including the naturally-born — [they see] the Guru of the World for a time measured by ten <s>ghaṭikās</s>.
The <s>karmadevās</s> see the Supreme Lord until midday.
Those free from rivalry with their immediate superiors, free from bad <s>prārabdha</s> (commenced karma),
free from positive-form ignorance, free from possession by <s>Daityas</s> (demons) —
they see the Lord of the universe at the time of the previously stated radiance.
The real (<s>tāttvika</s>) ones, free from the previously stated faults, [see] <s>Hari</s> always
for the entire day. These faults indeed [afflict] the lower ones;
among the highest of the highest, they are slight, and in others they are regarded as moderate.

children.text: brahmaṇo doṣa sambandho na kvāpi kva cad dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Any connection of fault with <s>Brahmā</s> is never seen anywhere.
Kings, mortal <s>Gandharvas</s>, and those above — [they worship] qualities beginning with six, ten,
a hundred, ten thousand, and those measured by <s>lakṣas</s> and <s>koṭis</s>,
and <s>arbuda</s> (hundred million) portions of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s qualities, and all those even beyond that,
the infinite qualities proclaimed in the <s>Vedas</s> — <s>Brahmā</s> worships, and no other.

children.text: martyoccā hṛdi devāṃśca padasthā pīṭhadevatāḥ // PS_1,10.117 //
children.translated_text: The highest mortals see the gods in the heart, those established in their positions, the pedestal (<s>pīṭha</s>) deities,
and also the gods dwelling in the coverings (<s>āvaraṇas</s>), and the <s>maṇḍala</s> (disc) as well,
the <s>suṣumnā</s>, the seven lotuses, and the Lord dwelling in them,
the lord of the stations, and the lord of the root — kings and mortal singers [see these].
Those situated in the <s>iḍā</s> and <s>piṅgalā</s> <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels), progressively higher, pervading the entire body,
the lords of the principles (<s>tattvas</s>) and all the forms of <s>Hari</s> situated in them —
meditating upon and worshipping [these], those called the naturally-born (<s>ājānaja</s>) gods are liberated.
These, and also those situated in images who depend on the feet of <s>Hari</s> —

children.text: karmadevā atatveśā api rūpāṇi sarvaśaḥ // PS_1,10.121 //
children.translated_text: the <s>karmadevās</s>, even those who are not lords of principles — all the forms
and also the <s>Virāṭ</s> (cosmic) form — having worshipped and fully worshipped, they are liberated.

children.text: apratīkālambanāste tu karmadevāḥ surā api // PS_1,10.122 //
children.translated_text: Those who do not depend on images — the <s>karmadevās</s> and gods too —
for the one whose <s>liṅga</s> is abandoned, the liberated one, from grass and insects onward,
their bodies of true form (<s>svarūpadeha</s>) all extend ten <s>yojanas</s> (approximately 80 miles).
For trees and the like, and deer and the like — the radiance is double that.
For liberated mortals, <s>Śūdras</s> and others — beyond that,
extending by one, two, three, four additional [units of] radiance, always.
The <s>kṣatriyas</s>, mortal <s>Gandharvas</s> — they have two-fold, three-fold additional radiance from that.
All around, equal to [Mount] <s>Meru</s>, is the radiance of the divine <s>Gandharva</s> host.
The ancestors, liberated at the time of <s>Cira</s>, have radiance up to <s>Bhuvarloka</s>.
The <s>gopīs</s> worthy of contact with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s feet — they have radiance of the level just below.
The naturally-born are equal to them, shining up to <s>Svarga</s> (heaven).

children.text: yasya yasya ca jīvasya prakāśo yatra ceritaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever radiance of whatever soul has been declared, and wherever —
by divine [sight], through external vision, <s>Hari</s> appears like the highest mortal.
The body of <s>saccidānanda</s> (being-consciousness-bliss) cannot be an object of external sight.
Having seen and worshipped the <s>Virāṭ</s> (cosmic) body, the <s>karmadevās</s> are liberated.
Such radiance, to that extent — one sees <s>Viṣṇu</s> with the eye

children.text: svārūpikeṇa bādhyena naiva paśyanti ceśvaram // PS_1,10.130 //
children.translated_text: of one's own true form; with the obstructed [eye], one does not see the Lord.
They do not see, nor do they worship the Lord who pervades the cosmic egg (<s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>).
Those from <s>Puṣkara</s> onward up to <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — [they see] him who has all the previously stated forms,
outside the egg, from earth and the other elements up to the <s>manas</s>-<s>tattva</s> (mind-principle) host —

children.text: dṛṣṭvādhyātvopāsya sarve muktiṃ yāsyanti kālataḥ // PS_1,10.132 //
children.translated_text: having seen, having meditated upon and worshipped, they all shall attain liberation in time.
Those capable of seeing that situated in <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) and worshipping <s>Īśāna</s> —
those from <s>Puṣkara</s> up to great <s>Indra</s>, with progressively greater radiance,
[they see] the god with the radiance of a <s>koṭi</s>-<s>arbuda</s> (billion) suns — <s>Vāmadeva</s> and others [see] <s>Hari</s>,
having worshipped the Lord pervading the <s>ahaṃkāra-tattva</s> (ego-principle) body —

children.text: mucyate ca mahattatve tamasyapi tataṃ harim /
children.translated_text: one is liberated. In the <s>mahat-tattva</s> (great principle) and in <s>tamas</s> too, <s>Hari</s> pervading [those] —
<s>Vāruṇī</s> and others preceding her see [him]; those situated in <s>tamas</s> shall be led [to liberation].
[They see] the imperishable one, pervading up to the boundary of <s>sattva</s>, with the radiance of infinite suns —
having worshipped [him], <s>Gīr</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>) attains liberation; and with even greater radiance beyond that.
<s>Brahmā</s> alone sees [<s>Hari</s>] entered into the covering of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and no other.

children.text: yāvatpaśyanti taṃ jīvaṃ tāvatsāmānyaruk sa hi // PS_1,10.137 //
children.translated_text: As long as they see that soul, for that long they have ordinary radiance;
as long as <s>Viṣṇu</s> is to be worshipped, for that long they have special radiance.

children.text: brahmaṇo naiva sāmānyarugviśeṣaprabho hi saḥ // PS_1,10.138 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> indeed has neither ordinary nor special radiance [separately] — he has both.
The portions of the bliss-form of souls are exceedingly small, abiding in their fitness.
Just as the radiance belonging to <s>Bhāramāyā</s>, pervading all regions,
the lamplight radiance entered into sunlight — as it does not shine,
so too the radiance of <s>Māyā</s> extinguished by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s radiance does not shine.
Thus, the radiance of the lower merges into the radiance of the higher;

children.text: tathāpi ca yathārthajñā muktāptai tatvavettamāḥ // PS_1,10.141 //
children.translated_text: yet those who know things as they truly are — the liberated, the accomplished, the foremost knowers of reality — (PS 1.10.141)

children.text: yo yāvatīṃ harau kāntiṃ vetyasau tacchatāṃśabhāk /
children.translated_text: whoever knows a certain measure of <s>Hari</s>'s splendor, that one partakes of a hundredth part of it;
the radiance shines forth — let the foremost knowers understand the hierarchy of radiance. (PS 1.10.142)
Thus, in the <s>Śrī Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, in the first section, the tenth chapter.
<s>Śrī Haṃsa</s> said:
Among males — <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, the sages, and the like — the Lord of <s>Ramā</s>,

children.text: puṃ rūpeṇa viśeṣāveśādikaṃ sarvadā hariḥ // PS_1,11.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, in male form, always performs special empowerment (<s>viśeṣāveśa</s>) and the like. (PS 1.11.1)
He does so among women — <s>Mā</s> (Lakṣmī), <s>Vāgīr</s> (Sarasvatī), and <s>Vāyu</s>'s wife, in their essential forms;
<s>Viṣṇu</s> performs special empowerment according to the fitness and the nature of the connection. (PS 1.11.2)
In the foremost ones, a single one enters as the special self — through those gods (or through their own [capacities]);
the Lord, the master of ascetics, causes great deeds that are impossible for [ordinary] souls to be accomplished. (PS 1.11.3)
The type of empowerment (<s>āveśa</s>) that is acknowledged in the highest of the highest souls
does not exist in the lower souls — therefore they are of little power. (PS 1.11.4)
Among the gods stationed in [their respective] positions, there is no such empowerment for those who have attained liberation;
nor is there empowerment in those without parts; in those with parts, from <s>Aja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) down to the lowest-born. (PS 1.11.5)
In all the <s>avatāras</s> of <s>Vāyu</s>, it is indeed special empowerment;
in the essential form, subtle body, and gross body — always. (PS 1.11.6)
For the sake of protection, in all principles (<s>tattvas</s>), the Lord always dwells;

children.text: āveśo(tha) na tathā viṣṇorviśeṣākhyaḥ sureṣvapi // PS_1,11.7 //
children.translated_text: but the empowerment of <s>Viṣṇu</s> called 'special' is not the same even among the gods. (PS 1.11.7)
Sometimes in manifestation, sometimes in enjoyment — sevenfold empowerment in the cosmic-egg-born ones;
above the cosmic egg, always in the gods, and inwardly in the righteous ones, it is acknowledged. (PS 1.11.8)
The empowerment of the highest gods in the lower ones is sometimes acknowledged;
for the sake of strength, the Lord performs empowerment in the <s>asuras</s> (demons) — the heroic one. (PS 1.11.9)
He gave commands; the arrogant ones, empowered by those [commands], were destroyed by the gods, by <s>Hari</s>'s will;

children.text: bhavanti nityadā viṣṇuḥ sureṣvantarhito hi saḥ // PS_1,11.10 //
children.translated_text: they are always [thus]; <s>Viṣṇu</s> indeed is hidden within the gods. (PS 1.11.10)
Qualities such as knowledge, bliss, strength, and the like are considered common;
[they exist] from grass and the like up to <s>Brahmā</s>, and even in <s>Māyā</s> and in <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). (PS 1.11.11)
Nevertheless, in the lower of the low, the qualities and the like are based on analogy;
common ones, those of the same class, those of a different class, and those of distinctive [nature]. (PS 1.11.12)
Independence, self-delighting nature, pervading with good qualities,
absence of dependence on others, and controllership — [these belong to] the teacher of the universe. (PS 1.11.13)
Being the agent of creation and the like — these are considered qualities of a different class in <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: akṣa(ra)tvādayo māyāṃ naiva te brahmaṇi sphuṭam // PS_1,11.14 //
children.translated_text: imperishability and the like and <s>Māyā</s> — they are clearly not in <s>Brahmā</s>. (PS 1.11.14)
Righteousness, natural superiority, presiding over eternal substances,
sovereignty over all, being subject to effect in the subtle body — (PS 1.11.15)
fitness for desireless [action] and the like — these are recalled as qualities of a different class;

children.text: ete harīrayoḥ proktāḥ naiva te vipaśeṣayoḥ // PS_1,11.16 //
children.translated_text: these are said to belong to <s>Hari</s> and <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), not to the two [other] distinguished ones. (PS 1.11.16)
Thus, in these foremost ones, the qualities of a different class have been stated — they do not belong to the lower ones;
yet because of the truly infinite nature of these, liberation can never indeed be [fully] described. (PS 1.11.17)
Beginning from the <s>karma</s>-deities, <s>Brahmā</s> — in those embodied ones,
the lines of the discus (<s>cakra</s>), conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>), and the like [appear] — arrow, spear, goad, and the like, (PS 1.11.18)
javelin, lance, axe-mark, plough, auspiciousness, nectar, and the like;
cow, sesame, wheat, parasol, fly-whisk, gateway, (PS 1.11.19)
banner, upward fan-shape, swing, chariot-shapes;
fish, tortoise, lion, and the like; bull, gem-bearer, and the like; (PS 1.11.20)
<s>Garutmat</s> (Garuḍa), <s>Śeṣa</s>, and other lines — on the right foot,

children.text: puṃsāntu dakṣiṇepāde strīṇāṃ vāme vasanti hi // PS_1,11.21 //
children.translated_text: for men on the right foot, for women they reside on the left. (PS 1.11.21)
Cow, conch, and mace lines on the left [foot] of men are considered auspicious;
in the lower [beings], the marks are of diminished form; in the foremost, they are of elevated form. (PS 1.11.22)
All the lines are always complete in <s>Prāṇa</s> (<s>Vāyu</s>), in <s>Māyā</s>, and even in <s>Hara</s>;
even among those, there is a hierarchy of superiority; the lines are the cause of [that] superiority. (PS 1.11.23)
One who is ninety-six finger-breadths [in height], of the proportions of a banyan tree (<s>nyagrodha-parimaṇḍala</s>),
seven [spans in] foot-[height], four [spans in] hand-[width], endowed with the thirty-two [major] marks — (PS 1.11.24)
in the bodily limbs of the virtuous, in five places there is length,

children.text: hṛsvatvaṃ pañcasu tathā saptasthāneṣu raktimā // PS_1,11.25 //
children.translated_text: shortness in five likewise, and redness in seven places. (PS 1.11.25)

children.text: ṣaḍaunnatyaṃ yasya samyak pṛthutā triṣu yasya tu /
children.translated_text: For one who has six [places of] elevation properly, and breadth in three,

children.text: gambhīratā ca laghutā triṣu sthāneṣu bhāti vai // PS_1,11.26 //
children.translated_text: depth and lightness shine in three places indeed. (PS 1.11.26)

children.text: sa sulakṣaṇasampannaḥ sa tu jñānaprado gurūḥ /
children.translated_text: He, endowed with auspicious marks, is a teacher who bestows knowledge;

children.text: martyottameṣu vai viṃśallakṣaṇāni bhavanti hi // PS_1,11.27 //
children.translated_text: among the foremost of mortals, indeed twenty marks exist. (PS 1.11.27)
Gradually, one by one, the auspicious marks are increased;
all the marks are fully complete in <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and <s>Ramā</s>. (PS 1.11.28)
In the body and in the essential nature, in all righteous means fully —
they are exceedingly manifest in the superior ones, and unmanifest in the others. (PS 1.11.29)
Now hear the hierarchy in creation — what was previously and subsequently [stated]:,
the creations of self, subtle, quality, and gross were previously mentioned. (PS 1.11.30)
The five subtle elements (<s>tanmātras</s>), the unmanifest elements, through the fivefold activity, in sequence —
the previously mentioned fivefold ignorance of the nature of being arose therefrom. (PS 1.11.31)
The delusion of elemental bodies, even in some manifest wombs —

children.text: aṇḍādūrdhvamiyaṃ sṛṣṭi rasaṃ sṛṣṭeti kīrtyate // PS_1,11.32 //
children.translated_text: above the cosmic egg, this creation is called the secondary creation (<s>rasaṃsṛṣṭi</s>). (PS 1.11.32)
From <s>Mahat</s> up to the cosmic egg, it is called the primary emanation (<s>sarga</s>);
the created cosmic egg and its contents in entirety are proclaimed [as such]. (PS 1.11.33)
People call the secondary creation (<s>anusarga</s>) whatever arose from <s>Aja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) within the cosmic egg;
the gods beginning with <s>Mahat</s> were all powerless at the creation of the cosmic egg. (PS 1.11.34)
They praised the Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>), endowed with thirty-seven years' [worth of time];

children.text: kālaṃ tato hariḥ sarvatatvajātaṃ tadantakaiḥ // PS_1,11.35 //
children.translated_text: then, <s>Hari</s>, [taking] the entire collection of principles (<s>tattvas</s>), with their respective end-portions — (PS 1.11.35)
taking and combining the allotments, the unborn one made them unified;

children.text: tacca tredhā vibhajyeśaḥ teṣvādyaṃ bhāgamīśvaraḥ // PS_1,11.36 //
children.translated_text: and dividing it threefold, the Lord, the sovereign — (PS 1.11.36)
having taken the first portion, the Lord named <s>Viṣṇu</s>, having swallowed it, [deposited] <s>Śrī</s> herself;
the Lord of persons placed that seed of his own nature into her. (PS 1.11.37)
In the middle of the earthen covering, she gave birth to the cosmic egg, the body of <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>);
having created the cosmic egg of fifty <s>koṭi</s> (500 million) [<s>yojanas</s>] in extent, the teacher of the universe — (PS 1.11.38)
accompanied by all conscious temple-[deities], entered the egg of heroes;
with the cosmic egg filled with water, it became the support of all worlds. (PS 1.11.39)
That <s>Viṣṇu</s>, called <s>Padmanābha</s> (Lotus-naveled), in the auspicious waters of the earth's shaft,
<s>Hari</s>, the sovereign, from <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), by his own essential form, is absolutely non-different. (PS 1.11.40)
Endowed with all ornaments, with a thousand feet, eyes, and arms,
with head turned inward (or westward), face upward, wearing a yellow garment, he reclined evenly. (PS 1.11.41)
At the time of the creation of the cosmic egg and the rest, from the collection of principles divided threefold,
from the first, the cosmic egg arose; the other — <s>Padmanābha</s>, the foremost, the great all-pervading one — (PS 1.11.42)
having created it and placed the gift of earth at the navel — golden,
he caused a lotus to grow; from its bulb, the earth then came into being. (PS 1.11.43)
With seven continents and oceans and the like, filled with dense darkness and water,
fifty <s>koṭi</s> in extent, situated in the middle region of the cosmic egg — (PS 1.11.44)
one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in breadth, of exceedingly firm foundation;
twenty-five <s>koṭi</s> [<s>yojanas</s>] minus one <s>lakṣa</s> — the embryonic water below — (PS 1.11.45)
of <s>yojanas</s>; above that, the earth was established by <s>Hari</s>;
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, named <s>Bhū</s> (Earth), situated on the earth, is called after the embryonic water. (PS 1.11.46)
In things to be described and things already described, in insentient and conscious [entities], he bears that name;
the support, the protector, bearing all names, the supporter of all, the Lord. (PS 1.11.47)
<s>Meru</s>, situated in the middle of the earth, is four-sided and golden;
measured at one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height, with peaks of jewels. (PS 1.11.48)
Now, it is stated to be sixteen thousand <s>yojanas</s> in width;
of that extent is the measure of the earth — it alone is the abode of all the gods. (PS 1.11.49)
Above, double that [width] in length — eighty thousand <s>yojanas</s>
plus four — raised above the earth on all sides, auspicious. (PS 1.11.50)
In the eight directions, east and so forth, from <s>Meru</s>, the abodes of the world-protectors (<s>lokapālas</s>)
exist — all auspicious, [measuring] two and a half thousand each. (PS 1.11.51)
Four-sided, and in the middle of them, four times that extent in width,
are the assembly halls of <s>Brahmā</s>, made of jewels and gold. (PS 1.11.52)
Among them: <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Kravyāt</s> (the flesh-eater), <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Anila</s> (Wind), <s>Kṣapa</s> (Night = Kubera),
and <s>Śiva</s> — they with their wives, with their retinues and attendants. (PS 1.11.53)
In the middle of those, a pavilion (<s>maṇḍapa</s>), and the executors of <s>Vidhi</s>'s (<s>Brahmā</s>'s) commands likewise;
there, the lord of speech (<s>Vāṇīśvara</s>), upon the fine head of the serpent <s>Ananta</s>. (PS 1.11.54)
In the middle of the world-protectors' abodes, in the four directions from <s>Vindhya</s>,
equal [in measure], all auspicious, eight and a half thousand [<s>yojanas</s>] in extent — (PS 1.11.55)
<s>Mandāra</s>, <s>Pārijāta</s>, and other [trees] with divine flowers and fruits and canopies;
rivers and lakes there, with lotus and other flowering plants. (PS 1.11.56)
Attended by various celestial women, with swans and other birds;
attended by servants of the same class, from <s>Aja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) down to the lowest-born. (PS 1.11.57)
Attended — the best of mountains, shining, radiant, of divine-mountain expanse;
the abodes of gods adorned with divine ornaments, garments, and the like. (PS 1.11.58)
In the eight directions, east and so forth, from that [<s>Meru</s>]: <s>Mandara</s>, <s>Merumandara</s>,
<s>Supārśva</s>, and <s>Kumuda</s> — the buttress-mountains, in order. (PS 1.11.59)
They are three thousand [<s>yojanas</s>] in width, ten thousand in height;
mango, rose-apple (<s>jambu</s>), <s>kadamba</s>, and banyan trees are on them. (PS 1.11.60)
They are eleven hundred [<s>yojanas</s>] in height, with fruits resembling elephants;
resembling gold and jewels, with a hundred branches, covered [with foliage]. (PS 1.11.61)
There, various flocks of birds, with fragrant flowers and canopies;
above them, on grounds of golden and jeweled <s>mandāra</s> [trees] — (PS 1.11.62)
<s>Nandana</s>, <s>Caitrarathaka</s>, and what is called <s>Vaibhrājaka</s> —
indescribable forests, called <s>Sarvatobhadra</s> (auspicious on all sides). (PS 1.11.63)

children.text: teṣu vai kāmikāḥ siddhāḥ caranti lalanānvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: In them, the <s>Siddhas</s> (accomplished beings), fulfilling desires, roam accompanied by women;

children.text: teṣu sañcaratāṃ saukhyam adhikaṃ na śramādayaḥ // PS_1,11.64 //
children.translated_text: for those who wander in them, there is great happiness, no fatigue and the like. (PS 1.11.64)
From the fallen fruits of these [trees], split open, with pure sweet sap,
from the flowing sap, four [rivers] arise in the four [directions]; (PS 1.11.65)
two hundred thousand [<s>yojanas</s>] in circumference and length — terrible with aging and foul smell;

children.text: nīlaḥ śvetaḥ śṛṅgavāṃśca meroruttarato nagāḥ // PS_1,11.66 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, and <s>Śṛṅgavān</s> — the mountains to the north of <s>Meru</s>. (PS 1.11.66)
Nine thousand <s>yojanas</s> in length and of the measure of the earth's surface,
the boundary mountains, all extending to the respective oceans. (PS 1.11.67)
Ten thousand in height, two thousand in breadth;
<s>Niṣadha</s>, <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, and <s>Himavān</s> — these are on the southern side. (PS 1.11.68)
Of the previously stated measurements, these boundary mountains are acknowledged;
in breadth, height, and length, equal to <s>Nīla</s> and the rest, in sequence. (PS 1.11.69)
Attended by various hosts of <s>Siddhas</s>, filled with all kinds of gems;
to the east of <s>Meru</s>, the mountain <s>Gandhamādana</s>; (PS 1.11.70)
to the west of <s>Meru</s>, the mountain called <s>Mālyavān</s>;
extending from <s>Nīla</s> to <s>Niṣadha</s> in length, the two mountains, worshipped by the gods. (PS 1.11.71)
Those two, equal to the former in measure, divine, adorned with all excellent trees;
in the four directions from <s>Meru</s>, nine thousand <s>yojanas</s> — (PS 1.11.72)
the extensive land is called the <s>Ilāvṛta</s> region, they say;
<s>Ramyaka</s>, <s>Hiraṇmaya</s>, and <s>Kuruvarṣa</s> and the like — the three — (PS 1.11.73)
the continents (<s>varṣas</s>), divided by <s>Nīla</s> and the other mountains, are lands of gold.
to the east of <s>Gandhamādana</s>, in the land of <s>Bhadrāśva</s> region; // PS_1,11.74 //
west of <s>Mālyavat</s>, the <s>Ketumāla</s> region is proclaimed;
<s>Hari</s>, <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>, and <s>Bhārata</s> regions are in due order, // PS_1,11.75 //
to the south, the lands divided by mountains beginning with <s>Niṣadha</s>, in sequence.
<s>Vaivasvata Manu</s>, the lord of <s>Ramyaka</s>, is the [deity] worshipped by mortals; // PS_1,11.76 //
<s>Aryamā</s>, the lord of the ancestors, who worships the <s>Kūrma</s> (Tortoise) [avatāra], is in <s>Hiraṇmaya</s>;
<s>Bhūmi</s> (Earth), the wife of <s>Ādivarāha</s> (the Primordial Boar), goes to <s>Kuru</s> region; // PS_1,11.77 //
the worshipper of <s>Hayāsya</s> (Horse-faced [Viṣṇu]) is <s>Bhadraśravā</s> in the <s>Bhadrāśva</s> region;
the two [forms] worshipped by <s>Rati</s> and <s>Kāma</s>, named <s>Kṛti</s> and <s>Pradyumna</s>, // PS_1,11.78 //

children.text: ketumālye strījanārcyo na jīvaṃ bhadrake khalu /
children.translated_text: are worshipped by women in <s>Ketumālya</s>; but in <s>Bhadraka</s>, there is no <s>jīva</s> [worship];
<s>Narasiṃha</s>, worshipped by <s>Prahlāda</s>, goes to <s>Hari</s> region; // PS_1,11.79 //
<s>Rāma</s>, worshipped by <s>Hanumān</s>, is the lord of <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>;
south of <s>Bhadrāśva</s>, the region called <s>Bhārata</s>, rich in virtues — // PS_1,11.80 //
the presiding deity of men, <s>Śeṣa's</s> portion, the younger brother of this <s>Bhārata</s>;
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and <s>Nara</s>, born from <s>Mūrti</s>, the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>, arisen from <s>Dharma</s> — // PS_1,11.81 //

children.text: tau nāradasya ca ṛṣeḥ jñānadau lokapūjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: those two, the bestowers of knowledge to the sage <s>Nārada</s>, worshipped by the world.
In <s>Ilāvṛta</s>, on the eastern side of <s>Meru</s>, to the left and right, // PS_1,11.82 //
<s>Jaṭhara</s> and <s>Devakūṭa</s> [mountains stand]; and on <s>Meru's</s> crest, to the east,
touching <s>Gandhamādana</s>, made of gold and jewels, equal [in size], // PS_1,11.83 //
two thousand <s>yojanas</s> in breadth and height;
in the midst of the nine-thousand-[yojana] good land, between <s>Jaṭhara</s> and <s>Nīla</s>, // PS_1,11.84 //
the land between <s>Bhū-Devakūṭa</s> and <s>Niṣadha</s> is regarded as of the same extent;
six thousand [yojanas] apart in land, <s>Gandhamādana</s> and <s>Mandara</s> [mountains]; // PS_1,11.85 //
transversely, twice that extent is the land of the two mountain ranges east of <s>Meru</s>;
<s>Kailāsa</s> and <s>Karavīra</s> — two, likewise to the south of <s>Meru</s>; // PS_1,11.86 //
<s>Pavana</s> and <s>Pariyātra</s> — two, to the west of <s>Meru</s>;
<s>Śṛṅga</s> and <s>Makara</s>, to the north of <s>Meru</s> likewise; // PS_1,11.87 //
the southern and northern ends of <s>Niṣadha</s>, equal to <s>Nīla</s>;
the western ones, equal to the eastern mountains, [emanated] from <s>Mālyavat</s>. // PS_1,11.88 //
By these [mountains], the entire <s>Ilāvṛta</s> region is enclosed and divided, pure;

children.text: sukumāraṃ vanaṃ ramyaṃ sarvatryaiṇyaiva teṣvalam // PS_1,11.89 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Sukumāra</s> grove is delightful — in all of them there are only three [types of beings]. // PS_1,11.89 //
In those [regions], eight women [deities] are stationed on [Meru's] ridges, facing the directions;
in six hundred forms, from <s>Ādiśeṣa</s>, the thousand-faced lord, // PS_1,11.90 //
the great <s>Rudra</s> of this one dwells, and <s>Sāmba</s>, himself of eight bodies;

children.text: sadopāsta iti śeṣaṃ tadgaṃ saṅkarṣaṇaṃ param // PS_1,11.91 //
children.translated_text: he always worships — the remainder being that <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, the supreme, who goes to that [abode]. // PS_1,11.91 //
Again, <s>Śambhu</s> of eight bodies, <s>Bhava</s>, with <s>Bhavānī</s>, [adorned] with ashes;
in those very eight abodes, <s>Śaṅkara</s> always delights with his consort; // PS_1,11.92 //

children.text: prārabdhakarmaṇā sāpi patiṃ ramayati sphuṭam // PS_1,11.93 //
children.translated_text: she too, by the force of <s>prārabdha karma</s> (commenced karma), clearly delights her husband. // PS_1,11.93 //
Thus, in the <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, the eleventh chapter of the first section.
The Blessed Lord said:
From the opening in the shell of the cosmic egg, split by the toenail of <s>Trivikrama</s> (Viṣṇu's cosmic stride),
the external water that entered within, from the summit of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> downward, // PS_1,12.1 //
falling into <s>Brahmā's</s> water-pot, the Creator held it at the Lord's lotus-feet;
washing [those feet], from the remaining water, he made the river named <s>Gaṅgā</s>. // PS_1,12.2 //
She is called <s>Araṇā</s> and <s>Anaghanāmnī</s> (the Sinless-named); in the portions of <s>Bhū</s> and <s>Durgā</s>, [she is] twofold;

children.text: pṛthak saptāvarṇagā parighā rūpiṇī matā // PS_1,12.3 //
children.translated_text: going through each of the seven continents, she is regarded as having encircling forms. // PS_1,12.3 //

children.text: nandinī satyaloke sā nalinī ca tapomaye /
children.translated_text: In <s>Satyaloka</s> she is <s>Nandinī</s>, in [the world] made of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) she is <s>Nalinī</s>,

children.text: janoloke mālinīti maharloke tu bhoginī // PS_1,12.4 //
children.translated_text: in <s>Janaloka</s> she is <s>Mālinī</s>, and in <s>Maharloka</s> she is <s>Bhoginī</s>; // PS_1,12.4 //
she is <s>Svardhunī</s> in <s>Svargaloka</s> (heaven), <s>Viyadgaṅgā</s> (Celestial Gaṅgā) in <s>Dhruva's</s> abode,
<s>Madāpagā</s> in the atmosphere; above <s>Brahmā's</s> seat on <s>Meru</s>, // PS_1,12.5 //

children.text: nipatantī ca pūrvādi caturdikṣu krameṇa sā /
children.translated_text: falling in the four directions — east and the others — in order, she [becomes]
<s>Sītā</s>, <s>Alakānandā</s>, <s>Cakṣus</s>, and the auspicious one called <s>Bhadrā</s>. // PS_1,12.6 //
The one called <s>Sītā</s>, from the force of the water's momentum, from outside <s>Ilāvṛta</s> everywhere,
being cast down by <s>Hari</s>, will first go to the eastern ocean. // PS_1,12.7 //
That same [river], in the southern portion, in the course of great time,
being worshipped by <s>Bhagīratha</s> for the purification of <s>Sagara's</s> sons, // PS_1,12.8 //
is called <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, the sole purifier of all the worlds;

children.text: jahnunā rājaḥṛṣiṇā pītātyaktā ca vākyataḥ // PS_1,12.9 //
children.translated_text: drunk and then released by the royal sage <s>Jahnu</s> at his word, // PS_1,12.9 //
she [became] <s>Jāhnavī</s>; from the ground at the north of <s>Meru</s> mountain,
through the path, she is situated in the seven worlds below. // PS_1,12.10 //
That same goddess, flowing by three paths, shines, having <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as her support;
she [flows] through <s>Ramyaka</s> and the preceding, <s>Harivarṣa</s> and two other, // PS_1,12.11 //
<s>Bhadrāśva</s> and <s>Ketumāla</s>, flowing, beloved of the ocean.

children.text: bhāratesmin mahāvarṣe nadyaḥ santi sahasraśaḥ // PS_1,12.12 //
children.translated_text: In this great region of <s>Bhārata</s>, rivers exist by the thousands. // PS_1,12.12 //
<s>Śrīraṅga</s>, the one called <s>Veṅkaṭeśa</s>, <s>Totādri</s>, the one called <s>Puṣkara</s>,
<s>Śrīmuṣṇa</s>, <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s>, <s>Gaṇḍakī</s>, and the site of <s>Badarī</s> — // PS_1,12.13 //
these eight are the self-manifest [shrines] in <s>Bhārata</s>, bestowing all <s>siddhis</s> (perfections);
beginning with <s>Svāmipuṣkariṇī</s>, sacred tanks exist by the thousands. // PS_1,12.14 //
<s>Manus</s>, ancestors, <s>Siddhas</s>, all devoted to their spiritual practices,
gods and <s>Asuras</s> in this <s>Bhārata</s>, devoted to their own spiritual pursuits — // PS_1,12.15 //
here, by good <s>karma</s> one attains <s>svarga</s> (heaven), by sinful <s>karma</s> one attains hell,

children.text: miththā jñānena ca tamo jñānenaiva padaṃ hareḥ // PS_1,12.16 //
children.translated_text: by false knowledge one [reaches] darkness, and by knowledge alone the abode of <s>Hari</s>. // PS_1,12.16 //
A person here attains — and the <s>tātvika</s> deities, stationed in their abodes,

children.text: kecit sarvāvatāreṣu bhūmau bhūtvā bhavantyalam // PS_1,12.17 //
children.translated_text: some, in all <s>avatāras</s> (incarnations), having been born on earth, exist [here]. // PS_1,12.17 //
All the gods, stationed in their abodes, during the <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> <s>avatāras</s>,
having been born on earth and having worshipped the Lord, again with their original forms, // PS_1,12.18 //

children.text: ekī bhavantyapi surāḥ bhāvinaḥ prāyaśotra tu /
children.translated_text: the gods become unified [with their originals]; future ones also, mostly here,
devoted solely to their own spiritual practice — <s>Devadāsa</s> and others too. // PS_1,12.19 //
Both portioned and portionless ones, each devoted to their respective spiritual practice;

children.text: vidhayaśca niṣedhādyāḥ atratyānāṃ bhavanti hi // PS_1,12.20 //
children.translated_text: injunctions, prohibitions, and the like apply to those situated here. // PS_1,12.20 //
Encircled by a salt ocean one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> wide,

children.text: dvīpoyaṃ jambvākhyo hi merustasyaiva madhyamaḥ // PS_1,12.21 //
children.translated_text: this continent, named <s>Jambu</s> (Rose-apple) — <s>Meru</s> is at its very center. // PS_1,12.21 //
Above <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>Ilāvṛta</s>, its grove is auspicious,
called <s>Sukumāra</s> — due to <s>Rudra's</s> curse, any man who enters there // PS_1,12.22 //
becomes a woman; <s>Pārvatī</s>, desiring seclusion, caused this.
Twice the size of this is <s>Plakṣa</s> (Fig-tree) [continent], encircled by the sugarcane-juice ocean; // PS_1,12.23 //
there are great mountains there, corresponding to <s>Śrī Hari's</s> [forms];
those, from the milk-ocean onward, touching the sugarcane-ocean; // PS_1,12.24 //
in <s>Bhārata</s> and the other eight regions, the six other continents too,
being of middling desire-prompted merits, are created by <s>Hari</s> for enjoyment. // PS_1,12.25 //
By sin, there is no birth there; only by desire-prompted merit;

children.text: na tatra cāyurnayamo yāvatpuṇyantu jīvanam // PS_1,12.26 //
children.translated_text: and there, there is no fixed lifespan — as long as the merit, so long is life. // PS_1,12.26 //
There are men, women, of beautiful limbs, giving objects fit for enjoyment;
and trees of meritorious jewels, and houses of golden ground; // PS_1,12.27 //

children.text: vinaiva kālamaraṇaṃ tatra duḥkhādikaṃ na hi /
children.translated_text: there is no death without [due] time there, nor suffering and the like;
by mere wish, the accomplishment of all objects — created by the Lord. // PS_1,12.28 //
The wise worship <s>Hari</s> there in his solar form;

children.text: tato hi dviguṇodvīpaḥ śālmalaḥ sarvavartulaḥ // PS_1,12.29 //
children.translated_text: thence, twice the size, is the <s>Śālmala</s> (Silk-cotton) continent, entirely circular, // PS_1,12.29 //
four hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> [in extent], encircled by the honey-ocean;

children.text: jāmbavaṃ puṣkaraṃ tyaktvā madhyadvīpeṣu pañcasu // PS_1,12.30 //
children.translated_text: excluding <s>Jāmbava</s> (Jambu) and <s>Puṣkara</s>, in the five middle continents, // PS_1,12.30 //
in all there are seven rivers and seven mountains proclaimed;
the rivers in the seven continents flow into their respective outer oceans. // PS_1,12.31 //
All are useful for enjoyment, teeming with objects and people;
the mountains there touch the eastern and northern oceans. // PS_1,12.32 //
Divided by them into seven regions, each sheltering its respective <s>Manu's</s> lineage;

children.text: candrāntaryāmiṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ śālmalasthā bhajanti hi // PS_1,12.33 //
children.translated_text: those dwelling in <s>Śālmala</s> worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> as the inner controller of the Moon. // PS_1,12.33 //
The <s>Krauñca</s> (Heron) continent is twice the size [of the previous], in an ocean of sixteen hundred thousand [yojanas];
encircled by clarified-water, abounding in gems like <s>Sūryakānta</s>. // PS_1,12.34 //

children.text: varuṇāntargataṃ viṣṇuṃ bhajanti hi tatotra hi /
children.translated_text: They worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> as dwelling within <s>Varuṇa</s> there;

children.text: tato hi dviguṇāḥ śākadvīpaḥ kṣīrābdhiveṣṭhitaḥ // PS_1,12.35 //
children.translated_text: then, twice the size, is the <s>Śāka</s> (Teak) continent, encircled by the milk-ocean. // PS_1,12.35 //
Thirty-two hundred thousand [yojanas] in extent, it is declared [to have inhabitants] worshipping the Wind;
in the center of the <s>Śāka</s> continent, <s>Hari</s> himself in infinite forms, // PS_1,12.36 //
with a ground-body of half a <s>lakṣa</s> [yojanas], the Lord, seven <s>lakṣa</s> [yojanas] in height,
facing <s>Meru</s>, <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain, facing <s>Ananta</s>; // PS_1,12.37 //
of the form of a wheel-shaped rampart, always surrounding that continent,
stationed a <s>lakṣa</s> [yojanas] high — the Sun, the eye of the world, moves there. // PS_1,12.38 //
Circumambulating <s>Meru</s> to the right, by the velocity of the <s>Rūkṣa</s> (stellar) wheel,
once every day, the thousand-rayed one creates illumination. // PS_1,12.39 //
The northern end of the Sun's axle is wound like an oil-press;
the other end, furnished with a wheel, on <s>Mānasottara</s> mountain, // PS_1,12.40 //
they revolve — in the middle of those, on a raised [area] on the earth's surface,
at a height of forty <s>yojanas</s> from the middle, // PS_1,12.41 //
of equal measure, the connection with the axle is at equal intervals;

children.text: stambhāḥ ṣaṣṭhisahasrāśca catvāraḥ santi sadṛḍhāḥ // PS_1,12.42 //
children.translated_text: there are sixty thousand pillars, four [of which are] very sturdy, // PS_1,12.42 //
a hundred <s>yojanas</s> thick, made of blazing adamant, auspicious;
above that, on a platform a <s>lakṣa</s> [yojanas] high, illuminated by gems, // PS_1,12.43 //
in a blazing disc of ten thousand <s>yojanas</s>, the Sun is mighty;
the maker of day, accomplisher of all good endeavors, giver of fruits, [presided over by] <s>Yama</s>. // PS_1,12.44 //
Stationed east of <s>Meru</s>, he causes sunrise for those in <s>Bhārata</s>;
going south of <s>Meru</s>, the maker of midday, with seven <s>sandhis</s> (junctions); // PS_1,12.45 //
going west of <s>Meru</s>, the maker of sunset for those situated in <s>Bhārata</s>;
going north of <s>Meru</s>, the maker of midnight for men in <s>Bhārata</s>. // PS_1,12.46 //
In just this way, for the people existing in the four directions,
he is the activator of morning, midday, nightfall, and midnight. // PS_1,12.47 //
His own motion is enhanced by the special empowerment of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;
though one, by differentiation of names, by the will of <s>Śrī Hari</s>, // PS_1,12.48 //
the Sun who, in the seven continents, is the lord of the waters and the arms,
of those [stellar bodies] revolving leftward, moving at a height of three <s>lakṣa</s> [yojanas], // PS_1,12.49 //
laterally and upward, from a base of fifty-six <s>lakṣa</s> and more <s>koṭis</s>,
the <s>Rūkṣa</s> (stellar) wheel is constructed with long rods; // PS_1,12.50 //
a hundred <s>yojanas</s> wide, at the tips of the rods [the stellar bodies] shine;
the nine planets dwell and move along its path. // PS_1,12.51 //
Those rods are made of adamant, with one hundred and eight
openings and furnished with nooses controlled by <s>Dhruva</s> (Pole Star) and [made of the element of] <s>Varuṇa</s> (water); // PS_1,12.52 //
connected at their tips by a cord, each one allocated as the support of a [stellar body];
all rods, furnished with four openings — in them the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (water-element) // PS_1,12.53 //
nooses enter within; between a <s>lakṣa</s> [yojanas] above the earth,
situated [there], the tips of the Sun's chariot-axle are in front; the axle-ends too are in front; // PS_1,12.54 //
at the tips of the yoke and axle, [the chariot is] fitted with the end of a noose bound [to them];
the nooses of <s>Dhruva</s>, with the quarters of the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), counter-clockwise, // PS_1,12.55 //
once in a year cause the revolving [Sun] to revolve fully;
<s>Dhruva's</s> horses are seven, green-colored, of great speed. // PS_1,12.56 //
Those not mentioned are equal to the <s>tāttvika</s> (essential) ones; <s>Garuḍa</s>'s elder brother is their ultimate;
he, <s>Anūru</s>, is <s>Varuṇa</s>, who binds them well with serpent-nooses. // PS 1.12.57 //
On the <s>Mānasottara</s> mountain touching <s>Meru</s>, situated in the middle of the beautiful [region],
in a great pavilion adorned with diamond-studded mansions— // PS 1.12.58 //
the support of the moving sun's orbit, situated in the middle of the <s>Śāka</s> [continent],
<s>Hari</s>, seventy-seven and a half <s>lakṣa</s> (7,750,000) [<s>yojanas</s>] from <s>Meru</s>; // PS 1.12.59 //
at the same distance to the north of it, on the <s>Mānasottara</s> mountain,
a mighty wheel, elevated sixty thousand <s>yojanas</s>, // PS 1.12.60 //
with a central opening, made of diamond, revolves by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s [power];
having twelve spokes, six rims, and three <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) on the inner and outer surfaces— // PS 1.12.61 //
on the lines of the three [elements]: the yoke, the pole, and the axle, are the <s>tithis</s> (lunar days) and weekdays;
on the others, the months are stationed; the seasons reside in its rims. // PS 1.12.62 //
The four-month periods (<s>cāturmāsya</s>) are stationed in three rims; the two solstices divide [them];
the year resides in the entire wheel; the chariot has one wheel. // PS 1.12.63 //
Moving through <s>Karkaṭa</s> (Cancer) and the following [signs], the sun decreases [the days] by one each,
lengthening the nights by six [<s>nāḍīs</s>], causing the <s>dakṣiṇāyana</s> (southern course). // PS 1.12.64 //
Moving through <s>Nakra</s> (Capricorn) and the following six [signs], it causes decrease of the night;
increasing the days, alone it causes the <s>uttarāyaṇa</s> (northern course). // PS 1.12.65 //
By fifty <s>vināḍikās</s>, in each month to be increased—
the days during the northern [course], where it makes the nights half [shorter]. // PS 1.12.66 //
When the sun moves in <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) and <s>Tulā</s> (Libra), the day and night are equal;
and in the five [signs] beginning with <s>Vṛścika</s> (Scorpio), it makes the night half [longer]. // PS 1.12.67 //
Moving in the five [signs] beginning with <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus), it makes the daytime half [longer];
the twenty-eight <s>nakṣatra</s> (constellation) rods, elevated three <s>lakṣa</s> [<s>yojanas</s>], // PS 1.12.68 //
beginning from the northeastern corner, <s>Kṛttikā</s> and the others are situated;
constructed with seven times seven rods, obliquely and vertically, // PS 1.12.69 //
fitted with two diagonal lines at each corner,
the <s>nakṣatra-maṇḍala</s> (constellation circle) is three <s>lakṣa</s> [<s>yojanas</s>] above the earth. // PS 1.12.70 //

children.text: ekaikasyāṃ śalākāyāṃ chidrāṇi ca pṛthak pṛthak /
children.translated_text: In each rod, there are separate openings,

children.text: catvāri tāni daṃsrakṣādyādikāni vanāni ca // PS_1,12.71 //
children.translated_text: four [openings], beginning with <s>daṃśa</s> and <s>rakṣā</s>, and also the forests; // PS 1.12.71 //
those marked with <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), those marked with <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus), the human pairs—nine [each],
those of <s>Karkaṭa</s> (Cancer), <s>Siṃha</s> (Leo), <s>Kanyā</s> (Virgo), <s>Tulā</s> (Libra), and <s>Vṛścika</s> (Scorpio), // PS 1.12.72 //
those of <s>Dhanus</s> (Sagittarius), <s>Nakra</s> (Capricorn), <s>Kumbha</s> (Aquarius), and those marked with <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces)—nine [each];

children.text: teṣu teṣu praviṣṭāśca pādadyaṣṭottaraṃ śatam // PS_1,12.73 //
children.translated_text: having entered those respective [openings], one hundred and eight with their quarters. // PS 1.12.73 //
With its quarters, <s>Dhruva</s> (Pole Star), together with the sun, in counterclockwise direction,
will progressively grow in all the quarters of the <s>nakṣatras</s>. // PS 1.12.74 //
Within <s>Dhruva</s>, by <s>Hari</s>'s [power], three days of twenty <s>ghaṭikās</s> (time-units) each

children.text: ekaika nakṣatrapāde baddho bhavati vai kramāt // PS_1,12.75 //
children.translated_text: are bound sequentially in each quarter of a <s>nakṣatra</s>. // PS 1.12.75 //
The sun stays in one <s>nakṣatra</s> for thirteen and a half days;

children.text: māsena navapādāni bhuñjan dvādaśa rāśiṣu // PS_1,12.76 //
children.translated_text: enjoying nine quarters in a month, [it traverses] the twelve <s>rāśis</s> (zodiac signs). // PS 1.12.76 //
In a year, the sun moves counterclockwise;
the openings marked with <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) and others—<s>Meṣa</s> and the rest are called the <s>rāśis</s>. // PS 1.12.77 //
The sun travels at the tips of <s>Dhruva</s>'s cords, at a height of one <s>lakṣa</s> [<s>yojanas</s>];
the moon [travels] at the tips of <s>Dhruva</s>'s cords, at a height of two <s>lakṣa</s> [<s>yojanas</s>]. // PS 1.12.78 //
The moon and sun are considered situated below the <s>nakṣatra</s> circle;
<s>Kuja</s> (Mars) and the other five [planets] revolve above the <s>nakṣatra</s> circle. // PS 1.12.79 //
Always bound by <s>Dhruva</s>'s cords, they move counterclockwise;
<s>Budha</s> (Mercury) is at five <s>lakṣa</s> height; <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) at seven <s>lakṣa</s> height; // PS 1.12.80 //
<s>Śukra</s> (Venus) at nine <s>lakṣa</s> height; <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) at eleven <s>lakṣa</s>;
the orbit of the sun is proclaimed as thirteen [<s>lakṣa</s>]; // PS 1.12.81 //
above fifteen <s>lakṣa</s> is the orbit of <s>Śani</s> (Saturn);
above twenty-six <s>lakṣa</s>, the orbit of the <s>Saptarṣis</s> (Seven Sages/Ursa Major). // PS 1.12.82 //
At eleven <s>lakṣa</s> from that, <s>Dhruva</s> is stationed, dear to <s>Hari</s>;
he is stationed at the great wheel of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>Śiśumāra</s> (Dolphin constellation). // PS 1.12.83 //

children.text: dhruvādīn grahān viṣṇuḥ cakre sarvān suvāruṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> made all the planets beginning with <s>Dhruva</s>, with excellent <s>Varuṇa</s>-cords;
the glorious one conquers on both sides, connected to the openings of the rods. // PS 1.12.84 //
All these, in regions equal to the sun's [height], successively higher,
move by means of the cords stationed at the quarters of the <s>nakṣatras</s>, measured thereby. // PS 1.12.85 //
Through the movements of these through the <s>rāśis</s>, the Lord connects time;
the moon traverses the twelve <s>rāśis</s> in one month. // PS 1.12.86 //

children.text: kujo māsārdhato rāśiṃ bhuktvā rāśiṃ sameṣyati /
children.translated_text: <s>Kuja</s> (Mars), having enjoyed a <s>rāśi</s> in half a month, will approach [the next] <s>rāśi</s>;
<s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) in twelve months; <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) in thirty months. // PS 1.12.87 //
<s>Budha</s> (Mercury) and <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) each occupy a <s>rāśi</s> in one month;

children.text: sadā samagatī vakraśūnyau dvau śaśibhāskarau // PS_1,12.88 //
children.translated_text: always of equal motion and free from retrograde, [are] the two: the moon and the sun. // PS 1.12.88 //
The moon, when in the orbit of the sun, becomes invisible at new moon (<s>darśa</s>);

children.text: evaṃ kujādayaḥ pañca astaṃ yāsyanti bhānugāḥ // PS_1,12.89 //
children.translated_text: thus the five [planets] beginning with <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) also set when in the sun's [orbit]. // PS 1.12.89 //
<s>Śukra</s> (Venus) and <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), setting in the east, rise in the west;

children.text: pratyagastaṅgatau tau dvau tu pūrvadiśyuditau matau // PS_1,12.90 //
children.translated_text: those two, setting in the west, are considered to rise in the east. // PS 1.12.90 //
Likewise the others also—the sun has no setting by its own nature;

children.text: meruchāyāgataṃ cāstaṅgataṃ sūryaṃ vadanti hi // PS_1,12.91 //
children.translated_text: they say the sun enters the shadow of <s>Meru</s> and [thus appears to] set. // PS 1.12.91 //

children.text: candrārka kavyastamaye laukike tu śubhaṃ tyajet /
children.translated_text: At the mundane setting of the moon, sun, and <s>Kāvya</s> (Venus), one should abandon auspicious [activities];
<s>Śukra</s> (Venus), having set in the eastern direction, rises after two months. // PS 1.12.92 //
<s>Kāvya</s> (Venus), having set in the west, rises after seven days;
<s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) certainly rises on both sides after one month. // PS 1.12.93 //
The motions of <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) and the others—retrograde, first, stationary, direct, and swift—
are various and are indicators of inauspicious time. // PS 1.12.94 //

children.text: na samā hi gatisteṣāṃ kvacideva samāgatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Their motion is never uniform; only sometimes is it equal;
yoked to the city [of the sun] with a pair of yokes, each a <s>lakṣa</s> long, // PS 1.12.95 //
bearing the yoke at one-twelfth [of the circle], the seven horses of the sun,
around <s>Mānasottara</s>, nine <s>koṭi</s> (90 million) [<s>yojanas</s>] in extent, // PS 1.12.96 //
yoke [themselves] to complete the full circumambulation with great speed;

children.text: itthaṃ navagrahaiḥ kālacakraṃ paramaḥ pumān // PS_1,12.97 //
children.translated_text: thus through the nine planets, the Supreme Person [operates] the wheel of time. // PS 1.12.97 //

children.text: sūryasya gatyā meṣādīn māsān saureṇa mānataḥ /
children.translated_text: By the motion of the sun, [He determines] the months beginning with <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries), by the solar reckoning;
<s>Hari</s> also determines, by the motion of the moon, [the months] beginning with <s>Caitra</s>. // PS 1.12.98 //
They determine the lunar months; the <s>nakṣatra</s> [month] from the succession of constellations;

children.text: āvṛtyaṃ caturorāptiṃ cārān mānaṃ bṛhaspateḥ // PS_1,12.99 //
children.translated_text: the revolution of the four [planets] and their attainment [constitutes] the reckoning of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter). // PS 1.12.99 //
The <s>Sārasvata</s> and <s>Gāndharva</s> [reckonings]—a fortnight constitutes their day-and-night;
the learned call the <s>Sārasvata</s> and <s>Gāndharva</s> reckoning [thus]. // PS 1.12.100 //
A month constitutes a day-and-night in the <s>Maitra</s> reckoning, the wise know;
the divine reckoning [has] a year as its day-and-night period, of equal [duration]. // PS 1.12.101 //
The reckoning of <s>Manu</s> is called <s>Mānava</s>; the reckoning of <s>Brahmā</s> belongs to the unborn one;
<s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is the originator of the nine reckonings of time. // PS 1.12.102 //
From the middle region of the milk-ocean, thirty-two <s>lakṣa</s> [<s>yojanas</s>] in extent,
half that extent in height, in the form of a wall without ramparts— // PS 1.12.103 //
elevated ten <s>lakṣa</s> [<s>yojanas</s>] above the earth, <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (White Island) is of the nature of <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī);
the Vedic sounds, space, and time are eternally pervading, [yet] considered inert. // PS 1.12.104 //
Air, space, and solar light are non-eternal and considered inert;
they are unobstructed substances, and they are mutual supports. // PS 1.12.105 //
<s>Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa</s>, of pure conscious nature, with all-pervading forms,
and the obstructers of all [mundane] purposes—<s>Śvetadvīpa</s> and the other three— // PS 1.12.106 //
are worlds that are unobstructed, having world-forms with pillars and the like;
the <s>Durgā</s>-portion is above that; the <s>Bhū</s>-portion is above that; // PS 1.12.107 //
the <s>Śrī</s>-portion is above that; and the peak is above that;
in the three portions too, the earth-bulbs, elevated five <s>lakṣa</s>, ten thousand [<s>yojanas</s>]. // PS 1.12.108 //
In the three sub-portions also, <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī) has the form of the region's mansion;
the mansions, the regions, and the earth-portions have bulbs of one <s>lakṣa yojana</s>. // PS 1.12.109 //
Above, the three portions of coverings are equal to the earth-bulb;
in the three portions also, pillars of gem-studded ground surface [are present]. // PS 1.12.110 //
Measuring two and a half <s>lakṣa</s>, adorned with various gems,
the Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, of infinite radiance, is stationed on the altar in the middle of the <s>Śrī</s>-portion. // PS 1.12.111 //
Worshipped by infinite liberated souls of pure consciousness, He exists above heaven;
in the three [portions] is the station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s three steps, in the elevated place above the heavenly realm. // PS 1.12.112 //
<s>Śvetadvīpa</s> [measures] twenty-eight <s>lakṣa</s>; the <s>Durgā</s>-portion is of equal [measure];
the <s>Bhū</s>-portion is half of that; the <s>Śrī</s>-portion is half of that. // PS 1.12.113 //
Shining with ramparts of gem-and-gold radiating <s>sattva</s>, having self-portions,
adorned with many arched gateways, watchtowers, altars, and courtyards; // PS 1.12.114 //
filled with gem-studded rivers, mountains, lakes, and reservoirs;
radiant with golden lotuses [and] water, accompanied by various flocks of animals; // PS 1.12.115 //
rich with flowers of all seasons, with golden trees bearing sprouts,
filled with the sounds of swans, cuckoos, peacocks, parrots, and the like; // PS 1.12.116 //
teeming with exceedingly beautiful lions and various animals,
with many pavilions constructed of indescribable gems; // PS 1.12.117 //
endowed with groups of men and women possessing various sweet voices,
adorned with the singing of <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Cāraṇas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Apsarases</s>; // PS 1.12.118 //
resounding with various musical instruments, great <s>vīṇās</s>, conch-shells, and drums;
marked with elephants, horses, chariots, foot-soldiers, banners, and parasols; // PS 1.12.119 //
rich with all ornaments and garments, filled with rows of celestial vehicles;
furnished with various means of play, enhanced by various fragrances; // PS 1.12.120 //
covered with gem-studded couches [filled] with many swan-feather [cushions],
thronged with pleasure-women, [furnished] with gem fans and mirrors; // PS 1.12.121 //
adorned with many implements of gem-and-gold walls, vessels, and the like,
embellished with innumerable and infinite accessories of every kind; // PS 1.12.122 //
furnished with <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks), palanquins, swings, and footstools;
adorned with <s>tulasī</s> flowers, fine gems, and pearl garlands; // PS 1.12.123 //
blazing with the radiance of a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) suns, in the form of vessels and food-offerings,
in the form of ghee, curds, and water—she is of the nature of the previously described purposes. // PS 1.12.124 //
Surrounded by maid-servants and servants, in the form of a consort—the Goddess of all,
<s>Durgā</s>, <s>Bhū</s>, and <s>Śrī</s>, in their respective portions, of infinite and infinite forms; // PS 1.12.125 //
she always worships <s>Viṣṇu</s> of infinite form, the Lord, together with [His] consort;
by her very nature, there is no purpose to be attained by her. // PS 1.12.126 //
<s>Hari</s>, whose desires are fulfilled, out of love, the unborn one accepts her worship;
in the three stations also, that Goddess is of the nature of infinite stated purposes. // PS 1.12.127 //
<s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī) is present in all places, at all times, established in all forms. // PS 1.12.128 //
Thus ends the twelfth chapter of the first section of the glorious <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>.
The divine <s>Haṃsa</s> (Swan) said:
Those who have been described—gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, those born of <s>karma</s> and knowledge, and the non-<s>tāttvika</s> ones,
those who have ripened in qualification, having departed from the earth, [stationed] in <s>mahat</s> and the other [<s>tattvas</s>]— // PS 1.13.1 //
are stationed in their respective higher [regions] by the path declared by <s>Vipaśeṣa</s>;
established in their enjoyment-bodies, within the cosmic egg, on the surface of the second <s>Virajā</s>; // PS 1.13.2 //
having abandoned the subtle body, under the control of <s>turīya</s> (the fourth state), when the destruction of the cosmic egg approaches,
in the remaining time of one-eighth of <s>Parā</s>, they dwell within the womb of <s>Hari</s>; // PS 1.13.3 //
though liberated, they are not called 'liberated'; at the next creation of the cosmic egg,
having gone outside from <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s belly, with bodies of pure <s>sattva</s>— // PS 1.13.4 //
With the previously described infinite <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) objects fit for enjoyment, given by <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī),
elevated, situated in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island), [they behold] <s>Hari</s> directly.
Having seen [Him], having bowed, having pleased the Lord, and having obtained the state called liberation by His command,
with their desired paths unobstructed, in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, with purely <s>sāttvika</s>
bodies they rejoice in the portions of <s>Bhū</s> and <s>Durgā</s>, cherished by the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>;

children.text: cinmātradehaiḥ śrībhāge na cātra jaḍasaṃsthitāḥ // PS_1,13.7 //
children.translated_text: with bodies of pure consciousness alone in the <s>Śrī</s>-portion—and therein no inert matter exists.
Trees, birds, animals, oceans, rivers too—nine <s>koṭis</s> (ninety million)—

children.text: sarāṃsi nānāvidhabaddhā api lokeṣu vai hareḥ // PS_1,13.8 //
children.translated_text: lakes, of various kinds, even though bound in the worlds of <s>Hari</s>,
in the portions of <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Bhū</s>, and <s>Durgā</s>, they serve <s>Hari</s> directly,
for the accomplishment of their own superiority, desiring an increase of their own bliss.
They dwell in the portion of enjoyment solely through the subtle body;

children.text: (bhūbhāge saṃvasanti hi) niraṃśānāṃ sūkṣmadehāḥ aṇḍāntaḥsatyalokagā tu // PS_1,13.10 //
children.translated_text: (in the <s>Bhū</s>-portion they dwell) the subtle bodies of the portionless [beings] go to <s>Satyaloka</s> within the cosmic egg.
From <s>Aniruddha</s>, after a short interval of time, they come into existence;
before the destruction of the cosmic egg at dissolution, there is no destruction of the subtle body.
Beginning from grass, up to the pious mortals and <s>gandharvas</s>—all of them entirely—
the creation of their subtle bodies, in the previously described sequence, and their dissolution likewise.
Having created [them], among these very immortal <s>gandharvas</s> and others, the deities are fashioned;
situated in the <s>Durgā</s>-portion, from <s>Aniruddha</s>, they become endowed with subtle [bodies].
In the reverse of the order of creation, their destruction [occurs] by <s>Hari</s> through those stationed therein;
before the destruction of the cosmic egg itself, these become mere subtle-body-bearers.
Grass and other beings, and the non-<s>tāttvika</s> (non-essential) as well, dwell in the <s>Bhū</s>-portion;
for them, in the moat of the <s>Śrī</s>-portion, in the waters of the river <s>Virajā</s> belonging to <s>Śrī</s>—
before the destruction of the cosmic egg, those whose subtle bodies have been destroyed find refuge in the fourth state;
those who have reached the womb of <s>Śrī Hari</s>—that will be their abode.
Those ascending from the earth, having abandoned their bodies—the great ones,

children.text: tapaḥ satyeṣu durgākhyabhāge nīcoccakāḥ kramāt // PS_1,13.17 //
children.translated_text: in <s>Tapas</s> and <s>Satya</s> [worlds], in the portion called <s>Durgā</s>—the low and high in sequence—
dwell with bodies of enjoyment; but as for the portionless, through enjoyment

children.text: śīrṇā bhavanti hi aniruddhena ye cate // PS_1,13.18 //
children.translated_text: they become worn out; and those by <s>Aniruddha</s>—

children.text: praviṣṭāni bhavanti hi aniruddhena ye cate /
children.translated_text: they enter [into Him]; and those by <s>Aniruddha</s>,
having entered <s>Aniruddha</s>, are created by <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> for his victory.
Therefore those whose subtle bodies are liberated, the non-<s>tāttvika</s> beings, come into existence;

children.text: bhogedehaiḥ svottameṣu praviṣṭāḥ prabhavanti hi // PS_1,13.20 //
children.translated_text: having entered their superiors through bodies of enjoyment, they come into being.

children.text: gandharvāṇāṃ kuberantu pitṝṇāṃ yama eva hi /
children.translated_text: <s>Kubera</s> is [the destination] of the <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>Yama</s> of the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors);
the <s>gopīs</s>, in contact with the body of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, from all births, are seventy—
measured in number, those born and unborn, together with their wives, in the lord of wealth;
the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) equal to them are a hundred less than a hundred <s>koṭis</s>.
Equal to these are the hosts of <s>Agniputras</s> (sons of Fire);

children.text: vahnau karmajadevānāṃ layaḥ svāyambhuve mataḥ // PS_1,13.23 //
children.translated_text: the dissolution of the <s>karmaja</s> (karma-born) gods in Fire is considered [to occur] in the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [Manvantara].
Therein, eleven <s>Manus</s> are non-<s>tāttvika</s>;

children.text: tātvikau dvau saptamādyau yau tau manupadeśvarau // PS_1,13.24 //
children.translated_text: two are <s>tāttvika</s>—the seventh and the one beginning [from him]—those two are lords of the <s>Manu</s>-lineage.
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is <s>Viṣṇu</s> Himself; the <s>Tāpasa Manu</s> is declared;

children.text: vinā tān strīn manūn svāyambhuve laya udīritaḥ // PS_1,13.25 //
children.translated_text: the dissolution of the <s>Manus</s> without those women is declared in the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [cycle].
The first <s>Indra</s> is <s>Hari Yajña</s>; then <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s> in order;
the sixth is named <s>Mandradyumna</s>; the seventh is <s>Purandara</s>.

children.text: dvau śacīramaṇāṃśau tau ṣaḍaite tātvikāḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Two of these are portions of the husband of <s>Śacī</s>; these six are remembered as <s>tāttvika</s>;
the future <s>Indras</s> are <s>karmaja</s> (karma-born), non-<s>tāttvika</s>; their dissolution [occurs] in the first <s>Manu</s> [cycle].

children.text: saptakānāṃ ṛṣīṇāntu śatasya ca layaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The dissolution of the groups of seven <s>ṛṣis</s>, and of the hundred, is remembered

children.text: dakṣe dharme ca tattulyapitṝṇāṃ saptakasya tu // PS_1,13.28 //
children.translated_text: [to occur] in <s>Dakṣa</s> and <s>Dharma</s>; likewise for the seven <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors) equal to them.
Equal to them are eight <s>gandharvas</s>; eight less than a hundred <s>apsarases</s>—
<s>Urvaśī</s> and others, equal to them—they enter <s>Kubera</s>.
Therefore the portionless, [through the yoga of] ascent—the yogins and their superiors—
the non-<s>tāttvika</s>, ascending from the earth-world, go to <s>Mahar</s> and other [worlds],
consumed by their superiors through bodies of enjoyment, they come into being.
The yogins, ascending in reverse order, singing, proclaimed them.
The eternally transmigrating [souls], on earth, having abandoned the gross [body], through the subtle—
entering <s>Dharma</s> [world] and abandoning beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance)—they come to be.
Some are liberated right here; some on the summit of <s>Meru</s>;

children.text: vaiśvānare dyunadyāṃ vā sūrye vā deha eva vā // PS_1,13.33 //
children.translated_text: in <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (the cosmic fire), in the heavenly river, in the Sun, or in the body itself—
having abandoned <s>avidyā</s>, at the time of the mixed fruition, at dissolution, they go to the navel of <s>Hari</s>;
in heaven, earth, and other [realms], at creation, they wander by the will of <s>Śrī Hari</s>.
At dissolution, the unfit—by the fire of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> within the cosmic waters—
in <s>Pātāla</s> (the netherworld), in eternal hell, their subtle bodies broken—
by the blow of <s>Vāyu</s>'s mace, their subtle bodies shattered, following darkness—

children.text: laye sṛṣṭau tamasyandhe patanti śrī harīcchayā // PS_1,13.36 //
children.translated_text: at dissolution and creation, they fall into blind darkness, by the will of <s>Śrī Hari</s>.
The presiding deities of the categories, both inside and outside the cosmic egg—
without ascending, [they go] to their own superiors, by the path of <s>Vipas</s> (Sarasvatī) and others.
Having abandoned their bodies, they dwell in <s>Satyaloka</s> with subtle bodies;

children.text: naṣṭe satye brahmadehe naṣṭe taiḥ saha padmajāḥ // PS_1,13.38 //
children.translated_text: when <s>Satya</s> [world] is destroyed and <s>Brahmā</s>'s body is destroyed, together with them, the lotus-born ones—
when the destruction of the cosmic egg approaches, they attain a special state together with them;
those situated here with subtle bodies, together with all the subtle [beings] in all categories—
they become unified—thus even the twenty-one groups of categories

children.text: vyutkrameṇa tu bhūmyādi tatvopādāna sañcaye // PS_1,13.40 //
children.translated_text: in reverse order, the categories beginning from earth, in the collection of material causes—
on the ground, when subject to the presiding deities, by <s>Viṣṇu</s>—
by the gods named <s>Anna</s> and others, from that upward in ascending order—
the coverings are abandoned; they go to destruction in the previously stated measure,
in the previously stated sequence, progressively from <s>Aniruddha</s> and others.

children.text:
saṅkarṣaṇādvinaṣṭe(ṣu) tu sūkṣmadeheṣu kṛtsnaśaḥ /
tadā satvārdha śrībhāgasthalakṣmyālakṣmyātmake jale// 43 //
children.translated_text: When the subtle bodies are completely destroyed from <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>—then, the half of <s>sattva</s>, the <s>Śrī</s>-portion-ground, in the waters consisting of <s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Alakṣmī</s>—
(meaning: in the principal river <s>Virajā</s>)
in the order of the lowest, those whose subtle bodies are destroyed enter the belly of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: punaraṇḍe samutpanne śvetadvīpe samāpya ca // PS_1,13.44 //
children.translated_text: When the cosmic egg arises again, and having completed [their stay] in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>,
that world, situated in the middle of the <s>Kṣīrasāgara</s> (Milk Ocean), becomes liberated.
Created by <s>Lakṣmī</s>, measured as sixty-four, the island called <s>Puṣkara</s>,
surrounding the Milk Ocean, shining with gems and diamonds—
around the middle region thereof, circular, is <s>Mānasottara</s> [mountain],
a great mountain, uplifted, two thousand [yojanas] in extent,

children.text: dhṛḍho vajramayaḥ saptarathacakraṃ raveḥ sthitam // PS_1,13.47 //
children.translated_text: firm, made of diamond—the seven chariot-wheels of the Sun are situated upon it.
Inside it is the mortal world of transmigration; outside it is the domain of the immortals;
surrounded by a pure-watered ocean, equal to the island in extent.
Around that too, an auspicious golden land with a diamond coating;
a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) less four <s>lakṣas</s> (hundred thousand) in extent—a mountain therein,
called <s>Lokāloka</s>, circular in form, a mountain on all sides,
made of gems and gold, in the shape of a rampart, pure and great.
It is fifty thousand [yojanas]; its breadth is fifty <s>lakṣas</s>;
equally tall—rising from that, half a <s>lakṣa</s> higher in elevation.
Where it shelters various trees, the previously described world shines;
in the eight directions, its peaks have openings.
A hundred [yojanas] high; the groups of directional elephants are stationed upon them;
surrounding those openings, they support [the world] with the staffs of their trunks.
At the end of the mountain range, situated in the atmosphere, endowed with <s>Hari</s>'s presence, auspicious—

children.text: te ca pūrvādyaṣṭadikṣu garbhodasthāgataṃ(tā) bhuvam // PS_1,13.54 //
children.translated_text: they, in the eight directions beginning from the east, having come from the cosmic waters, [support] the earth—
upward, with their own hands adorned with ornaments, they bear [it] by the will of <s>Śrī Hari</s>.

children.text: te mānasottare merau svarge rūpāntarasthitāḥ // PS_1,13.55 //
children.translated_text: They [also exist] on <s>Mānasottara</s>, on <s>Meru</s>, in heaven—stationed in different forms—

children.text: kurvanti śrī harerājñāṃ dikpālānāṃ ca vāhanāḥ /
children.translated_text: they carry out the command of <s>Śrī Hari</s>; they are also the vehicles of the directional guardians.
The <s>Bhagavān</s>, in infinite forms, above that mountain, ascending upward—
<s>Hari</s>, whose <s>Ananta</s> (infinite) head touches the peaks above and below—
in the space between <s>Lokāloka</s> [mountains], the radiances of the Sun, Moon, trees, and planets—
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Atri</s>, and others declare that the golden land extends to infinity;
as in the previous islands, so between sunrise and [sunset]—
likewise on the mountain peaks, <s>Maitreya</s> and others,
having passed beyond the golden land, declare the supreme mountain to be situated [there].
<s>Paiṅgya</s> and others affirm this; <s>Mṛkuṇḍaja</s> (Mārkaṇḍeya) says otherwise.
The region between <s>Meru</s> and <s>Lokāloka</s> is three <s>koṭis</s> (thirty million)
<s>yojanas</s> plus one <s>koṭi</s>, it is declared as its measure;
together with the land of <s>Lokāloka</s>, the measurement [is stated].
Blind darkness surrounds that mountain—seven <s>koṭis</s> [yojanas];
where those endowed with false knowledge fall, in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s>.
Those who are enemies of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Ramā</s>, the guru of the <s>asuras</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the Vaiṣṇavas;
those who causlessly revile virtuous women, the <s>Vedas</s>, and the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures);
those devoid of even a trace of devotion, those who have abandoned obligatory and occasional rituals;
those devoid of even a trace of fear in committing infinite sins—
[those who hold:] non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> [from Brahman], attributelessness [of Brahman], incomplete qualities [of Brahman],

children.text: sāmyādhikye tadanyeṣāṃ bhedastadgata eva ca // PS_1,13.64 //
children.translated_text: equality or superiority of others [to Viṣṇu], or difference located in Him alone—
the distortion of His manifestations, hatred of His devotees,

children.text: tatpramāṇasya nindā ca dveṣā etekhilā matāḥ // PS_1,13.65 //
children.translated_text: and censure of His <s>pramāṇas</s> (authoritative sources)—all these are considered hatreds.
Having obtained birth in <s>Bhārata</s> (India), through the ripening of hatred toward <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the like,
according to their fitness, through perversion, those who hate the remote guru—
through the ripening of essential hatred, having cast off their own accumulated [merit],

children.text: bhuktvā duṣprārabdhaphalaṃ pūrṇaṃ pramādikā gatam // PS_1,13.67 //
children.translated_text: having experienced the full fruit of evil <s>prārabdha</s> (commenced karma), completely by negligence—
the fruit of good <s>prārabdha</s>, diminished by hatred of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by <s>Hari</s>'s [will]—
having experienced the future [results], casting aside the future [good], through the ripening of hatred—
they desire the suffering that is due to them; [they abandon] their gross bodies through poison, fire,
weapons, and abandon [them]; through torments and the like, they [enter] the eternal [hell] called <s>Tāmiśra</s> (Gloom).
Before the destruction of the cosmic egg, having cast off their subtle bodies therein,
by the blow of <s>Vāyu</s>'s mace, the destruction of their subtle bodies will occur.
For a long time, in the thigh-region of <s>Śrī Hari</s>, the wicked experience allotted suffering;
when the cosmic egg arises again, they fall abundantly into blind darkness.
The lowest among mortals, the portionless, <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating demons)—slightly <s>tāmasic</s>;
among them, some have the appearance of <s>tattva</s>-gods, [but dwell] in the lower [realm].
They wander in heaven and other [realms], proud of their sinful deeds;
<s>daityas</s> (demons) and <s>rākṣasas</s>—those with portions, of many forms.
From <s>Aniruddha</s> stationed in <s>Rasātala</s> (the nether region), having first resorted to the subtle body,
subject to their <s>karma</s>, having obtained gross bodies, together with the great <s>asuras</s>—

children.text: svayaṃ naṣṭā parān sādhūn nāśayanti kusādhanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: they themselves destroyed, they destroy others, the virtuous, through evil means;
situated in the ground of blind darkness, at a depth of a <s>lakṣa</s> (hundred thousand) below—
they experience the suffering due to them, in pure <s>tāmasic</s> bodies;
with pus, blood, urine, excrement, and the like; with heated oil, weapons, and blades;
experiencing unseen, unheard-of suffering, with instruments appropriate to [their] practice;
fashioned by <s>Durgā</s>, terrible, with thunderbolts and the like, manifoldly.
Together with [<s>Durgā</s>] in forms of lions, tigers, and the like, possessing such a true form,
<s>Vāyu</s> will deliver an indescribable flood of suffering upon them.
They say that suffering is destined to be obtained; below that too, the appointed suffering —
they experience, situated in their own true form, all diseases, wounds, and the like.
All cuts and similar [afflictions], always — they undergo complete suffering.

children.text: tato dvisaptakoṭibhyāṃ(kyāṃ) ghanodaḥ paritaḥ sthitam // PS_1,13.80 //
children.translated_text: Then, at the distance of two times seven <s>koṭis</s> (140 million yojanas), the dense waters (<s>ghanodaka</s>) are situated all around,
where <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, of infinite body-form, with <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) of that very nature,

children.text: sadā viharati śrīśo brahmādyairapi sevitaḥ // PS_1,13.81 //
children.translated_text: the Lord of <s>Śrī</s> always sports, served by <s>Brahmā</s> and others.
Above that, measured by half a <s>koṭi</s>, is the throne of <s>Ananta</s>, the Lord's —
touching the shell of the cosmic egg, with a platform twenty <s>lakṣas</s> (2 million yojanas) high,
the earth-portion is proclaimed as measuring forty <s>lakṣas</s> (4 million yojanas);
the <s>Śrī</s>-portion, thirty <s>lakṣas</s> (3 million yojanas) high, auspicious in every way.
Beyond that, multiplied by infinite qualities, it is remembered as equal to <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>.
Thus, in the glorious <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, in the first section, the thirteenth chapter.
The glorious <s>Haṃsa</s> said:
Below the earth: <s>Atala</s>, <s>Vitala</s>, then <s>Sutala</s>,
each ten thousand [yojanas] in depth and breadth — <s>Talātala</s> and <s>Mahātala</s>,
<s>Rasātala</s>, and <s>Pātāla</s> — these from north to south, each below the other.
The earth-spheres (<s>bhūkaṇḍas</s>) are two thousand [yojanas] extensive, resembling interiors filled with cavities.
Illuminated by the radiance of great jewels, devoid of the sun and other planets.
<s>Meru</s> is to the north of them; the path is universally accepted everywhere.
In all of them, the trees are equal to <s>Kalpa</s>-trees (wish-fulfilling trees);
the cows are like <s>Kāmadhenu</s> (wish-granting cow); the stones are like <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems).
For those dwelling there, according to their fitness, they yield fruits for the good and the bad alike;

children.text: yacchanti svacchasalilaṃ cāpi tattadgataṃ śubham // PS_1,14.5 //
children.translated_text: and the water there is clear, and the auspicious things belonging to each [realm].
There, happiness does not [come] from exertion; effortlessness is happiness-bringing.
Abundant with an infinite mass of objects fit for enjoyment and use.
As long as desired good [karma lasts], so long is the lifespan; for the wicked, below [this measure].

children.text: bhūmau bhāratagā ye ca kṛte lakṣāyuṣaḥ smṛtāḥ // PS_1,14.7 //
children.translated_text: Those born in <s>Bhārata</s> on earth, in the <s>Kṛta</s> (golden) age, are remembered as having lifespans of a <s>lakṣa</s> (100,000 years).
In the <s>Tretā</s> and the other three [ages], humans have lifespans diminished by a tenth each.
Mental affliction, physical disease, old age, increase, fatigue — and the names beginning with these —
due to the regulation of the age-lifespan, untimely deaths do not exist there at all.
For both the good and the bad dwelling there, without devotion or hatred in any case,

children.text: tathā vidhiniṣedhau ca na ca varṇāśramādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: there are likewise no injunctions and prohibitions, nor <s>varṇāśrama</s> (caste and life-stage) distinctions.
There is no action (<s>karma</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), or the like; all are consumers of past <s>karma</s>.
Mostly those with parts, born there — [but also] those born on earth, by the grace of <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and <s>Īśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
through boons — enemies of the gods, [slain] by the <s>avatāras</s> (incarnations) of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>,
those killed by them — again in their former abode, as long as their commenced desired [karma lasts],

children.text: śubhaṃ bhuñjanti niṣkāmyaśubhaṃ teṣāṃ na vai kvacit // PS_1,14.12 //
children.translated_text: they enjoy what is auspicious; there is never inauspicious desireless [karma] for them.
Those who go to hell due to desired sins; those free from desire, due to inauspicious [karma], take bodies;
desiring inner-moving <s>Daityas</s> — the partless ones [reborn] from what was earned in <s>Bhārata</s>.
Due to desired [karma], the spirits (<s>bhūtas</s>) who are refuges of the <s>Dānavas</s> (demons) dwell among them.

children.text: sadā śeṣādikastatra vasanti sati kāraṇe // PS_1,14.14 //
children.translated_text: Always <s>Śeṣa</s> and others dwell there when there is cause,

children.text: harīcchayā surāstatra vasantaḥ karmato na hi /
children.translated_text: by the will of <s>Hari</s>; gods dwell there, not by [their own] <s>karma</s> indeed.
These worlds are within the hundred thousand earth-spheres; below these,
in <s>Pātāla</s>, the hells are twenty-eight in number, created by <s>Hari</s>.
Below that, twenty-five <s>koṭis</s> [deep] — pure, free from impurity within the womb of waters,
minus one <s>lakṣa</s> — where the Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, in the form of the Lord of Waters (<s>Yāda</s>), shines.
Of the thousand-headed serpent (<s>Śeṣa</s>) — upon one head,
the entire universe becomes like a mustard-seed; of the Lord of <s>Vāruṇī</s>.
This entire earth, with its seven continents, together with oceans and mountain-ranges,
its support is the tortoise <s>Vāyu</s> (<s>Kūrma</s>); and that tortoise-formed one is <s>Hari</s>;
the power (<s>śakti</s>) in the form of the foundation, situated in the midst of the waters, supports him.
Of the nature of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> and <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, the destroyer, named <s>Ananta</s>.
Below that is the frog [form]; below that is the boar (<s>Varāha</s>);
touching the shell of the cosmic egg — they call [that] the foot at the bottom level.
Above them is <s>Bhūloka</s> (earth-world); in its middle is <s>Meru</s>, the mountain-support.
It has the form of the lotus-stalk (<s>bisa</s>) arisen from the navel of the lotus-naveled one (<s>Padmanābha</s>), of golden-navel radiance.
This stalk arising from the middle of <s>Meru</s>, above, is the abode of six lotuses.
A hundred <s>yojanas</s> in width, extending in length up to <s>Satyaloka</s>;
harder than diamond, the interior opening radiates with light.
A <s>lakṣa</s> (100,000 yojanas) elevated above the earth's surface — <s>Bhuvarloka</s> is supported by it.
Made of jewels and gold, with a <s>lakṣa</s> of earth-spheres, beautiful in the world,
adorned with seven ramparts, with various enjoyments, great yogins,
with insentient objects, with an abundance of <s>sattva-guṇa</s> qualities, with bright dwellings.
A <s>koṭi</s> (ten million yojanas) above the earth, <s>Svargaloka</s> (heaven-world), charming, very circular,
