a <s>koṭi</s> of <s>yojanas</s> in width, like <s>Bhuvarloka</s> itself.
Endowed with two <s>lakṣas</s> of earth-spheres, reached by the stalk of <s>Meru</s>,
radiant with seven high ramparts made of jewels and gold.
The beautiful streets are ten <s>yojanas</s> wide, four-sided,
where there are many banners, and [streets] abounding in numerous mirrors.
With jeweled beds, seats, infinite <s>sāttvic</s> means of practice,
adorned with palaces adorned with gold of previous merit.
Radiant with various gardens and eight abodes of the eight directional guardians;
in the middle, a great pavilion of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s temple, shining with hosts of gems.
Filled with all weapons, chariots, <s>cintāmaṇi</s> gems, and the like;
endowed with strings of pearls and gems, with all kinds of ornaments.
Abundant with divine garments, food-gifts, numerous <s>pārijāta</s> trees, and the like;
with twenty-eight city-gates, arched doorways, watchtowers, and gate-towers.
a jeweled <s>Mandākinī</s> [river], of a form equal to a <s>kalpa</s>-tree, with lotus abodes.
Surrounded by ten thousand palaces, with rivers flowing by the doors of many houses;
There, in the form of a moat, it shines, accompanied by hosts of aquatic creatures;
with excellent sound, touch, and form; well-flavored and fragrant.
Enjoyable by mortals, gods, and <s>asuras</s>, filled with various separate objects.
<s>Bhuvarloka</s> is the world below [<s>Svarga</s>], superior by a hundredfold in qualities.
From that, the worlds beginning with <s>Svarga</s> are progressively tenfold superior in qualities.
And likewise, the hosts of gods and celestial attendants situated in each respective world,
and for the authorized good mortals, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and other small-minded ones,
the fruit appropriate to each of them — the imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the support of all.
Then, one and a half <s>koṭis</s> above, is <s>Maharloka</s>, free from [ordinary] action.
Then, two <s>koṭis</s> above, is <s>Janaloka</s>, greatly honored.
Then, two and a half <s>koṭis</s> above, is <s>Tapoloka</s>, attainable by pure consciousness.
Then, one <s>koṭi</s> above, is <s>Satyaloka</s>, most radiant.
With three, four, five, and six <s>lakṣas</s> of earth-spheres — the domain of knowledge,
situated at the tip of the great stalk arisen from the navel — in <s>Satyaloka</s>,
the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s> was born, created by <s>Viṣṇu</s> as the creator of all worlds.
The special objects of <s>Svarloka</s> are extended in <s>Maharloka</s> and the others.
At the time of <s>Aja</s>'s (<s>Brahmā</s>'s) creation, many hosts of mortals find their abode [there].
Such is the cosmic structure — at midday on the last day of the half-lifespan of the age,
<s>Hari</s> creates in that place; the presiding deity of the material (<s>Prākṛta</s>) [world] —
the world of <s>Aja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) is regarded as thirteen <s>koṭis</s> above the earth.
Thus, in the glorious <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, in the first section, the fourteenth chapter.
The glorious <s>Haṃsa</s> [said]:
Twelve <s>koṭis</s> above <s>Satyaloka</s> is the world called <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>;
the <s>Durgā</s>-portion is the lower region; the earth-sphere is ten <s>lakṣas</s> [high].
Above that is the earth-portion; the <s>Śrī</s>-portion is above that.
Three earth-spheres are equal; the summit is measured as thirty <s>lakṣas</s> high.
In those three portions — many great palaces,

children.text: maṇyātmakāni vaidvyaṣṭasaṃkhyāni ca śubhāni ca // PS_1,15.3 //
children.translated_text: made of gems, in various groups of sixteen, auspicious.
In the middle, numerous coverings (<s>paryāvaraṇas</s>) made of diamond,

children.text: maharādīni catvāri hayajataṃ vistarāṇi ca // PS_1,15.4 //
children.translated_text: and the four [worlds] beginning with <s>Mahar</s>, each a hundred [yojanas] in extent —
regions — as in the three portions of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, so are the planes.
Touching the shell of <s>Aja</s>'s (<s>Brahmā</s>'s) cosmic egg, in the middle are seven ramparts,
endowed with gates in the east and other directions, seven-fold in each, made of gold,
with gates of <s>puṣkarāga</s> (topaz) color, with doors of rubies (<s>padmarāga</s>).
Radiant with great thresholds of sapphire (<s>indranīla</s>) and diamond slabs,
on the right and left, shining jeweled platforms, with elevated edges.
At each gate, magnificent assemblies with jeweled lotus-seats,
blazing with radiance of infinite suns, adorned as ornaments of the world.
In each of those three portions, <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) presides — of infinite <s>Ananta</s>-like forms,

children.text: vipeśānāṃ samastānāṃ brahmaṇā saha karhicit // PS_1,15.9 //
children.translated_text: together with all the special lords, along with <s>Brahmā</s>, at times
there is indeed a vision of the three portions of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and the rest.

children.text: na tatra saṃsthitisteṣāṃ maharādiṣu saṃsthitiḥ // PS_1,15.10 //
children.translated_text: There is no permanent residence for them there; their permanent residence is in <s>Maharloka</s> and the others.
Those from grass onward [reside] in <s>Maharloka</s>; those from humans onward, above that.
Kings [reside] in <s>Tapoloka</s>; in <s>Satyaloka</s>, the human singers.
For the liberated — whether [previously] bound or [already] freed — this is the abode here.
From human <s>Gandharvas</s> up to the naturally-born — the departed ones are established in <s>Tapas</s> [<s>loka</s>].
The <s>karmadevās</s>, having departed, dwell in <s>Satyaloka</s>.
The non-real (<s>atāttvika</s>), freed from the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), even those gone to the three stations —
in none of the three portions do they have residence within the ramparts.
Above that, the ramparts — situated outside the <s>Śrī</s>-portion,
of four <s>koṭis</s> in dimension; around it, in the form of a moat,
with twelve <s>koṭis</s>, endowed with watches (<s>yāmas</s>) — the outer rampart is declared.
Six ramparts are within it, with <s>koṭi</s>-intervals of space between.
Eight <s>koṭis</s> in dimension — above and outside that is the covering (<s>āvṛti</s>).
<s>Śrī</s> — measuring a <s>koṭi</s> of <s>yojanas</s> — the auspicious river called <s>Virajā</s>;
by the touch of whose waters, the <s>liṅga</s>-bound ones are immediately freed.
People there — <s>Hari</s>, always delighting in water-play, is attended [there].
The coverings above the earth-portion — the earth herself is of the nature of coverings.
In the middle of that, on the surface of the <s>Śrī</s>-portion, a <s>lakṣa</s> above —

children.text: virajā tatra dvau bhāgau muktāmuktāśrayau śubhau // PS_1,15.19 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Virajā</s> [river is] there; the two portions — auspicious abodes of the liberated and the unliberated.
Thus, the <s>Durgā</s>-portion, together with the surrounding coverings,

children.text: bhūbhāgadurgā bhāgau dvau madhyo bhūrunnatākṛti // PS_1,15.20 //
children.translated_text: the earth-portion and the <s>Durgā</s>-portion are two; the middle earth-portion has an elevated form.
Above those two, at the junction of the covering — two [rivers]
called <s>Araṇya</s>, rivers of the waters of <s>Durgā</s> and <s>Bhūmi</s>, dear to <s>Śrī Hari</s>.

children.text: na tatra liṅgabhaṅgādi hariṇā cintitaṃ kvacit /
children.translated_text: There, the breaking of the <s>liṅga</s> and the like was never designed by <s>Hari</s>.
Between <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and the supreme sky (<s>Paravyoman</s>) is the <s>Virajā</s> river.
Those two — <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> with their consorts — having bodies made of <s>Pradhāna</s>,
going above the earth-portion's covering, during dissolution, together with all the gods,
and without the gods, at the beginning and completion of the incarnations (<s>avatāras</s>),

children.text: kāle bhūbhāgordhvagatau syātāṃ kvāpi harīcchayā // PS_1,15.24 //
children.translated_text: in time, the two go above the earth-portion, sometimes by the will of <s>Hari</s>.
Therefore, the region above the earth-portion is proclaimed as <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter).

children.text: yadadhīnā yasya sattā tattadityeva bhaṇyate // PS_1,15.25 //
children.translated_text: That upon which the existence of anything depends — that alone is called [its name].
The <s>Śrī</s>-portion, mixed with such <s>Pradhāna</s>, is the supreme sky (<s>Paramāmbara</s>).
Therefore, the one who is supreme above the principal [gods] is called 'sky-dweller' (<s>vyomaga</s>). (PS 1.15.26)
For the <s>sāttvic</s> ones without parts, within the cosmic egg, there is immersion in that;

children.text: tātvikānāṃ tu sarveṣām aniruddhāvṛti sthite // PS_1,15.27 //
children.translated_text: but for all the <s>sāttvic</s> ones, stationed in <s>Aniruddha</s>'s covering — (PS 1.15.27)
in the impurity situated in the upper region, the <s>sattva</s>-covering —
the auspicious <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (White Island) and his own abode become unified at the end. (PS 1.15.28)

children.text: śrīdurgābhyāṃ ca bhūmyā ca ekībhūte vilakṣake /
children.translated_text: With <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Durgā</s> and <s>Bhūmi</s> (Earth) becoming unified, [each being] distinctive —

children.text: śrībhāge tatrage tasya parighā virajā nadī // PS_1,15.29 //
children.translated_text: in the <s>Śrī</s>-portion, reaching that, is the river <s>Virajā</s> as its boundary moat. (PS 1.15.29)

children.text: tajjale tu tataḥ snātvā liṅgabhaṅgaḥ pradṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Bathing in that water, the dissolution of the subtle body (<s>liṅgabhaṅga</s>) is seen;
during dissolution, for the virtuous ones who depart crossing the covering of the earth — (PS 1.15.30)
the covering of earth is said to be the first; the covering of <s>sattva</s> is the last;
above that, the unmanifest space (<s>avyākṛtākāśa</s>) is referred to by the word 'sky' (<s>vyoman</s>). (PS 1.15.31)
Between the final covering and the sky, is the <s>Virajā</s>; therefore,
among the gods who arise there, union with [divine] limbs (<s>aṅgasāyujya</s>) is acknowledged. (PS 1.15.32)
In the <s>Śrī</s>-portion of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, belonging to that <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the discus-bearer —
in his infinite form, complete limb-union (<s>sarvāṅgasāyujya</s>) is obtained by <s>Brahmā</s>. (PS 1.15.33)
And for the liberated one, an increase of the atomic [soul] by its own nature is not possible;
nor is there diminution, return, suffering, ignorance, fear, and the like. (PS 1.15.34)
For the lower and least of the liberated, fulfillment comes only from their own [measure of] bliss;
there is no desire for the bliss of the supreme; the fruit of service and meditation and the like [is this]. (PS 1.15.35)
Neither of <s>Hari</s> nor of another — the liberated enjoy their own bliss;

children.text: pralayatvaṃ kvacitsṛṣṭiḥ kāle śrībhāga eva hi // PS_1,15.36 //
children.translated_text: sometimes there is dissolution, sometimes creation — at the [proper] time, indeed in the <s>Śrī</s>-portion alone. (PS 1.15.36)
<s>Brahmā</s>, with a body of pure consciousness, is considered to be within the inner enclosure;
<s>Rudra</s> and the others are at the sixth [enclosure]; <s>Indra</s> and the others are stationed at the fifth. (PS 1.15.37)
<s>Sūrya</s> and the others are at the fourth; the <s>Marut</s>-hosts (storm gods) at the third;
stationed at the second enclosure are <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain god) and the other foremost gods. (PS 1.15.38)
With bodies of pure consciousness, in the <s>Śrī</s>-portion, in the first [enclosure], preceded by <s>karma</s>-[deities] —

children.text: ete muktāstu bhūbhāge durgābhāge tathaiva ca // PS_1,15.39 //
children.translated_text: these are the liberated ones; but in the <s>Bhū</s>-portion and in the <s>Durgā</s>-portion likewise, (PS 1.15.39)
with pure <s>sāttvic</s> bodies, having obtained the happiness of <s>Hari</s>;
of the host of eighty-four hundred thousand (8,400,000) souls — (PS 1.15.40)
the archetype-self (<s>bimbātman</s>), of that very form, always present there, protects;
all the liberated hosts of souls exist in the <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> palace. (PS 1.15.41)

children.text: jīvā(na)nāṃ pātya(pāyo)pi hariḥ sa hi rūpāntaraivibhuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> is also the protector of souls; he, the all-pervading one, exists in other forms;
with forms equal to [but slightly] smaller than all souls, and with gross [forms] of such nature — (PS 1.15.42)
worshipped by the liberated for infinite <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, present in the three portions;
endowed with such infinite forms, he moves about together with <s>Śrī</s>. (PS 1.15.43)
Those two there, of infinite forms and purposes fit for worship —
there, with essential crown and the like, with conch and discus and the like as instruments, (PS 1.15.44)
with the <s>Sudarśana</s> and other weapons, with offerings of sandal, garlands, and the like,
with food offerings, garments, beds, and the like — he is worshipped by his own forms. (PS 1.15.45)
Having attained unity with <s>Śrī</s> always, he delights in the form of joy (<s>moda</s>);
<s>Śrī</s>, the goddess of all forms, worships <s>Viṣṇu</s> with those [offerings] fully. (PS 1.15.46)
With those garland-remnants (<s>nirmālyas</s>) given by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Ramā</s> clearly becomes one [with them];
in the <s>Bhū</s> and <s>Durgā</s> portions likewise, with pure <s>sāttvic</s> means — (PS 1.15.47)
<s>Śrī</s>, who presides over those, having worshipped, with those remnants, <s>Aja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and the others —
the wise liberated ones she satisfies with auspicious fragrance, garlands, and the like. (PS 1.15.48)
They, with celestial chariots, swings, cradles, and special ornaments,
with beds, ornaments, garments, and the like, with elephants, horses, and the like sometimes, (PS 1.15.49)
with equal and excellent attendants, with fruits, flowers, rice-grains, and the like,
with their own beloved young women, with water-sports and the like — (PS 1.15.50)
going wherever they wish without obstruction, with worship, holy discourse, and the like,
free from return — all of them bow [to <s>Hari</s>]. (PS 1.15.51)
Nine <s>koṭis</s> (ninety million) of hosts of deities, the gods stationed in [their] positions,
all endowed with subtle body, subtle [body], and gross body, together with their wives — (PS 1.15.52)
for the sake of serving <s>Śrī Hari</s>, they dwell properly in the <s>Durgā</s>-portion;
they, with [objects] produced from wish-fulfilling cows (<s>kāmadhuk</s>), wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpavṛkṣa</s>), and wish-fulfilling gems (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>) — (PS 1.15.53)
with infinite objects fit for worship and use, with water bestowed by <s>Śrī</s>,
with the garland-remnants of <s>Hari</s> worshipped by her, again offered [to them] — (PS 1.15.54)
with limbs purified, they move about everywhere, rejoicing;

children.text: sāyujyamapi sālokyaṃ sāmīpyaṃ sarvadā hareḥ // PS_1,15.55 //
children.translated_text: <s>sāyujya</s> (union) and <s>sālokya</s> (same-world), <s>sāmīpya</s> (proximity) — always with <s>Hari</s> — (PS 1.15.55)
and <s>sārūpya</s> (same-form) — liberation is indeed declared to be fourfold;
<s>Viṣṇu</s> makes the liberated ones, situated in his own body, enjoy only their own [measure of] bliss. (PS 1.15.56)

children.text: karoti taddhi sāyujyaṃ tatsurāṇāṃ ca nīcagam /
children.translated_text: That indeed is <s>sāyujya</s>; and for the gods, it pertains to the lower ones;

children.text: sāmīpyādi trayaṃ karmadevānāṃ yujyate kvacit // PS_1,15.57 //
children.translated_text: the triad of <s>sāmīpya</s> and the rest is sometimes applicable to the <s>karma</s>-deities. (PS 1.15.57)
For the divine servants who are different from those, <s>sārūpya</s> and the second are acknowledged;
dwelling in the same world is called <s>sālokya</s> — for the remaining ones. (PS 1.15.58)
With pure <s>sāttvic</s> bodies, endowed with four arms,
bearing [the weapons of] the enemy-destroyer, wearing yellow garments — if <s>sārūpya</s> is declared — (PS 1.15.59)
<s>Jaya</s> and <s>Vijaya</s>, and <s>Bala</s> and <s>Prabala</s> likewise,

children.text: caṇḍaḥ pracaṇḍaśca tathā nandaścāpi sunandakaḥ // PS_1,15.60 //
children.translated_text: <s>Caṇḍa</s> and <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, and also <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Sunandaka</s>, (PS 1.15.60)
<s>Kumuda</s> and <s>Kumudākṣa</s>, and likewise <s>Bhadra</s> and <s>Subhadraka</s>,
named <s>Sudhāman</s> and <s>Dāman</s>, stationed under the command of <s>Viṣvaksena</s> — (PS 1.15.61)
all with four forms, in the four directions and at the seven —
beginning from the gate of the innermost enclosure — [they are] the gate-keepers. (PS 1.15.62)
<s>Nandinī</s>, [the river] arising from <s>Hari</s>'s feet, with auspicious water in the <s>Durgā</s>-portion;

children.text: parighā sa tu vaikuṇṭhaścaturasraḥ prakīrtitaḥ // PS_1,15.63 //
children.translated_text: and the moat — that <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> is proclaimed to be four-sided. (PS 1.15.63)
Of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, pervading the outer cosmic egg, the realm is called <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>;
<s>Ananta</s> (the infinite serpent) of <s>koṭi</s>-height heads, [on which <s>Viṣṇu</s> rests] — [<s>Ananta</s>] is thought of [as being] at the face and crown. (PS 1.15.64)
With feet touching the inner shell of the cosmic egg, within the embryonic water,
his couch is called the seat of <s>Ananta</s>; his hip is of the nature of the yellow garment. (PS 1.15.65)
The dense water is the hip-region; <s>Meru</s>, situated in the middle of his navel,
twenty-five <s>koṭi</s> <s>yojanas</s> from Mount <s>Meru</s> — (PS 1.15.66)
the shell of <s>Aja</s>'s (<s>Brahmā</s>'s) cosmic egg, in the directions, intermediate directions, above, and below, it is recalled;
with ten coverings beginning with earth, and ten more — (PS 1.15.67)
the upper coverings that remain beyond are given — all of them;
the lower [parts] are the feet; the sages call those the grounds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. (PS 1.15.68)
Like an image in stone, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s image, through <s>Aja</s>'s (<s>Brahmā</s>'s) and the others' identification,
[they identify] the cosmic egg and the worlds as the bodies of the gods, in sequence — these are the identifiers. (PS 1.15.69)
Thus, with <s>koṭis</s> of such cosmic eggs, with infinite self-forms,
moving about with space [between them], from the play-pores [of <s>Hari</s>] — (PS 1.15.70)
knowing especially that this universe is under <s>Hari</s>'s control,

children.text: virāḍrūpasya ca hareḥ satyalokaḥ śirasyalam // PS_1,15.71 //
children.translated_text: of <s>Hari</s>'s cosmic form (<s>virāṭ</s>), <s>Satyaloka</s> is at the head. (PS 1.15.71)
<s>Lokāloka</s> [mountain] of that <s>Hari</s> is contemplated at the waist-cord;
the yellow garment is the golden earth; the pure ocean is at the hip-surface. (PS 1.15.72)
At the hip, the principal thigh-region — one should contemplate <s>Mānasottara</s>;
at the root-support (<s>mūlādhāra</s>), the [land] called <s>Jāmbava</s>; at the filaments, <s>Ilāvṛta</s>. (PS 1.15.73)
The belly and other [parts] are those [continent] lines; <s>Meru</s> is at the center of the navel;
the abodes of the lords of the worlds above <s>Meru</s>, and all [other abodes] — (PS 1.15.74)
contemplating [them] at the seed-sheaths, the best of persons is liberated;

children.text: bhuvarlokaṃ tasya nābhau svarlokaṃ hṛdi cintayet // PS_1,15.75 //
children.translated_text: one should contemplate <s>Bhuvarloka</s> at his navel, <s>Svarloka</s> at his heart. (PS 1.15.75)
<s>Maharloka</s> at the chest, <s>Janaloka</s> at <s>Hari</s>'s throat,

children.text: tapolokaṃ mukhe dhyātvā satyalokaṃ tu mastake // PS_1,15.76 //
children.translated_text: having meditated on <s>Tapoloka</s> at the face, <s>Satyaloka</s> at the crown. (PS 1.15.76)
Six, eight, twelve, sixteen, two thousand petals —

children.text: nābhyādikāni padmāni bhuvarādīni vai hareḥ // PS_1,15.77 //
children.translated_text: the lotuses from the navel upward are <s>Bhuvarloka</s> and the rest, of <s>Hari</s>. (PS 1.15.77)

children.text: pātālaṃ tasya pāde tu prapadeṣu rasātalam /
children.translated_text: <s>Pātāla</s> is at his foot; at the toes, <s>Rasātala</s>;
<s>Mahātala</s> at the buttocks; at the shins, <s>Talātala</s>. (PS 1.15.78)

children.text: sutalaṃ jānudeśe tu ūrvo(pi tu)stu vitalātale /
children.translated_text: <s>Sutala</s> at the knee-region; at the thighs, <s>Vitala</s> and <s>Atala</s>;
the worlds should be contemplated at the limbs of the cosmic form (<s>virāṭ</s>) by the wise. (PS 1.15.79)
The lotus arising from the navel of <s>Padmanābha</s>, of material (<s>prākṛta</s>) [nature], mighty,
born from the combined principles (<s>tattvas</s>), composed of elements and the like — (PS 1.15.80)
consisting of all worlds — at the tip of its filament, in [the realm] called <s>Satya</s>,

children.text: ādyaḥ brahmāṃśato jāto viṣṇunaiva caturmukhaḥ // PS_1,15.81 //
children.translated_text: the first <s>Brahmā</s>, four-faced, was born from a portion, by <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself. (PS 1.15.81)
Created — desiring to see <s>Hari</s> in the four directions, <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>)

children.text: mukhāni lebhe catvāri nāpaśyaddhikṣu vai svayam // PS_1,15.82 //
children.translated_text: obtained four faces; [but] he did not see [<s>Hari</s>] in the directions himself. (PS 1.15.82)
Then, [thinking] 'I shall see <s>Hari</s> who has entered inside through the hollow of that stalk's center,'
he performed austerity — [but] he did not find the Lord there. (PS 1.15.83)
Touched by [the waters] in contact with the lower part of <s>Satya</s>-portion, by <s>Śrī</s> stationed in the water,
and by [<s>Śrī</s>] stationed in the form of <s>Vāyu</s> — the Creator became fearless of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s fear. (PS 1.15.84)

children.text: iti śrī prakāśasaṃhitāyāṃ prathamaparicchede pañcadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ sampūrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Śrī Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, in the first section, the fifteenth chapter is complete.
May it be offered to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>.
The Second Section (<s>Dvitīyaparicchedaḥ</s>).
Now, the first chapter.
<s>Śrī Haṃsa</s> said:

children.text: kañjasthitaḥ svayaṃ brahmā nāpaśyat sarvagaṃ harim /
children.translated_text: Situated on the lotus, <s>Brahmā</s> himself did not see <s>Hari</s> who pervades all;
though making effort, before that, he thought thus in his mind: (PS 2.1.1)
'Even though [I am] the presider over the positive-form ignorance of <s>Durgā</s>, [belonging to] the teacher of the universe,
because of being an eternal vessel of grace, and because of [my] sonship — <s>Ramā</s> is my [mother]. (PS 2.1.2)
Because of my devotion to my own worship, there is no positive-form ignorance [in me];
[yet <s>Durgā</s>] desires [to bestow it] upon one who is endowed with a subtle body and beginningless ignorance — (PS 2.1.3)
[she], who is under [my] own [mother] <s>Indirā</s>'s (Lakṣmī's) command — my intention [is known by her]; <s>Śiva</s> and the others,
not knowing, would speak otherwise — <s>Durgā</s> is indeed a bestower of ignorance. (PS 2.1.4)
She is not capable of giving ignorance to <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>)' — thus those under the <s>asuras</s>' influence [say];
thus, the words of the ignorant are the cause of my infamy. (PS 2.1.5)
[But] my infamy is not caused [by this];

children.text: tatrāhaṃ saṃmato mātuḥ kīrtyarthaṃ prārthayāmi tām /
children.translated_text: 'There, I am honored by [my] mother; for the sake of fame, I beseech her —

children.text: durgāmiti tathā cakre tenādātsasya saṃśayam // PS_2,1.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Durgā</s>' — thus he did; then she gave him doubt. (PS 2.1.6)
Having given ignorance for half a moment, she then extended devotion to her lord;

children.text: bhayaśokau ca tenāsāvajñobhīto babhūva hā // PS_2,1.7 //
children.translated_text: and fear and sorrow [came]; by that, the unknowing one became afraid — alas! (PS 2.1.7)
That positive-form ignorance, four times; fear of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: śoko dvivāraṃ ramayā prārthito jagadīśvaraḥ // PS_2,1.8 //
children.translated_text: sorrow twice — entreated by <s>Ramā</s>, the Lord of the universe (PS 2.1.8)
gave [these] during the state of non-seeing; a rule was established;
because of the many occurrences of functional ignorance, even for <s>Brahmā</s> — (PS 2.1.9)
since it is spoken of with numerical specificity, they call it positive-form ignorance;
then, thus, doubt arose three times for the lotus-born one: (PS 2.1.10)
'Has this lotus arisen by itself, or by some other being?'

children.text: iti sañcintya puṃsyaiva jātaṃ naiva jaḍasya tat // PS_2,1.11 //
children.translated_text: Thus reflecting, [he concluded]: 'It was born from a person alone; an insentient thing could not [produce] it.' (PS 2.1.11)
'Spontaneous activity is impossible due to the absence of knowledge, desire, and the like;

children.text: ahaṃ padmena vā jātaḥ matsṛṣṭiḥ puruṣeṇa vā // PS_2,1.12 //
children.translated_text: either I was born from the lotus, or my creation was by a Person.' (PS 2.1.12)

children.text: iti saṃścitya matsṛṣṭiḥ puruṣeṇai no vā /
children.translated_text: Thus deliberating: 'My creation was by a Person — or was it not?'

children.text: iti niścitya sa pumān svatantro vāsvatantrakaḥ // PS_2,1.13 //
children.translated_text: Thus determining — 'Is that Person independent or dependent?' (PS 2.1.13)
Thus reflecting — 'If dependent, how could he create me?

children.text: tasmāt svatantrājjātohaṃ taṃ pasyāṃ punarutthitaḥ (paśyeyaṃ) // PS_2,1.14 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, I was born from an independent [being]; let me see him!' — thus having risen again. (PS 2.1.14)
Thus saying, he entered the [lotus] stalk but did not see [anything]; rising up again,

children.text: kañjastha āsa tajjñānaṃ viparītamajasya hi // PS_2,1.15 //
children.translated_text: seated on the lotus, <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā) indeed had inverted knowledge. // PS_2,1.15 //
He who was not seen outside — how could he go on the path of inner vision?
Then, from a fierce wind arising, the earth shook from the agitated water; // PS_2,1.16 //
as if falling from the lotus, he became seized by great fear.
Then, for half a moment, sorrow arose in <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme). // PS_2,1.17 //
Having created <s>Kāla</s> (Time) and <s>Mahākāla</s> (Great Time), he extended their presiding deity;
at the approach of the end of <s>Kāla's</s> dwelling, he gave [Brahmā] what would seize him. // PS_2,1.18 //
The face of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> [appeared] then — [Brahmā] became filled with fear and sorrow;
for this very reason, he became endowed with existential ignorance. // PS_2,1.19 //
Nowhere else [does] suffering, ignorance, and the like [arise] — what is stated otherwise is indeed false.

children.text: tatastapatapa iti viṣṇoreva vaco śṛṇot // PS_2,1.20 //
children.translated_text: Then he heard the word of <s>Viṣṇu</s> itself: 'Practice austerity, practice austerity!' // PS_2,1.20 //

children.text: tato dhyānaṃ jagaddhātuḥ kṛtvā paśyat sasarvagam /
children.translated_text: Then the Creator of the world, having performed <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), saw the all-pervading one;

children.text: brahmā dadarśa vaikuṇṭhaṃ harerlokaṃ mahādbhutam // PS_2,1.21 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> beheld <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, the wondrous world of <s>Hari</s>, // PS_2,1.21 //
exalted with the previously described supreme, great, and excellent qualities and meanings;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭāva natveśaṃ kṛtārthobhūt sakañjajaḥ // PS_2,1.22 //
children.translated_text: having seen it, having bowed, he praised the Lord — the Lotus-born became fulfilled. // PS_2,1.22 //
The Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> gave him sovereignty over all and omniscience;
though independent, the Blessed One, tender toward his devotees, became subject to him. // PS_2,1.23 //
He ordained the time for the enjoyment of fourteen <s>Manus</s> as the Creator's day;

children.text: yathā tathā rātrikālaṃ vyabhajadbhagavān vibhuḥ // PS_2,1.24 //
children.translated_text: likewise, the all-pervading Blessed One divided the night-time. // PS_2,1.24 //
In the first portion of the night, he extended the cosmic egg with its limbs;
therein, <s>Viṣṇu</s> called <s>Aṇḍa</s> (the Egg), entering within, caused it to flourish. // PS_2,1.25 //
In the second portion of the night, from the navel of <s>Padmanābha</s> (Lotus-naveled Viṣṇu),
with another portion of what was created, <s>Hari</s> fashioned the world-lotus. // PS_2,1.26 //
<s>Brahmā</s> at the tip of the lotus, his ignorance and fear and the like,

children.text: tacchāntiṃ tasya tadbhaktyudrekaṃ tasya tapasthitim // PS_2,1.27 //
children.translated_text: the pacification of that, the surge of his devotion, his establishment in austerity — // PS_2,1.27 //
upon him, <s>Hari</s> bestowed complete and mighty grace.
In the third portion of the night, the exceedingly beautiful <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> — // PS_2,1.28 //
he created that, and the lord of that world — <s>Hari</s> showed it to <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā);

children.text: sa dṛṣṭvā taṃ vidadhyau muktāmukteśvaraṃ harim // PS_2,1.29 //
children.translated_text: having seen it, he meditated on <s>Hari</s>, the lord of both the liberated and the unliberated. // PS_2,1.29 //
In the fourth portion of the night, he beheld the <s>Virāṭ</s> (cosmic) creation;
having seen the gods situated in the <s>Virāṭ</s> body in the fourteen worlds, // PS_2,1.30 //
those with subtle bodies, previously [created] with subtle forms from <s>Aniruddha</s>,
<s>Aja</s> (Brahmā) then there and there itself endowed them with gross bodies. // PS_2,1.31 //
At the time of the creation of the cosmic egg, all the principles,
which were unmixed, <s>Hari</s> took and joined them, dividing them threefold. // PS_2,1.32 //
With the first [portion] he made the cosmic egg; with the second he extended the lotus;
the third he divided threefold, and again each of those into three — // PS_2,1.33 //
for gods, semi-gods, and mortals, he fashioned gross [bodies] with the first three [sub-portions];
with the second three sub-portions, gross [bodies] for the <s>Asuras</s>, by the will of <s>Śrī Hari</s>. // PS_2,1.34 //
Thus, in the <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, the first chapter of the second section.
<s>Śrī Haṃsa</s> [said]:
Having made the gross bodies, <s>Virāṭ</s> placed them in their respective regions;

children.text: teṣāṃ tadupayuktārthān jaḍāni vividhāni ca // PS_2,2.1 //
children.translated_text: their requisite objects and various inert things — // PS_2,2.1 //
all gross bodies and material causes, <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā) himself,
having gathered those given by <s>Virāṭ</s>, in order, following the course of time, // PS_2,2.2 //
their respective qualities, actions, births, forms, and characteristics,
their customs, behaviors, dress, languages, and natures, // PS_2,2.3 //
their gifts, honors, food, drink, and worthy [objects], preceding and endless collections of purposes,
suited to the qualities of eighty-four <s>lakṣa</s> (8,400,000) plus four <s>lakṣa</s> <s>jīvas</s> (souls) — // PS_2,2.4 //
as declared and intended by <s>Virāṭ</s>, the knower of his will thus carried out.

children.text: yathottaratra sthūlopi na dṛṣṭastena tacchrutam // PS_2,2.5 //
children.translated_text: As the gross [form] was not seen above, that was heard [from tradition]. // PS_2,2.5 //
Before that, from <s>Padmanābha</s> (Lotus-naveled [Viṣṇu]), from the lotus-foot of <s>Trivikrama</s>,
from its right [side], the <s>Gaṅgā</s> [flowed], sustained from the tip of his great toenail; // PS_2,2.6 //
the water that passed upward above <s>Kṣmā</s> (Earth) and <s>Varuṇa</s>, through the upper opening in the middle of the shattered cosmic egg,
previously situated in the fire-principle, protected by the primordial feet — // PS_2,2.7 //
arisen from <s>Viṣṇu's</s> foot, that water entered the interior of the cosmic egg;
placing it in the water-pot, <s>Brahmā</s> performed the washing of <s>Viṣṇu's</s> feet. // PS_2,2.8 //
He did so, and by that, the water became the excellent river named <s>Gaṅgā</s>;
therefore they call her born from <s>Viṣṇu's</s> foot and arisen from <s>Brahmā's</s> water-pot. // PS_2,2.9 //

children.text: vadanti sā suṣumnā hi brahmāṇḍavyāpino hareḥ /
children.translated_text: She is indeed <s>Suṣumnā</s>, of <s>Hari</s> who pervades the cosmic egg.
In the fifth portion of the night, [<s>Brahmā</s>] created all the immortals beginning with <s>Brahma-Īśa</s> (Brahmā and Śiva), // PS_2,2.10 //
and placed them in the <s>Durgā</s>-portion of the <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> world;
for the service of the infinite forms of <s>Śrī Hari</s> and <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) residing there. // PS_2,2.11 //
He instructed them in the appropriate knowledge and service of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: ṣaṣṭamāṃśe niśāyāśca punaḥ sarvān surottamān // PS_2,2.12 //
children.translated_text: In the sixth portion of the night, again, all the best of gods, // PS_2,2.12 //
<s>Aja</s> (Brahmā) created for his own service; and they, in the previously stated manner,
going through the seven enclosures, fully gratify the Lord of the seven worlds. // PS_2,2.13 //
Extending down to the ground below <s>Satya</s> [loka], the cosmic egg filled with water,
drying up by a greatly fierce wind, receded from <s>Maharloka</s> downward. // PS_2,2.14 //
In the seventh portion of the night, <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā) again created gods;

children.text: teṣu pradhānān sarvān manaso dehato 'sṛjat // PS_2,2.15 //
children.translated_text: among them, he created the chief ones from mind and from body. // PS_2,2.15 //
Among them, the chief ones beginning with <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Aja</s> placed in <s>Tapoloka</s>;
there, the lord of that world directly worships <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, the sinless one. // PS_2,2.16 //
He [also] created other gods from mind and from body;
<s>Indra</s> and <s>Kāma</s> — <s>Aja</s> placed them in <s>Janaloka</s> as the third pair; // PS_2,2.17 //
they worshipped <s>Pradyumna</s>; having created their subordinate gods,
the Creator placed [others] in <s>Maharloka</s>, beginning with <s>Aniruddha</s>. // PS_2,2.18 //
They, worshipping <s>Aniruddha</s>, created their subordinate gods.
In the eighth portion of the night, the Grandfather [Brahmā] created <s>Sanaka</s> and the others; // PS_2,2.19 //
having created them and appointed them to creation — through their ignorance they acted hastily.
Then, from the anger of the Creator, <s>Rudra</s>, of eleven-fold self, // PS_2,2.20 //
was born with his consort; urged by <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā) for the purpose of creation,
[instead] he practiced austerity; then in the course of time, the water within <s>Svarga</s> having been drunk [up], // PS_2,2.21 //
through <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā), having obtained [beings] not in heaven — <s>Pretas</s> (ghosts) and <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons),
<s>Nandin</s>, the seven <s>Mātṛkās</s> (Mother-goddesses), <s>Piśācas</s> (ghouls) frightening to the world — // PS_2,2.22 //
devotees, portions of gods, yet endowed with evil dispositions, naked;

children.text: krūrasṛṣṭiṃ tato jñātvā brahmā taṃ pratyaṣedhata // PS_2,2.23 //
children.translated_text: then, knowing the cruel creation, <s>Brahmā</s> restrained him. // PS_2,2.23 //
Then <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā), from his own region, created <s>Nārada</s> the sage;
from <s>Aja's</s> right thumb, <s>Dakṣa</s>; from his body, he fashioned <s>Bhṛgu</s>. // PS_2,2.24 //
<s>Marīci</s> from his mind, <s>Atri</s> from his eye, <s>Aṅgirasa</s> from his mouth,

children.text: karṇarandhrāt pulastyaṃ ca pulahaṃ nābhideśataḥ // PS_2,2.25 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pulastya</s> from the opening of his ear, <s>Pulaha</s> from the navel region, // PS_2,2.25 //

children.text: karāt kratuṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca prāṇāt kāmāccagādhijam /
children.translated_text: <s>Kratu</s> from his hand, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> from his breath, and <s>Gādhi's</s> son (<s>Viśvāmitra</s>) from desire;
<s>Kardama</s> from his shadow, <s>Ruci</s> from his intellect — the all-pervading one generated [them all]. // PS_2,2.26 //
The Lotus-born one fashioned the gods of the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and other [Vedas] from his faces in order — east and the other [directions];
the <s>Bhārata</s> (Mahābhārata), the <s>Pañcarātras</s>, the <s>Purāṇas</s>, and the <s>Smṛti</s> (law-codes) likewise — // PS_2,2.27 //
he fashioned from his faces in the east and other [directions]; likewise the <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), <s>āśramas</s> (life-stages), and the rest;
<s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Manu</s>, <s>Budha</s>, and <s>Śani</s> — the four activators of the <s>varṇas</s> — // PS_2,2.28 //
he made; the divisions of time, the directions, and their presiding deities;
<s>Yajña</s> (sacrifice) and <s>Puṇya-Dharma</s> (meritorious law) from his heart; from his back, the expansion of <s>Adharma</s> (unrighteousness); // PS_2,2.29 //
likewise the fivefold ignorance and <s>Durgā</s>, its presiding deity;
day and night, the two fortnights; shame he created from his upper lip. // PS_2,2.30 //
From his lower lip, greed; from his veins, he emitted rivers;
from his bones, mountains; from his belly, the presiding deities of all oceans; // PS_2,2.31 //
clouds from his hair; from his body-hair, trees, shrubs, and creepers;
in the eighty-four <s>lakṣa</s> plus four <s>lakṣa</s> (8,400,000) species of birth, the <s>tātvika</s> [beings], // PS_2,2.32 //
numbering ten, the Creator emitted, as well as other conscious beings;
the <s>Karma-devas</s> (action-gods) and other gods arose in order through time; // PS_2,2.33 //
a hundred <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>, thirty <s>Cāraṇas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
a hundred <s>Siddhas</s>, and likewise in the other species, seventy in all types — // PS_2,2.34 //
born from [their own] kinds, arisen from <s>Kubera</s> — from them, the portionless ones;
<s>Devadāsas</s> (divine servants), portionless, from the <s>Padma-kalpa</s> (Lotus-aeon) onward. // PS_2,2.35 //
Born on earth everywhere in the <s>Svāyambhuva Manvantara</s> (era of the first Manu), gathered together;
in the ninth portion of the night, <s>Mahīdāsa</s> and <s>Hayānana</s> (Horse-face), // PS_2,2.36 //
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> and <s>Macchalā</s> (?), were appointed and instructed <s>Manu</s> on behalf of the Creator;

children.text: avatīryākhilān vedān sāraṃ caiva(veda sāraṃ) purāṇakam // PS_2,2.37 //
children.translated_text: having brought down all the <s>Vedas</s>, and the essence — the <s>Purāṇa</s>, // PS_2,2.37 //
the great scripture <s>Pañcarātra</s>, and the auspicious <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>.

children.text: daśame tu niśābhāge padmanābhasya karṇayoḥ // PS_2,2.38 //
children.translated_text: In the tenth portion of the night, from the ears of <s>Padmanābha</s> (Viṣṇu), // PS_2,2.38 //
from the tāmasic [substance], in abundance, from the bone — the enemy-pair arose;
then, in the auspicious tenth portion of <s>Kusumanābha's</s> (Viṣṇu's) night, // PS_2,2.39 //
from the tāmasic [substance], in abundance, from the bone — the enemy-pair arose;
<s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, two <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons), arrogant with evil pride — // PS_2,2.40 //
at some point, having drunk the water standing in the upper region of <s>Meru</s>,
in another form, having reached the Lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>), the two demons challenged him to battle. // PS_2,2.41 //

children.text: āhvayāmāsa tu brahmā tāvāhāhaṃ hi durbalaḥ /
children.translated_text: They challenged <s>Brahmā</s>, who said: 'Alas, I am weak!'

children.text: ityuktvā sa hariṃ dadhyau hayagrīvāhvayaṃ hariḥ // PS_2,2.42 //
children.translated_text: Having said this, he meditated on <s>Hari</s> — <s>Hari</s>, called <s>Hayagrīva</s> (Horse-headed), // PS_2,2.42 //
became manifest from <s>Brahmā's</s> heart; he fought those two for a long time,

children.text: kṛtvā hatvācchādyakuntaṃ medhasā medinīṃ vyadhāt // PS_2,2.43 //
children.translated_text: and having slain [them] and covered with fat, he made the earth from their marrow. // PS_2,2.43 //
In the eleventh portion of the night, <s>Brahmā</s>, himself situated on <s>Meru</s>,

children.text: piśācān dānavān daityān niraṃśān sāṃśarūpakān // PS_2,2.44 //
children.translated_text: <s>Piśācas</s> (ghouls), <s>Dānavas</s> (titans), <s>Daityas</s> (demons) — portionless and portioned forms — // PS_2,2.44 //
these enemies of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the fit ones, and <s>Rākṣasas</s> and <s>Kali</s> likewise,
he emitted — he made them dwellers of the lower worlds in due course of time. // PS_2,2.45 //
The Creator gave them a boon of invincibility and indestructibility;
[with] birth in <s>Bhārata</s> in each <s>Manvantara</s> (Manu-period) through time, // PS_2,2.46 //
obtaining birth as appropriate, having performed austerity, obtaining a boon from <s>Śiva</s>,
'You shall always be haters of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, Aryans, teachers, cows, and gods' — // PS_2,2.47 //
such a boon the Lotus-born gave to them.
Excluding the supreme white triad, in the severed [portions of] the <s>Bhāgavatas</s>, // PS_2,2.48 //
having entered and caused intellectual delusion here and there,
'You shall destroy the merit arising from transgression of fitness' — thus also. // PS_2,2.49 //
The highest gods stationed in the body-principles as material causes,
you all, going to the diminution of all principles, shall then terrify [them]; // PS_2,2.50 //
'And the connection with sin and suffering shall be yours' — thus;
even in the bodies of the good who are endowed with forgetfulness of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, // PS_2,2.51 //
'May there be false identification for you among the evil ones and those of mixed intellect';
the <s>Daityas</s> are false claimants, the <s>Devas</s> are true claimants of the principles; // PS_2,2.52 //
and <s>Kali</s>, in all principles, claims the <s>jīva</s> through evil obstinacy;
the deities stationed in the body, eating the full prior merit and happiness in order, // PS_2,2.53 //
and other body-claimants, eating sin and suffering — both types;
for the <s>jīvas</s> situated inside and outside, there is some suffering also; // PS_2,2.54 //
from the possession by <s>Daityas</s>, there is no possession of <s>Vāyu</s> by <s>Daityas</s> ever —

children.text: jīvamānyuttamo brahmā dehastho madhyamaḥ svayam // PS_2,2.55 //
children.translated_text: The <s>jīva</s> (soul) who considers <s>Brahmā</s> as the highest, stationed in the body, is of middling [rank] himself; // PS 2.2.55 //
<s>Kali</s> is the lowest—those who consider the <s>jīva</s> [as supreme] are indeed gods and demons;
thus, for those who know the truth of the <s>tattvas</s>, [<s>Brahmā</s>] gave an appropriate boon from <s>Brahmā</s> onward. // PS 2.2.56 //
Outside the pure ocean, in <s>Maharloka</s> and above that,

children.text: garbhodake tu(ca) daityānām āveśo nāsti sarvathā // PS_2,2.57 //
children.translated_text: in the embryonic waters, there is absolutely no possession by <s>daityas</s> (demons). // PS 2.2.57 //
Elsewhere, for the stability of the <s>daityas</s>, the all-pervading Lord gave a boon;
at the twelfth part of the <s>tāmasī</s> [night], when the waters issue forth from the cosmic egg, // PS 2.2.58 //

children.text: cintyatojasya vai ghrāṇāt ghroṇī rūpī babhūva ha /
children.translated_text: from the nose of the contemplating luminous one, a boar-shaped form came into being;

children.text: ghroṇī rūpī varāhātmā haristvavatatāra ca // PS_2,2.59 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, of the nature of the <s>Varāha</s> (Boar), the boar-formed one, descended. // PS 2.2.59 //
He, known as <s>Śvetavarāha</s> (White Boar), praised by <s>Brahmā</s>, created
sacrifices with their presiding deities, <s>mantras</s>, ritual procedures, priests, and sacred plants; // PS 2.2.60 //
sesame, <s>darbha</s> grass, horses, sacrificial animals, ghee, oblations, and fuel-sticks in sequence;
He established <s>satras</s> (extended sacrificial sessions), the <s>soma</s> hall, and the initiatory and concluding [rites]. // PS 2.2.61 //
He also created sacrificial posts, sacrificial fires, ghee for sprinkling, and fruits;
then a <s>rākṣasa</s> (demon) named <s>Hayagrīva</s>, terrible in appearance, // PS 2.2.62 //
seizing from the mouth of the unborn one the manifest preceptor who presides over the <s>Vedas</s>,
seized [them] by force—then the <s>Vedas</s> became misrecited and hidden. // PS 2.2.63 //
Then, when implored, He assumed the form of a fish and entered the waters;
having slain the horse-headed demon, the Lord recovered the <s>Vedas</s>. // PS 2.2.64 //
Then, requested by <s>Dhātṛ</s> (Brahmā), the primeval Boar [removed] the water that had entered the cosmic egg,
dried up the earth, and made the lower worlds pure. // PS 2.2.65 //
All the planets beginning with <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun) became luminous from that time onward;

children.text: tadādi kalpaṃ taṃ prāhuḥ vārāhamiti sajjanāḥ // PS_2,2.66 //
children.translated_text: from that time, the virtuous call that <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age) the <s>Vārāha</s> (of the Boar). // PS 2.2.66 //

children.text: rātrau trayodaśāṃśe tu purīṃ barhiṣmatīṃ vyadhāt /
children.translated_text: In the thirteenth part of the night, [<s>Brahmā</s>] of the Boar-nature established the city <s>Barhiṣmatī</s>,
for the dwelling of the first <s>Manu</s>, being the knower of all. // PS 2.2.67 //
At that very time, the eight self-manifest [deities], various cities,
rivers, divine rivers, forests, and groves [appeared]; // PS 2.2.68 //
then <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā) created everywhere all things useful;
in the fourteenth part of the night, [He appointed] the guardians of the directions, who dwell in all worlds, // PS 2.2.69 //
commanding [them] everywhere in the directions and intermediate directions in due order;
these world-protectors had been produced by <s>Brahmā</s> even earlier than that. // PS 2.2.70 //
<s>Hari</s>, stationed in the <s>Virāṭ</s> (cosmic) body, the fourth, named <s>Aniruddha</s>, the all-pervading Lord,
showed the subtle [bodies] to those who were unfit in <s>Atala</s> and the other [nether regions]. // PS 2.2.71 //
He, born from the lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>), the lotus-born one stationed in the middle of <s>Meru</s>,
lifting [them] upward and endowing them with gross bodies again, // PS 2.2.72 //
establishing them in their respective worlds, placed [them] under the authority of <s>Mukhyaprāṇa</s> (chief life-breath, i.e., <s>Vāyu</s>);

children.text: tadā brahmavarodbhūto hiraṇyākṣo hi rākṣasaḥ // PS_2,2.73 //
children.translated_text: then, born from <s>Brahmā</s>'s boon, the <s>rākṣasa</s> (demon) <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, // PS 2.2.73 //
having seized the earth with its five elemental coverings, [entered] <s>Rasātala</s> (the nether region);
he entered [there]; to liberate her, the Boar-formed one, implored by the Egg-born (<s>Brahmā</s>), // PS 2.2.74 //
entering <s>Rasātala</s>, having swiftly freed the earth,

children.text: taṃ gadāpāṇinā(mā) kruddhaṃ prāpayitvaiva bhārata // PS_2,2.75 //
children.translated_text: and having confronted that enraged one, with mace in hand, O <s>Bhārata</s>— // PS 2.2.75 //

children.text: yudhvā svaṃ daṃṣṭrāgrahataṃ kṛtvā taṃ narake vyadhāt /
children.translated_text: fighting, [He] lifted him on His own tusk and consigned him to hell;

children.text: tato merugato dhātā savyātsvāyaṃbhuvaṃ vyadhāt // PS_2,2.76 //
children.translated_text: then <s>Dhātṛ</s> (Brahmā), having gone to <s>Meru</s>, from his right side created <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [Manu]; // PS 2.2.76 //
from the left side of his body, he created <s>Śatarūpā</s>, the virtuous one;
[he summoned] <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Marīci</s> and others, and the first <s>Manu</s>, for the purpose of austerity; // PS 2.2.77 //
having summoned [them], the unborn one, the refuge of the righteous, spoke about creation for the sake of expansion;

children.text: śatarūpā patiḥ prāha tapastaptvā sudāruṇam // PS_2,2.78 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śatarūpā</s>'s lord (<s>Manu</s>) said, having performed exceedingly severe austerity— // PS 2.2.78 //
[he asked:] 'Since the <s>Varāha</s> upliftment [of the earth] was accomplished, how long [has passed]?', the wise one [inquired];
[the response:] 'From <s>Hari</s>'s boon, through the union of woman and man, the creation proclaimed by <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā)— // PS 2.2.79 //
through the union of woman and man, this creation proclaimed by <s>Vidhi</s> is to come about';

children.text: sṛtvā tasyāmajanayat putrau dvau lokaviśrutau // PS_2,2.80 //
children.translated_text: having created in her, he begot two sons, renowned in the world— // PS 2.2.80 //
<s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s>, and three daughters, O best of beings;
known as <s>Ākūti</s>, <s>Devahūti</s>, and <s>Prasūti</s>. // PS 2.2.81 //
Of the first one (<s>Ākūti</s>), from <s>Ṛci</s> (Ruci), the Lord of <s>Ramā</s> was born, named <s>Yajña</s> (Sacrifice);

children.text: tenaiva saha sambhūtā dakṣiṇā nāmikā ramā // PS_2,2.82 //
children.translated_text: together with him was born <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī) named <s>Dakṣiṇā</s>; // PS 2.2.82 //
the two unborn ones, born without [a natural] womb, endowed with transcendent bodies, supreme;
by the law of adopted sonship, <s>Manu</s> [adopted] <s>Yajña</s> as his own son; // PS 2.2.83 //

children.text: cakāra dakṣiṇā yajñe dakṣiṇāmāninī ca sā /
children.translated_text: <s>Dakṣiṇā</s>, presiding over the sacrificial fee, became [the consort] in the sacrifice;

children.text: tuṣitā nāma tatputrāḥ sambabhūvuḥ surottamāḥ // PS_2,2.84 //
children.translated_text: their sons, called the <s>Tuṣitas</s>, became the best of gods. // PS 2.2.84 //
All those presiding over the <s>tattvas</s> amounted to nine <s>koṭis</s> (ninety million);
<s>Prasūti</s>, younger [sister] of <s>Ākūti</s> and <s>Devahūti</s>— // PS 2.2.85 //
became <s>Dakṣa</s>'s faithful wife; from her, sixteen daughters [were born],
the son of <s>Narka</s>—thirteen [were given] to <s>Dharma</s> himself; // PS 2.2.86 //
one daughter was given to <s>Agni</s>; in her, the three fires were born—
<s>Āhavanīya</s>, <s>Gārhapatya</s>, and <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s>—these three. // PS 2.2.87 //

children.text: teṣāmekā dakṣasutā bhāryā(dattā) tasyāṃ tribhiḥ kramāt /
children.translated_text: One daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s> was given [as wife] to each of those; from her, sequentially by each of the three,
fifteen sons each were born, of the nature of fire. // PS 2.2.88 //
The first ones were the <s>Yajñabhujas</s> (sacrifice-eating fires); the middle ones were the <s>Havyabhojins</s> (oblation-eating fires);
the last were the <s>Kavyabhujas</s> (ancestral offering-eating fires)—with the former, the fires number forty-five [sic, fifty]. // PS 2.2.89 //

children.text: ekanyūnā dakṣasutā jyeṣṭhā dattā śivasya tu /
children.translated_text: One less [of Dakṣa's daughters], the eldest, was given to <s>Śiva</s>;
<s>Dharma</s>'s wife <s>Varūtvatī</s> gave birth to fifty <s>Maruts</s> (wind-gods) as sons. // PS 2.2.90 //
The ten <s>Viśvedevas</s> were born in <s>Viśvā</s>; the eight <s>Vasus</s> from <s>Vasu</s>;
the <s>Rudras</s>, unattached, [were born] in <s>Rudrāṇī</s>; in <s>Bhūtā</s>, the <s>Bhūta</s> lords; // PS 2.2.91 //
the <s>Upadevas</s> (minor deities) in <s>Sādhyā</s>; and from the other [wives] of <s>Dharma</s> also,
<s>Upadevas</s> and <s>Devas</s> came into being, indeed of many progeny. // PS 2.2.92 //
All of them are considered fit for [higher] stations of <s>Dharma</s> and suitable for [cosmic] creation;
those born from them, as well as future ones, are mostly directly perceiving [the truth]. // PS 2.2.93 //
The previously mentioned <s>tāttvika</s> ones, in a single form, on the earth in <s>Bhārata</s> (India),
having resided [there], desiring future meritorious <s>karma</s>, knowledge, devotion, and the like, // PS 2.2.94 //

children.text: śubhāśubhaṃ ca prārabdhaṃ bhoktuṃ yogyāstato bhavat /
children.translated_text: become fit to experience the auspicious and inauspicious <s>prārabdha</s> (commenced karma);

children.text: te ca dvīpādri varṣeṣu bhārate(tā)nyeṣu sarvaśaḥ // PS_2,2.95 //
children.translated_text: and they, in the islands, mountains, and regions, in <s>Bhārata</s> and the others, everywhere— // PS 2.2.95 //
worthy of enjoying the single fruit of well-commenced [karma], born of merit and demerit,

children.text: āsan devāśca pūrvoktā hyaparokṣya naparokṣiṇaḥ // PS_2,2.96 //
children.translated_text: were gods as previously described, having directly perceived or not directly perceived [the truth]. // PS 2.2.96 //
In this <s>Bhārata</s>, capable of performing true spiritual practice, with the best of gods—
the manifest directly perceiving ones were always born by the will of <s>Hari</s>. // PS 2.2.97 //
<s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s>—those two attained the highest accomplishment;

children.text: niśā caturdaśāṃśe tu sṛṣṭireṣā sumerugāḥ // PS_2,2.98 //
children.translated_text: in the fourteenth part of the night, this creation [occurred], centered on <s>Sumeru</s>. // PS 2.2.98 //
Thus ends the second chapter of the second section of the glorious <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>.
<s>Hari</s> <s>Oṃ</s>.
Then on <s>Meru</s>, the eldest [<s>Brahmā</s>] established the wish-fulfilling cow and wish-granting tree,
the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem), with varieties of form, in <s>Svarga</s> (heaven) and the sub-heavens. // PS 2.3.1 //
Then <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā) contemplated the reflected forms of all <s>jīvas</s> (souls);
becoming thus and thus himself, he created beings with corresponding bodies. // PS 2.3.2 //
For those stationed in heaven and in [higher] stations, in all <s>manvantaras</s> (Manu-epochs),
<s>Vidhi</s> carried out the command regarding <s>Hari</s>'s <s>avatāras</s> (descents) on earth. // PS 2.3.3 //
For the experience of evil <s>prārabdha</s>, for future meritorious practice,
for the sake of the gods' service to <s>Hari</s>, the <s>avatāras</s> [occur] in sequence; // PS 2.3.4 //
again, through their respective original forms, He always achieves unity;

children.text: bhuvaṃ spṛśantviti tathā te ca kurvantyajājñayā // PS_2,3.5 //
children.translated_text: 'Let them touch the earth'—thus they act, by the command of the unborn one. // PS 2.3.5 //
Due to the ever-increasing hatred of the enemies [of the gods], <s>Hari</s> did not command

children.text: nājñāpayadharistena tathā cakre satāṃ(tān) vidhiḥ // PS_2,3.6 //
children.translated_text: permanent residence in <s>Bhārata</s>; therefore <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā) arranged them accordingly. // PS 2.3.6 //
Then <s>Dhātṛ</s> (Brahmā), stationed on <s>Meru</s>, contemplated the <s>tattvas</s> (principles),
high and low, mixed, and their presiding lords, situated in his own body from the left side. // PS 2.3.7 //
In the middle of the body, below the navel, is the <s>Mūlādhāra</s> (root-support), that lotus,
with four petals, golden in color; <s>Māyā</s> and others are the deities of the petals; // PS 2.3.8 //
<s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Udāna</s> (upward breath), and <s>Suṣumnā</s> have the three [regions] as their support;
arising in the middle of that, the <s>nāḍī</s> (channel) <s>Suṣumnā</s>, of subtle form, // PS 2.3.9 //
is one, without branches, golden in color, supported by the Supreme;
protected by <s>Bhūmī</s> (Earth) and <s>Svāyambhuva</s>, arising in the lotus; // PS 2.3.10 //
having openings, it is the support of the seven <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) and other winds;
blazing in the middle, flanked by <s>Piṅgalā</s> and <s>Iḍā</s> born at its sides; // PS 2.3.11 //
from the crown to the navel-lotus, it is the support of the six lotuses;
the navel lotus has six petals; <s>Nīlā</s> and the others are the lords of its petals; // PS 2.3.12 //
in the region tinged with slight blue, endowed with red-yellow hue,
is stationed [the deity] named <s>Pradyumna</s>, served by the <s>prāṇa</s> called <s>Nāga</s>; // PS 2.3.13 //
He contemplated the seven winds beginning with <s>Pravaha</s>, stationed therein;
those two [<s>nāḍīs</s>] face upward; the heart lotus faces downward; // PS 2.3.14 //
situated sixteen finger-breadths above the navel, with eight petals arising from <s>Suṣumnā</s> in the eight directions,
with petals facing downward, of the color of the rising sun, eight [in number]; // PS 2.3.15 //
measuring ten finger-breadths inside, auspicious, bearing the sheaths of embryonic [existence],
with tips firmly interlocked with each other, measuring [the width of] a finger; // PS 2.3.16 //
that is the heart-lotus; therein, the Goddess of Speech (<s>Vāgdevī</s>), together with <s>Bhāratī</s>, presides;
<s>Prāṇa</s>, of the nature of <s>Kūrma</s> (Tortoise), is there; the <s>Vasus</s> are the deities of the petals; // PS 2.3.17 //
the presiding Lord, <s>Hari</s>, stationed within that, measures ten finger-breadths;
His heart-space is the pavilion, of the nature of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī); // PS 2.3.18 //
endowed with three portions—<s>Durgā</s>, <s>Bhū</s>, and <s>Śrī</s>—distinguished by their respective portions;
<s>Durgā</s> is of the nature of the bulb, <s>Bhū</s> (Earth) is in the middle, in the form of the stalk; // PS 2.3.19 //
in the <s>Śrī</s>-portion above, <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī) has the form of the lotus;

children.text: vedikā tu tribhāgasthā sārdhāṅguli dṛḍhā matā // PS_2,3.20 //
children.translated_text: the altar, situated in the three portions, is considered firm, measuring one and a half finger-breadths. // PS 2.3.20 //
That pavilion, made of gems, with four doorways, is an auspicious abode,
delightful with fragrances, gem-lamps, and plantain-tree pillars; // PS 2.3.21 //
adorned with arched gateways, full water-vessels, banners, and parasols,
with gem pillars, pearl garlands, and various white sprouts; // PS 2.3.22 //
the <s>Śrī</s>-portion is honored as the lotus; <s>Hari</s> Himself, called <s>Mūleśa</s> (Root-Lord),
above the lotus, the orbs of the moon, sun, and fire [shine] clearly; // PS 2.3.23 //
a beautiful, divine couch appeared, with a lovely bolster;
on it, <s>Hari</s>, in His essential form resembling <s>Śeṣa</s>, with raised hoods above; // PS 2.3.24 //
above Him, <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), of beautiful form, in the form of a seat, situated above;

children.text: prājñātmā sa tu jīveśo jīvoyadvaśagaḥ sadā // PS_2,3.25 //
children.translated_text: He, of the nature of <s>Prājña</s> (the Wise), is the Lord of the <s>jīva</s>—the <s>jīva</s> is always subject to Him. // PS 2.3.25 //
Four-armed, with discus, conch, mace, and lotus in [His] hands;
resplendent with crown, earrings, anklets, and armlets as ornaments; // PS 2.3.26 //
adorned with necklace, <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, <s>Kaustubha</s> gem on His neck, and the like;
honored with gem rings, bracelets, waist-cord, and the rest; // PS 2.3.27 //
wearing a yellow garment, endowed with beauty and grace befitting all limbs;
though having faces in all directions, He appears as if with one face, with dark eyes; // PS 2.3.28 //
the <s>Sthāneśa</s> (Station-Lord), together with the <s>Mūleśa</s> (Root-Lord), is to be worshipped by those without portions;
below the pavilion, the <s>Śakti</s> (Power) stationed in that region has the form of the support (<s>ādhāra</s>); // PS 2.3.29 //
<s>Kūrma</s> (Tortoise), <s>Śeṣa</s>, and <s>Bhū</s> (Earth) have the form of the <s>kṣaura</s> (tonsure), ocean, and continent;
contemplating <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī) as white, by those without portions—thus He contemplated. // PS 2.3.30 //
In the thighs, the palate, between the eyebrows, and on the head—with upward-facing [lotuses]—
The lotuses are of white color, with twelve, sixteen, and eight petals respectively;
two are endowed with a thousand petals each; the petal-deities:
the <s>Ādityas</s> (solar deities) in the first lotus; <s>Indra</s> and others are the deities therein.
The deities in the third lotus are <s>Bhāratī</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s>;
at the crown, the one in many forms, <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind), is the lord of all petals.
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>—He is the Lord of that [lotus];
<s>Kṛkala</s>, called <s>Devadatta</s>, named <s>Sūtra</s>—the lord of the <s>Maruts</s> (winds).
The <s>Maruts</s>, seven times seven, in the five [vital breaths] as well;

children.text: suṣumnā nālajātāni padmānyetāni sapta ca // PS_2,3.35 //
children.translated_text: born from the stalk of the <s>Suṣumnā</s>, these seven lotuses—
the <s>Suṣumnā</s> <s>nāḍī</s> (channel), whose nature is the three <s>guṇas</s>, [is described] by those who have mastered the <s>Vedas</s>;

children.text: syaikā śākhādi rahitā garbhechidrānvatāpi ca // PS_2,3.36 //
children.translated_text: it is one, without branches, though with openings within the womb.
<s>Sarasvatī</s>, the river within it, of the nature of water,

children.text: hairaṇmayī vaidhyutīti vajrikā bhāsvatīti sā // PS_2,3.37 //
children.translated_text: is [called] <s>Hairaṇmayī</s>, <s>Vaidhyutī</s>, <s>Vajrikā</s>, <s>Bhāsvatī</s>—
by these names; the worlds, <s>Bhūḥ</s> and others, are situated therein;
the lords of the <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, and <s>Svar</s> worlds; those of <s>Mahar</s> and above, in sequence.
<s>Bhū</s>, <s>Vighneśa</s> (Gaṇeśa), <s>Indra</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s>, and <s>Abjaja</s> (Brahmā) are considered [their lords];
at the waist, the two thighs, knees, calves, ankles, and feet—
the deities residing in <s>Atala</s> and other [nether worlds], servants of the Lord of gods, in the body;
<s>Mitra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Astra</s>, <s>Pava</s> (Vāyu), <s>Vārīśa</s> (Varuṇa), <s>Maya</s>, <s>Manda</s>, <s>Yama</s>—in sequence.
Thus in the body, the <s>Virāṭ</s> (cosmic) body-bearer, measured by that [standard],
the <s>Suṣumnā</s>, arising from the base region—<s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, and <s>Vārdharā</s>—
<s>Piṅgalā</s> and <s>Iḷā</s>, of red and blue colors, going to the right and left,
with openings within, branching into thirty-six thousand.
Separately, the left <s>nāḍīs</s> are considered to be of the nature of <s>Mahat-tattva</s> (the great principle);
divided threefold, reaching to the feet—measured as twelve thousand.
On the right, reaching to the right foot—the <s>nāḍīs</s> are equally measured, in sequence;
the <s>Piṅgalā</s>, pervading the upper body—equally measured, auspicious.
Those going below, in the middle, and above—seven, dependent on the path;

children.text: saptasantyeva vivarāḥ ghrāṇāsya śruti netragāḥ // PS_2,3.45 //
children.translated_text: there are indeed seven openings—in the nose, mouth, ears, and eyes.
The seven orbs, named after the seven face-paths, are declared;
seven upward <s>nāḍīs</s>, from beneath the heart-lotus, going to the left side.
Again from the heart-lotus, from the upper region, turning to the right, the <s>Piṅgalās</s>—

children.text: saptāsya pathagāḥ tatra(sūryo) vahnyādyā vatsareśvarāḥ // PS_2,3.47 //
children.translated_text: the seven going through the face-paths; therein the Sun, Fire, and other lords of the years.
The lords of the months of the northern solstice; the lords of days; the lords of the bright fortnight—
the three supreme bright [fortnights]—indeed, these very ones are the presiding deities.
The <s>Piṅgalā</s> [nāḍīs] are designated by the names of all gods beginning from the Sun;
in that [nāḍī], <s>Brahmā</s> is the presiding deity; <s>Gī</s> (Sarasvatī); the <s>ṛjus</s> (upright beings) are those with direct perception.

children.text: prāṇāpānā vilāyāṃ ca piṅgalāyāṃ ca vartataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Apāna</s> function in the <s>Iḷā</s> and the <s>Piṅgalā</s>,
in twenty-six thousand forms, in those [nāḍīs], the two, joined with <s>Bhāratī</s> (Sarasvatī).
Likewise <s>Aniruddha</s> and <s>Pradyumna</s> on the right, in male form;

children.text: strīsvarūpeṇa vāme tu tāvadrūpaiśca tāsvalam // PS_2,3.51 //
children.translated_text: in female form on the left—with that many forms in those [nāḍīs].
Situated in such forms of <s>Prāṇa</s>, worshipped by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others;
the lords of the months of the southern solstice; the deities who are lords of the nights;
the lords of the dark fortnights—<s>Rudra</s>, <s>Vipas</s> (Sarasvatī), <s>Śeṣa</s>, and others, with their wives;
in the <s>Iḷā</s>, which is of the nature of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle), all the deities are presiding entities.
<s>Ānandamaya</s> (bliss-sheath) and <s>Vijñānamaya</s> (knowledge-sheath) are the lords of <s>Piṅgalā</s> and <s>Iḷā</s> respectively;
<s>Vyāna</s>, dwelling in all the joints; <s>Udāna</s>, situated in the <s>Brahma-nāḍī</s> (channel of Brahman);
the <s>Suṣumnā</s> is [called] the <s>Brahma-nāḍī</s>; <s>Samāna</s> pervades the entire body.
Going below, in the middle, and above—seven times seven <s>Iḷā-nāḍīs</s>, in sequence;
the seven going through the horse-path; the upward <s>Iḷās</s>, like the <s>Piṅgalā</s>;
from the region below the heart-lotus, reaching the left side, then above—
then reaching the right again, the seven going through the horse-path, in sequence.
The <s>Iḷās</s>, designated by the names of deities of earth, smoke, and others, in their entirety.
In the <s>sūkta</s> portions of the <s>Ṛg Veda</s>, the <s>Bṛhatī</s> [meter] with a thousand <s>ṛks</s>;
with twice eight, eighteen minus one <s>sūtras</s>—the full <s>ṛk</s> will come into being.
A foot consists of nine syllables; with four such feet—
the <s>ṛk</s> joined with those syllables—seventy-two in number are declared.
Seventy-two thousand syllables pervade all the <s>ṛks</s>;
in seventy-two thousand, in the [nāḍīs] called <s>Piṅgalā</s> and <s>Iḷā</s>—
in those <s>nāḍīs</s>, in their respective groups, one should contemplate the designating forms.
From the four directions of the <s>Suṣumnā</s>, stationed below the heart-lotus—
mind, intellect, ego, and <s>citta</s> (consciousness)—thus fourfold;
therein, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Kāma</s>, with their wives—the presiding deities of those specific [faculties].
In the ears, the directional deities and <s>Candra</s> (Moon); of the skin, the one named <s>Prāṇa</s>;
of both eyes, <s>Bhāskara</s> (Sun); of the tongue, <s>Mānī</s> <s>Varuṇa</s> is declared.
The two <s>Aśvins</s>, residing in the nose—the presiding deities of those specific [faculties];

children.text: vaktre(vāci) vahniḥ karedakṣo jayantaḥ pādayordhvayoḥ // PS_2,3.64 //
children.translated_text: in the mouth (speech), <s>Vahni</s> (Fire); of the hands, <s>Dakṣa</s>; <s>Jayanta</s> of the two feet.
<s>Mitra</s> and <s>Svāyambhuvau</s> are the presiding deities of the excretory and generative organs;
<s>Prāṇa</s> is of sound; <s>Mānī</s> of the skin; <s>Apāna</s> relates to touch;
<s>Vyāna</s> relates to form; <s>Rasāmānī</s> (the lord of taste); <s>Udāna</s> is situated in smell;
<s>Samāna</s>—these are the presiding deities of the subtle elements, specifically.

children.text: bhūdevī māninī pṛthvīḥ abātmā varuṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūdevī</s> (Earth Goddess) presides over earth; <s>Varuṇa</s> is remembered as the soul of water;
<s>Agni</s> is of the nature of fire; in air, <s>Pravaha</s> is the lord and master;
<s>Vighneśa</s> (Gaṇeśa) presides over <s>ākāśa</s> (ether)—these are the specific lords of the elements.
Hair, bone, skin, flesh, and nails—these forms of earth are considered [to reside] in the body;
blood constitutes the water-element in the body; the digestive fire is the fire-element;

children.text: vāyuḥ śvāsātmakaḥ kāye hyavakāśo nabhastanau // PS_2,3.69 //
children.translated_text: breath constitutes the air-element in the body; space is the ether-element in the body.

children.text: pratyakṣasiddhasarveṣāṃ satvaṃ bā(bo)dhyaṃ na hi kvacit /
children.translated_text: The existence of all these, established by direct perception, is not to be doubted anywhere.
Good and bad smells are perceived by the nose in the body; the tongue-organ delights in
auspicious and inauspicious tastes; form is perceived by the eye in the body;

children.text: śītoṣṇādiḥ tvacāvedyaḥ sparśaḥ śabde(bdaḥ) śrutipriye(yaḥ) // PS_2,3.71 //
children.translated_text: cold, heat, and the like—touch is perceived by the skin; sound is [perceived] by the beloved ear.
The objects of the subtle elements and sense organs are declared as real and irrefutable.
Speech, giving, movement, excretion, enjoyment, and other functions—
the five organs of action are instruments of objective activity—this is irrefutable.
Truly, one hears, touches, sees, eats, and smells—
the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose are those principles;
they are indeed producers of objective activity—this is to be understood as Vedic teaching.
The mind too, being the cause of hearing, is the seventh, residing in the body;
because it is the foundation of ego-sense, the <s>Piṅgalā</s> is the seat of "mine-ness";
the <s>nāḍīs</s>, at the time of weakness, appear on the right and left;
they become the indicators of masculine and feminine nature in men and women.
Therefore, real and in many ways, they are the promoters of knowledge and ignorance;
the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) beginning with <s>sattva</s>, residing in the body, are real; their presiding deities—
the gods are real; the inert [matter] alone, without the proper connection for stability—
of bodies and embodied beings, those who have the notion of body-bondage—
because of tasting suffering, the cause of obtaining a body is indeed real.
<s>Karmas</s> (actions) are of two kinds: those described in the <s>Vedas</s> in sequence—good and bad—
giving happiness and suffering; therefore, the <s>Vedas</s> are entirely real;

children.text: deśe kāle kṛtaṅkarma phaladattvena tau vṛtau // PS_2,3.80 //
children.translated_text: action performed in [a certain] place and time—those two (place and time) are employed as fruit-givers;
the <s>jīvas</s> who experience the fruits of that <s>karma</s> are real, with their subtle bodies;

children.text: bhagnaliṅgā vimuktāśca śrutyuktāśca kṛtāḥ smṛtāḥ // PS_2,3.81 //
children.translated_text: those whose subtle bodies are destroyed are liberated—thus declared in <s>śruti</s> (scripture) and <s>smṛti</s> (tradition).
Here and elsewhere, with little or much knowledge and ignorance, by yogins—
the hierarchy of existence and non-existence—these seven are independent.
Of the nature of consciousness—these, devoid of bodily connection—

children.text: niyantā puruṣaśreṣṭhaḥ na ca etat prayujyate // PS_2,3.83 //
children.translated_text: the controller is the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person); this [view] is not properly applied [by opponents].
Therefore, the Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, all-pervading, independent, enjoined by <s>śruti</s> (scripture),

children.text: nirdeṣo nityasuguṇaḥ sadā nārāyaṇo hariḥ // PS_2,3.84 //
children.translated_text: beyond description, eternally possessed of good qualities—ever <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hari</s>.
Thus the <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self) is true; the <s>adhibhūta</s> (pertaining to elements), situated externally—
because of being the cause of all sprouts, earth is real, the cause of all.
Water, being suitable for moistening, etc.; fire being the instrument of protection and burning;
air as the desiccator; ether as the provider of space—
those causes, the subtle elements, and the sense organs within them—
all are real; likewise all the compounded [elements] within the cosmic egg.
The root causes of these, even uncompounded, are entirely real;
having gathered and fashioned this, the real one (<s>Brahmā</s>) goes, together with the unborn.
[The opponents say:] "Some are without limbs, without bodies, devoid of qualities such as knowledge,
without parts, of fragmentary form, invisible to all, undetermined,
without name or form, not granting fruits, not to be worshipped or contemplated—

children.text: brahmaikantu jaḍaṃ sarve brahmaṇyāropitaṃ mṛṣā // PS_2,3.90 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> alone; everything inert is superimposed upon <s>Brahman</s>; it is false.
Like silver in a shell, like a snake in a rope, it appears;

children.text: ajñānaṃ kalpitaṃ taddhi śuktijñānāddhi bādhyate // PS_2,3.91 //
children.translated_text: that ignorance is imagined; it is indeed refuted by the knowledge of the shell.

children.text: vicārite sati hi sā śuktirnarajataṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: When examined, that shell is not silver;

children.text: ato bodhyaṃ mṛṣābhūtaṃ mithyā tadrajataṃ yathā // PS_2,3.92 //
children.translated_text: therefore, what is to be known is false; it is illusory, like that silver.
The essential nature of a thing, through knowledge, because it is imagined—thus it is;
this universe, imagined by ignorance, is superimposed upon <s>Brahman</s>.
The <s>jīva</s> is the superimposer upon <s>Brahman</s>; nothing other than <s>Brahman</s> exists;
<s>Brahman</s>, though without parts, covered by that ignorance, directly
experiences infinite forms, born from various wombs.
Its ignorance arises from <s>upādhis</s> (limiting adjuncts); a real <s>upādhi</s> does not exist;
it is false, because it is born of ignorance; ignorance is not said to be real.
By that ignorance, situated in the <s>jīva</s>—since the <s>jīva</s> has no [independent] existence of its own—
in the attributeless <s>Brahman</s>, both knowledge and ignorance function.
Therefore, that [ignorance] is not established in <s>Brahman</s>; that knowledge and that <s>upādhi</s>-born [ignorance]—
thus, through false time, <s>karma</s>, place, scripture, and other [factors],

children.text: bhramadbrahma ca kalpānte brahmamūla svarūpakam // PS_2,3.98 //
children.translated_text: the wandering <s>Brahman</s>, at the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, [returns to] its <s>Brahman</s>-rooted essential nature.
Having known that, having attained oneness therein, one is not born again on earth;

children.text: muktasyāpi na cājñānaṃ nendriyāṇi na kvacit // PS_2,3.99 //
children.translated_text: even for the liberated, there is no ignorance, no sense organs, nowhere.
In the attributeless Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, such oneness indeed—

children.text: tadajñānaṃ na sannāsatsadasanna ca tarhikam // PS_2,3.100 //
children.translated_text: that ignorance is neither existent nor non-existent, neither both existent-and-non-existent, nor otherwise;
it is indescribable; its removal is called liberation."

children.text: pūrvāpareṣu kāleṣu sṛṣṭinmetyapi te jaguḥ // PS_2,3.101 //
children.translated_text: "In past and future times, 'creation is from me'—thus they declared."
This evil doctrine the saints, the <s>tāttvika</s> (true) ones, do not accept.
Thus, in the <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, the third chapter of the second section.
<s>Śrī Haṃsa</s> (the Divine Swan) spoke:
Having a body consisting of knowledge with all its limbs, filled with infinite qualities,
terrifying the wicked along with their limbs—the Lord, established by the scriptures to be known.
Rich in infinite names and forms, granting to each the fruit appropriate to their fitness,

children.text: vicāritamupāsyaṃ ca ramā brahmādibhiḥ sadā // PS_2,4.2 //
children.translated_text: contemplated and worshipped always by <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), <s>Brahmā</s>, and others.
Served by infinite liberated and unliberated minute <s>jīvas</s> who are distinct from Him and inferior—

children.text: sevitaṃ śrīpatiṃ vyāptaṃ cetanācetanasya tu // PS_2,4.3 //
children.translated_text: the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>, pervading the conscious and the unconscious.
The creator of all that is real, <s>Hari</s>, the experiencer of suffering and the like—

children.text: jānanti tasya cājñānaṃ kvacit kvāpi na yujyate // PS_2,4.4 //
children.translated_text: they know Him; His ignorance is nowhere, at any time, applicable.
That false ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) exists — for this there is no valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>).
That ignorance would be a limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) [of <s>Brahman</s>] — the sixth connection [argument] is fitting.

children.text: siddhau jñāne tu tajjopādhiḥ siddhai tadanvaye /
children.translated_text: But if knowledge is established, then that adjunct too is established by its connection;
since ignorance is connected with everything, due to its absence, that alone [follows] and nothing else.
Due to the absence of ignorance, there is no knower; nothing more than that exists.
Due to the absence of ignorance, [knowledge] whose form is the removal of that — this does not exist anywhere.
Scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) imagined by ignorance — it cannot be the destroyer of ignorance.

children.text: iti heyaṃ tanmataṃ hi baddhasyeśo vimuktidaḥ // PS_2,4.8 //
children.translated_text: Thus, that doctrine is to be rejected. For the bound one, the Lord is the giver of liberation.

children.text: viśvaṃ satyaṃ naiva mithyā na bādhyaṃ satyakāraṇam /
children.translated_text: The universe is real, never false; it is not sublated; the cause is real.
The world is established through valid means of knowledge such as perception — it is not superimposed.
The silver perceived in a mother-of-pearl shell does not produce practical effect — the world does produce practical effect;

children.text: arthakriyākāri tena taddṛṣṭānto na yujyate // PS_2,4.10 //
children.translated_text: therefore that analogy [of illusory silver to the world] is not applicable.
That which lacks an analogy — the cause of the world's falsity —

children.text: na bhavet tanmate brahma dṛśyatvācca tathā bhavet // PS_2,4.11 //
children.translated_text: cannot exist. According to that doctrine, <s>Brahman</s> too, because it is seen, would likewise [be false].
That limited space and the like are said by the <s>Vedas</s> to be <s>Viṣṇu</s> — that is not false;

children.text: na ca nyāyoktamithyātve mānaṃ tanmatāpi na // PS_2,4.12 //
children.translated_text: and the falsity propounded by [their] logic has no valid means of knowledge; nor is that their doctrine [really].
The <s>Śruti</s> (revealed scripture) is eternal and not of human origin — it is not vitiated by bad sentences.
Having known this, <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) awakened the knowledge of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s greatness.
The Lord of the entirely real universe, through real and true means of practice,
is to be worshipped always by real souls — the giver of real and true liberation.
Thus, <s>Brahmā</s>, stationed on <s>Meru</s>, at the end of night, having anointed the Lord with a sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>),

children.text: abhiṣicya sapatnīkaṃ sarge sampārthya yojayat // PS_2,4.15 //
children.translated_text: together with his consort, having requested [permission] for creation, set [it] in motion.
<s>Hari</s> protected <s>Svarga</s> (heaven), praised by all hosts of gods.
Then <s>Svāyaṃbhuva Manu</s>, accompanied by <s>Śatarūpā</s>,
was anointed by <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and settled on earth at <s>Barhiṣmatī</s>.
The future ones, those established in their positions, and the sub-gods — in thousands —

children.text: manuṃ paryacaran prītyā te niraṃśāstato bhavan /
children.translated_text: served <s>Manu</s> with devotion; they, being partless, came into being from that.
Then <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), from <s>Māyā</s>'s own expansion, created one called <s>Bala</s>,
and he created ninety-six <s>Māyās</s> through his own self-expansion —

children.text: svairiṇyaścaiva kāminyaḥ puṃścalya iti tridhā // PS_2,4.19 //
children.translated_text: wanton women (<s>svairiṇī</s>), lustful women (<s>kāminī</s>), and promiscuous women (<s>puṃścalī</s>) — of three kinds.
Those born from them — the ones [females] who enjoy — are regarded as many.
Having performed desired [karma] in this <s>Bhārata</s>, led by the lowest mortals,

children.text: adho lokeṣu viharaḥ etābhiḥ saha durmadāḥ /
children.translated_text: they sport in the lower worlds with these [women], intoxicated.
Many, accompanied by <s>Dānavas</s> (demons) — <s>Bala</s> is their chief.
Below that, in <s>Vitala</s>, surrounded by threefold hosts of beings,
accompanied by some <s>Rākṣasa</s> hosts — <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) dwells, it is said.
He always sports with her; and from his seed, wanderers (<s>āṭakas</s>) and the like,

children.text: ḥ nadī tadantagā tatra śuṣmatyapyagnivāyubhiḥ // PS_2,4.23 //
children.translated_text: and a river flowing within that [realm] — <s>Śuṣmatī</s>, born of <s>Agni</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>.
By drinking the water of that river, those dwelling in the lower worlds,

children.text: madoddhatā narānāryaḥ krīḍanti suciraṃ sadā // PS_2,4.24 //
children.translated_text: intoxicated with excitement — men and women — play for a very long time, always.
Below that, in <s>Sutala</s>, in every <s>Manvantara</s>,
