<s>Prahlāda</s> dwelt with his followers, under different names and forms.
In the <s>Vaivasvata Manvantara</s>, [the Lord], as <s>Vāmana</s>, requesting three steps of land from <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
for his own son, [who was] the son of the great-souled <s>Kaśyapa</s> —
<s>Bali</s>, the son of <s>Virocana</s>, being mighty, gave the three worlds.
He too, for <s>Indra</s> who was established in his position — having taken [from <s>Bali</s>], he gave
the three worlds to the gods; the younger brother [of <s>Indra</s>], having the form of a dwarf (<s>vaṭu</s>),
appeared from <s>Kaśyapa</s> by the power of the <s>Payovrata</s> observance.
The lord of the universe, [born] during <s>Indra</s>'s exile, for the satisfaction of his distressed mother,
established <s>Bali</s>, the son of <s>Virocana</s>, the greatest among the supreme devotees of the Lord,
in that world; he himself became the doorkeeper of that [world].
<s>Vāmana</s>, in his true form, became served by all the gods.
From the three <s>koṭis</s> (30 million) of hair-pores of his, <s>Vāyu</s> [manifested] in as many true forms;
together with <s>Vāṇī</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>) in as many beautiful forms, he became the worshipper of <s>Vāmana</s>.
<s>Bali</s>, the husband of <s>Vindhyāvalī</s>, dwells there with his followers.
Below that, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, filled with love, even [though] worshipped by all <s>Dānavas</s>,
was requested by the <s>Dānava</s> clan — he was born there as <s>Takṣā</s> (the carpenter) formerly.
The protector of that world, for the <s>Daityas</s>, designed the three cities (<s>Tripuras</s>) —
of indivisible and divisible forms, made of gold, silver, and iron.
He fashioned three cities made of gold, silver, and iron.
By desire, in those respective [cities], the inhabitants of the three cities were established,
and in the intervals of their pleasures, they did not harm any beings.
The gods, oppressed by their [power], sought the refuge of <s>Rudra</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), being empowered.

children.text: rudraḥ pṛthvīrathaṃ kṛtvā rathāṅgaṃ śaśibhaskarau // PS_2,4.36 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>, having made the earth his chariot, the sun and moon his wheels,
having made the gods his horses and the lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>) his charioteer,

children.text: śeṣaṃ maurvyāṃ vidhāyeśo patatraṃ(taṃ) ca khageśvaram // PS_2,4.37 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śeṣa</s> the bowstring, and the lord of birds (<s>Garuḍa</s>) the banner,
and having made <s>Viṣṇu</s> the form of the arrow — <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) himself, in a single instant,
burned the three cities — the Lord, the benefactor of all worlds (<s>Śaṅkara</s>).
Together with the sons and others of the <s>Tripura</s> demons, he dwells there indeed.
In the <s>Vaivasvata Manvantara</s>, the wives of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s daughter, who were the wives of <s>Kaśyapa</s> —
were thirteen; through austerity, in them he obtained sons.
<s>Vivasvān</s>, <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>,
<s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s> — in <s>Aditi</s>, the dwarf <s>Vāmana</s> [was born].
The sons of <s>Aditi</s> are the <s>Ādityas</s>; <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> and <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>,

children.text: danau tu dānavā gāvo mahiṣyaḥ surabhīsutāḥ /
children.translated_text: in <s>Danu</s> — the <s>Dānavas</s>; cows and she-buffaloes are the offspring of <s>Surabhī</s>.
From <s>Tāmrā</s> — birds; from <s>Iriṣṭā</s> — <s>Rākṣasas</s> (night-wanderers); and <s>Nirṛti</s> [likewise].
In <s>Ilā</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> were born; dogs and the like are the offspring of <s>Paramā</s>.

children.text: poṣṭāyā caiva betālāḥ kārdraveyā mahāhayaḥ // PS_2,4.43 //
children.translated_text: From <s>Poṣṭā</s>, the <s>Vetālas</s> (vampires); from <s>Kadraveyī</s>, the great serpents.
In this <s>Manvantara</s>, sixty thousand serpents,
born from <s>Kadrū</s> — among them, some are real (<s>tāttvika</s>), servants of <s>Śeṣa</s>.
Others are action-born (<s>karmaja</s>) or naturally-born (<s>ājānaja</s>) — equal; and their sons and grandsons,
with their wives, rich in jewels and earth — they dwell in <s>Mahātala</s>.
Greatly venomous, most terrible, able to assume any form, wicked.
<s>Kaśyapa</s>, on the banks of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>, with his wives, performed austerities.
At some distance from her, he arranged the dwellings of his wives,
endowed with appropriate furnishings; and their servants dwelt in them.
Once, the two mothers (<s>Vinatā</s> and <s>Kadrū</s>), going to the side of the <s>Himavat</s>,
having seen <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> [the divine horse], the earth-mother (<s>Kadrū</s>) with dark tail [claimed him] —
she spoke willfully to <s>Vinatā</s>: '<s>Kadrū</s>, [let us wager a] statement: if

children.text: satyaṃ dāsī tavāhaṃsyāmanyathātvaṃ mameti ca // PS_2,4.49 //
children.translated_text: it is true, I shall become your slave; otherwise, you [shall become] mine.'
'Today and through the night and tomorrow' — the two went to their houses.

children.text: tadbālanailyavarṇye tu sutānāha ca sādhavaḥ // PS_2,4.50 //
children.translated_text: Then the dark-colored children, regarding the tail — she said to her sons: 'O good ones,
hang upon the tail by the fire of your flames — it will not shine, O [sons]!'

children.text: krūrāhayāstathākṛtvā tā cakrurmātṛ kiṃ karīm // PS_2,4.51 //
children.translated_text: The cruel serpents, having done so — they made their mother [win]. What does a slave-maker do?
The cursed serpents — by <s>Śeṣa</s>'s words, recognizing their own inability,

children.text: jñātvā dadurjaratkāroḥ sanāmnīṃ bhaginīṃ muneḥ // PS_2,4.52 //
children.translated_text: they gave [to the sage] <s>Jaratkāru</s> their sister, named Saṃnāmnī, as [wife] of the sage.
Though dispassionate, he, entreated by his tormented, hopeless ancestors dwelling in hell,

children.text: pitṛbhiḥ prārthito gṛhṇaṃstadgarbhe tvāstikaṃ vyadhāt // PS_2,4.53 //
children.translated_text: accepting [her], he placed <s>Āstīka</s> in her womb.
He practiced great austerity to abandon her; she awakened him for the <s>Sandhyā</s> (twilight worship).

children.text: nidrābhaṅgakarā gacchetyāhu tatyāja tāṃ muniḥ // PS_2,4.54 //
children.translated_text: She who disturbs sleep — 'Go!' they said — the sage abandoned her.
Having reached her brother, she gave birth [to a son] wearing the top-knot and the sacred thread.

children.text: sa āpadi smṛto yāmītyuktogānmātulaṃ prati // PS_2,4.55 //
children.translated_text: He, when remembered in distress — being told 'Go to your maternal uncle' — went.
<s>Vāsuki</s>, having reached <s>Naimiṣa</s>, [received] ambrosia in the churning of nectar.

children.text: śaptā hīnā tātvikāno tenātyanvipa saṃmatāḥ // PS_2,4.56 //
children.translated_text: The cursed, diminished, real (<s>tāttvika</s>) [serpents] — by him, they were greatly honored.
<s>Takṣaka</s>, due to the curse of <s>Śṛṅgin</s>, bit <s>Parīkṣit</s>.

children.text: śaśāsa pṛthivīṃ tasya sutaḥ sa janamejayaḥ // PS_2,4.57 //
children.translated_text: The earth was ruled by his son, <s>Janamejaya</s>.
Then <s>Udaṅka</s>, the disciple of <s>Gālava</s>, who delighted in service,
[told his guru] 'I shall give even a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (gift)' — he, angered, commanded him,
'[Obtain] the unobtainable — from the wife of King <s>Pauṣya</s>, get the excellent earrings!'

children.text: ityuktogāt puraṃ tasya mārge gomayabhakṣaṇam // PS_2,4.59 //
children.translated_text: Thus instructed, he went to his city; on the road, he ate cow-dung.
Without performing <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping), having seen the king, he asked: 'Ask your beautiful wife!'

children.text: yācayetyāha tāṃ gehe henāyasya śaptumārabhat // PS_2,4.60 //
children.translated_text: 'Ask [her]!' he said. In the house — one destitute [person] — she began to curse the king.

children.text: nṛpaṃ na śapa māṃ brahman śuddhaḥ paśyasi bhāminīm /
children.translated_text: 'Do not curse the king, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! You are pure — see the beautiful lady!'

children.text: tata ācamya gatvā tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ prāpa saṅkuṇḍale // PS_2,4.61 //
children.translated_text: Then, having performed <s>ācamana</s> and going, having seen her, he obtained the earrings.

children.text: sāha pūrve takṣakāyemādāmāyā ca tepi ca /
children.translated_text: She said: 'These earrings were previously desired by <s>Takṣaka</s>; I gave them, and they too [wanted them];
I, a faithful wife, not to be challenged — neither <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) has the power [to take them].'

children.text: yato bhaveti taṃ prāhagurubhaktaṃ na mā spṛśet /
children.translated_text: 'Since you are [devoted]' — she told him — 'the one devoted to the guru shall not be touched [by harm].'

children.text: ityuktau yācitaḥ pauṣyādbhuñjan śrāddhānnagaṃ kacam // PS_2,4.63 //
children.translated_text: Thus told, he requested [food] from <s>Pauṣya</s>; while eating the <s>Śrāddha</s>-food, a hair
having been seen — 'May you become blind!' he cursed. And he too cursed the sage:

children.text: apatnī kosīti rājye lokasyāndhopi paśyasi // PS_2,4.64 //
children.translated_text: 'May you be without a wife!' 'In your kingdom, even a blind one can see' [said the king].

children.text: iti datvā varaṃ vipro yayau mārgetha takṣakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, having given the boon, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> departed. On the road, then, <s>Takṣaka</s>,

children.text: śiṣyo bhūtvā granthivāhaḥ soviśacca rasātalam // PS_2,4.65 //
children.translated_text: becoming a disciple, as the knot-bearer (<s>Granthivāha</s>), entered <s>Rasātala</s>.
The sage, by the power of <s>yoga</s>, went there by the serpent way.
Below, for the one who had become blind, he applied cow's urine to his eyes.
Then, seeing — the king of serpents, in fear, gave the pair of earrings.
Having taken those, having given them to the guru, he went angrily to <s>Janamejaya</s>.

children.text: taṃ prāhatvaṃ vṛthājāto pitṛmṛtyuṃ na cāvadhīḥ /
children.translated_text: He said to him: 'You were born in vain — you did not avenge the death of your father!
I shall be the reciter of <s>mantras</s>; prepare the materials quickly!
Without <s>Śeṣa</s>, I shall make all the worlds free of serpents!'
Having said this, through the serpent-sacrifice, hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of serpents
he killed; <s>Śakra</s> came; <s>Takṣaka</s> and others did not fall.

children.text: tato ṛṣiḥ sahendrotra takṣakaḥ patatāmiti // PS_2,4.70 //
children.translated_text: Then the <s>ṛṣi</s> [said]: 'Together with <s>Indra</s>, let <s>Takṣaka</s> fall!'
And offered an oblation saying 'for <s>Takṣaka</s> together with <s>Indra</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!'
Then heaven trembled; the <s>Nāgas</s> remembered the sage <s>Āstīka</s>.
He, out of fear, being honored by the king even with water — <s>Āstīka</s> —
his desired water came to <s>Janamejaya</s>.
'I shall give whatever is requested' — when this was declared — 'Grant the life of my maternal uncle!'
Thus he rescued <s>Takṣaka</s> and the rest from untimely death.
She (<s>Vinatā</s>), having meditated upon the water, assigned to <s>Takṣaka</s> and the rest the [nature of] slaying.

children.text: yajñaprāpya phalaṃ rājñe datvā sarpān athāśapat // PS_2,4.74 //
children.translated_text: Having given the fruit of the sacrifice to the king, then she cursed the serpents:
'Do not bite the guiltless! From the remembrance of me, O <s>Nāgas</s>,

children.text: anyathā vaḥ śiraḥ śīrṇaṃ bhavediti yayau muniḥ // PS_2,4.75 //
children.translated_text: otherwise, your head shall be shattered!' — thus the sage departed.
<s>Vinatā</s>, weary from service, while pregnant, struck her womb.
Those born prematurely — the great thighs and back, without thighs and feet.
'I shall give you my power in time' — having told the mother, the wise pre-born one,
speaking, departed, and stood upon the chariot of the sun.
In <s>Saudāminī</s>, his two sons were <s>Sampāti</s> and <s>Jaṭāyu</s>.

children.text: kālena garuḍo jāto viṣṇorvāho babhūva ha // PS_2,4.78 //
children.translated_text: In time, <s>Garuḍa</s> was born and became the vehicle of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
At his father's words, for obtaining strength, he devoured the elephant and the tortoise —
formerly on Mount <s>Gandhamādana</s>, they were <s>Gandharvas</s> born from a curse.
Against the sons of <s>Kadrū</s> and the great <s>Tamas</s> — if [they would give] the ambrosia in the cup —

children.text: dāsyānmokṣe mātaraṃ ca ityepāstu na cādhikam // PS_2,4.80 //
children.translated_text: 'He shall release [my] mother from servitude in [the course of obtaining] liberation' — these alone [are his conditions], and nothing more. (PS 2.4.80)
Thus addressed, [<s>Garuḍa</s>] took the nectar and gave it; from servitude he liberated [her];
from servitude, [he freed] his own mother. The gods, having gone to heaven, (PS 2.4.81)

children.text: prākṣipatṛṇavataṃ ca vidhūya ca sudhāṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: cast [the serpents] aside like straw and reclaimed the nectar again;

children.text: śakroyadāpa ca svargaṃ(śakrāyadādāpasakhya) tasya kardrumathāvadat // PS_2,4.82 //
children.translated_text: when <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) obtained heaven, <s>Kadru</s> then said: (PS 2.4.82)
'Whence was the nectar stolen?' When asked, the son of <s>Vinatā</s> [said]:,

children.text: mātā tvayā vañcitā me mayā tvaṃ tena vañcitaḥ // PS_2,4.83 //
children.translated_text: 'My mother was deceived by you; by me, you were deceived in return. (PS 2.4.83)
She said "give" [for the] nectar — "make [them] drink" was not said — therefore it was [rightly] taken;'

children.text: tadādi garuḍaḥ sarpān vañcakān hantumārabhat // PS_2,4.84 //
children.translated_text: from then on, <s>Garuḍa</s> began to kill the deceitful serpents. (PS 2.4.84)
<s>Kadru</s>, from treachery against the foremost, became afflicted with grief for [her] sons;

children.text: vañcakāste patan yajñe tadanye garuḍāśinaḥ // PS_2,4.85 //
children.translated_text: the deceitful ones perish in the sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>); the others are food for <s>Garuḍa</s>. (PS 2.4.85)
Those who arose after that, having given tribute to him, survive in entirety;
'Who, being without offense, being guileless — I would be eager to live, (PS 2.4.86)

children.text: ihāmutrāpi duḥkhaṃ te yogyā api bhavanti hi /
children.translated_text: here and hereafter [facing] suffering — even the fit ones become [thus];

children.text: kimayogyā rākṣasāstu viśanti tama ūrjitam // PS_2,4.87 //
children.translated_text: what of the unfit? The <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons) enter dense darkness.' (PS 2.4.87)
Thus, from <s>Śeṣa</s>'s proximity-service, from drinking nectar,
from friendship with <s>Garutmat</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), from devotion to the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>, from devotion to the teacher, (PS 2.4.88)
from sincerity, from being a believer, from [<s>Śeṣa</s>'s] boon, from being a servant of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) —

children.text: mātuḥ śāpaṃ tṛṇīkṛtya sukhamāpuḥ sa pannagāḥ // PS_2,4.89 //
children.translated_text: disregarding the mother's curse like a blade of grass, those serpents attained happiness. (PS 2.4.89)
'What is unattainable in the world through the service of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>?'

children.text: mahātale tu(ku) sarpāṇāṃ sthānaṃ vipati bibhratam // PS_2,4.90 //
children.translated_text: In <s>Mahātala</s>, there is indeed the abode of the serpents who bear the hoods [even] in calamity. (PS 2.4.90)

children.text: śivasya varatonyeṣu caranto yānti dur(gar)matiḥ // PS_2,4.91 //
children.translated_text: By <s>Śiva</s>'s boon, the others who wander [freely] go to a wicked state. (PS 2.4.91)
Thus, in the <s>Śrī Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, in the second section, the fourth chapter.
The glorious Lord said:
In <s>Rasātala</s>, [situated] below, the <s>Dānavas</s> (titans), numbering hundreds of <s>koṭis</s>,
the <s>Daityas</s> (demons), <s>Yātudhānas</s> (sorcerers), <s>Paulomas</s>, and <s>Kālakeyas</s> — (PS 2.5.1)
the <s>Nivātakavacas</s> (armor-clad demons), bold, and the <s>Rākṣasas</s> and <s>Surāṇakas</s>,
the <s>Piśācas</s> (ghouls), <s>Antyajas</s> (outcasts), and those of bloody [nature] — greatly wicked-minded, decrepit — (PS 2.5.2)
they dwell [there] out of fear of the discus (<s>cakra</s>) of <s>Hari</s> and fear of everything;
whatever <s>sāttvika</s> ones are there, excellent among the gods, they dwell together. (PS 2.5.3)
In each <s>Manvantara</s>, all of these, in this land of <s>Bhārata</s>,
having corrupted and brought down <s>Hari</s>'s [devotees], the righteous, the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, cows, women, and the other <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life) — (PS 2.5.4)
some, completely perverted in intellect, having defiled and brought down [others],

children.text: nitye vasanti narake hatā haryādi daiḥdvagddha // PS_2,5.5 //
children.translated_text: dwell in eternal hell, slain and burned by <s>Hari</s> and the others. (PS 2.5.5)
Those of eternally evil means, again taking refuge in <s>Rasātala</s>,
having been on earth, causing harm to the worlds through boons from <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Rudra</s> — (PS 2.5.6)
slain by all <s>avatāras</s>, by <s>Rāma</s> and also by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, all of them

children.text: vasanti nityanarake kālādyāsyanti vai tamaḥ // PS_2,5.7 //
children.translated_text: dwell in eternal hell; in time, they shall go to darkness. (PS 2.5.7)
There indeed, the she-dog named <s>Saramā</s>, arisen from <s>Brahmā</s>'s boon,

children.text: sadārtān bhīṣayanti daityān yamasya vaśavartinī // PS_2,5.8 //
children.translated_text: always frightens the afflicted <s>Daityas</s>, being subject to <s>Yama</s>'s authority. (PS 2.5.8)
The <s>Daityas</s> there, their lifespan exhausted, seeing the <s>Sudarśana</s> [discus] in a dream,

children.text: mṛtāyāsyanti narakaṃ tadvaṃśyā(syā)nāṃ sa āśrayaḥ(maḥ) // PS_2,5.9 //
children.translated_text: die and go to hell; <s>Rasātala</s> is the refuge of their descendants. (PS 2.5.9)
Below that, in <s>Pātāla</s>, in the shining northern direction,
<s>Śeṣa</s>, of a thousand faces, with all the <s>sāttvika</s> serpents — (PS 2.5.10)
worshipped by all <s>Nāga</s> (serpent) maidens, in a jeweled pavilion,
meditating on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the Lord, he always dwells, together with the immortals. (PS 2.5.11)
Blazing with the radiance of a thousand suns, adorned with a row of crowns,
with splendor exceeding <s>koṭis</s> of the brilliance of the full autumn moon — (PS 2.5.12)
adorned with the circle of hoods that eternally drip nectar, pure,

children.text: sadaikakuṇḍalo bhāsvan musalaḥ sahalaḥ prabhuḥ // PS_2,5.13 //
children.translated_text: with a single earring always shining, bearing a pestle (<s>musala</s>) and a plough (<s>hala</s>), the Lord — (PS 2.5.13)
the gem-radiance of <s>Śrī</s> on the crown atop his head dispels all diseases,
with necklaces, anklets, bracelets, armlets, rings, and the like — (PS 2.5.14)
the Lord, with crown-threads shining with many excellent gems and the like,
with sandals covered by the gems of the crowns of gods and <s>asuras</s> — (PS 2.5.15)
fragrant with sandal, garlands, and the like, meditating, he sits — the cosmic form (<s>virāṭ</s>) himself;

children.text: pātāladakṣiṇe bhāge saṃya(mya)minyāṃ puraḥ prabhuḥ // PS_2,5.16 //
children.translated_text: in the southern part of <s>Pātāla</s>, in the city of <s>Saṃyaminī</s>, the Lord — (PS 2.5.16)
beloved of <s>Śyāmalā</s>, bearing a staff, riding a buffalo,
<s>Samavartī</s> <s>Yama</s>, lord of the dead, with the appearance of a mountain of dark collyrium — (PS 2.5.17)
endowed with all ornaments, the <s>Dharmarāj</s> (King of Righteousness), meditating on <s>Rāma</s>;
the son of the Sun — and there, <s>Citra</s> and <s>Citragupta</s>, the two record-keepers — (PS 2.5.18)
by whose command, the accumulation of merit and sin arising from <s>Bhārata</s> —
there, the <s>Dharma</s>-speakers, stationed in their respective <s>Manvantaras</s> — (PS 2.5.19)
the <s>Ṛṣis</s> (sages), all the gods and sub-gods are his attendants;
with upward-standing hair, deformed eyes, of dark color, terrifying — (PS 2.5.20)
the servants of his command, his agents (<s>kiṅkaras</s>), bearing nooses in hand,
cruel, pitiless, fierce, bearing great iron clubs in hand — (PS 2.5.21)
they bind the sinners from <s>Bhārata</s> and bring them to <s>Yama</s>'s presence;
they number ten <s>lakṣas</s> (one million); those terrible ones, with beatings and scorchings — (PS 2.5.22)
they drag these sinners who have committed evil along the terrible path;

children.text: sa tānabhyagatān dṛṣṭvā yamadaṇḍaṃ paretarāṭ // PS_2,5.23 //
children.translated_text: seeing those who have arrived, the king of the departed, with <s>Yama</s>'s staff — (PS 2.5.23)

children.text: teṣāṃ mūrdhni sthāpayati yātanā dehināṃ tadā /
children.translated_text: he places [it] on their heads; then [comes] the torment of the embodied ones;

children.text: puṇyapāpāni te sarve kīrtayanti kṛtāni ca // PS_2,5.24 //
children.translated_text: they all declare the merits and sins they have committed. (PS 2.5.24)
There, all those of truthful nature stand and say 'It is true';

children.text: patreṣu tāni(ḷḥi) likhitānyapi te prapaṭhanti ca // PS_2,5.25 //
children.translated_text: and they also read out those written on leaves. (PS 2.5.25)
The foremost sages declare the fruit consisting of happiness and suffering;
the messengers of <s>Yama</s>, numbering ten <s>lakṣas</s>, [cast them] into hell — (PS 2.5.26)
having thrown [them in], they beat [them] according to [their] sins;
twenty <s>lakṣas</s> (two million) in number, the presiders over diseases are always there — (PS 2.5.27)
they are [diseases of] wind (<s>vāta</s>), bile (<s>pitta</s>), phlegm (<s>śleṣma</s>), and the like — combined fevers and the like,
fistula, dysentery, vomiting, loss of appetite, bad wounds — (PS 2.5.28)
colds, nasal congestion, deafness, heart disease and the like, near him;
they dwell [there], bestowing the fruit of sin, sometimes causing the destruction of the body. (PS 2.5.29)
Those in the forms of dogs, snakes, scorpions, biting-flies, poison, and evil wolves —
twenty <s>lakṣas</s>, they are the tormentors of those fallen into hell. (PS 2.5.30)
In <s>Pātāla</s> dwell these hells of many forms:
<s>Durgati</s> (Bad-fate), <s>Niraya</s> (Perdition), <s>Mahāraurava</s> and <s>Raurava</s> (the Great and Lesser Howling), (PS 2.5.31)
<s>Saṃghāta</s> (Crushing), called <s>Kālasūtra</s> (Thread-of-Time), called <s>Avīci</s> (Waveless), <s>Anirodha</s> (Obstruction),
<s>Tailayantra</s> (Oil-press), <s>Taptataila</s> (Hot-oil), <s>Giripāta</s> (Mountain-fall), and <s>Ayaḥśālā</s> (Iron-house); (PS 2.5.32)
<s>Sūci</s> (Needle), <s>Agni</s> (Fire), <s>Bhūrinirghāta</s> (Great-crushing), <s>Vakrakaṇṭaka</s> (Crooked-thorn), and <s>Dānava</s> (Demon);
<s>Śvabhojana</s> (Dog-food), <s>Vratapana</s> (Scorching-vow), <s>Karkaśa</s> (Harsh), <s>Alimukha</s> (Bee-face), and <s>Ulbaṇa</s> (Violent); (PS 2.5.33)
[hells of] pus, blood, urine, feces as food; [hells of] embracing heated weapons;
<s>Kālakūṭa</s> (Death-poison), <s>Agniśakala</s> (Fire-fragment), <s>Sarvaśastrāstrapātana</s> (All-weapons-falling); (PS 2.5.34)
<s>Prāṇarodha</s> (Breath-obstruction), <s>Mahābhāra</s> (Great-burden), <s>Krūrāśīviṣa</s> (Cruel-viper), and <s>Vṛścika</s> (Scorpion);
<s>Sarvāṅgacheda</s> (All-limb-cutting), <s>Ātmamāṃsa</s> (Own-flesh), <s>Taptavṛkṣābhipātana</s> (Heated-tree-falling); (PS 2.5.35)
the two <s>Śūlāroha</s> (Stake-mounting) and <s>Apakarṣa</s> (Dragging-down), <s>Durgandha</s> (Foul-smell), <s>Rākṣasādana</s> (Demon-dwelling);
<s>Bāṇāghāta</s> (Arrow-strike), <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> (the river), <s>Śaṅkamūla</s> (Bone-root), and <s>Karāla</s> (Dreadful); (PS 2.5.36)
[hells of] ants, leeches, and the like as food; vultures, herons, and the like as food;
the two <s>Āvartana</s> (Whirling) and <s>Asphālana</s> (Dashing), <s>Śilāyantra</s> (Stone-press), and <s>Śilādana</s> (Stone-eating); (PS 2.5.37)
<s>Karṇavastupūrṇa</s> (Ear-filled) and the two <s>Dvārakṣepaṇa</s> (Gate-throwing) and <s>Bandhana</s> (Binding);
<s>Śṛṅkhalā</s> (Chains), <s>Taptasikatā</s> (Hot-sand), <s>Sphuliṅga</s> (Sparks), and <s>Avadhūlaya</s> (Shaking); (PS 2.5.38)
[hells of striking] head, vital points, joints, deceit, and water-obstruction, and the like;
there exist one hundred and eight hells, abodes of sin. (PS 2.5.39)
These are the non-eternal hells; <s>Tāmiśra</s> (Darkness) and <s>Andhatāmiśra</s> (Blind-darkness) —

children.text: nityau dvau narakau tatra gatāyānti tamaḥ kramāt // PS_2,5.40 //
children.translated_text: these two are the eternal hells; those who go there proceed to darkness in sequence. (PS 2.5.40)
The gods in the lower worlds, in all <s>Manvantaras</s>,
engaged in the previously stated functions, without alternative names — (PS 2.5.41)
the names and forms of the unfit ones stated here are altogether;
here indeed, in the previous <s>Manus</s>' [times], they were given the designation 'command-bearers.' (PS 2.5.42)
All of these, at the dissolution of a <s>Manu</s>-period, abandoning their gross [bodies], subtly,
subject to their own <s>Prājña</s> [form], they go to <s>Maharloka</s>; at its end — (PS 2.5.43)

children.text: prāpyasthūlāni ṛṣibhiḥ svapūrvaṃ pātike(prāntike) kramāt // PS_2,5.44 //
children.translated_text: obtaining gross [bodies], with the <s>Ṛṣis</s>, in their own former [order], at the conclusion, in sequence. (PS 2.5.44)
Thus, in the <s>Śrī Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, in the second section, the fifth chapter.
The glorious Lord said:
The seven worlds beginning with <s>Atala</s> are proclaimed as the subterranean heavens (<s>bila-svargas</s>);

children.text: meroradhastātte sarve prāyaśo jñāni saṅkulāḥ // PS_2,6.1 //
children.translated_text: they are all below <s>Meru</s>, mostly filled with knowledgeable beings. (PS 2.6.1)
Above these is the Earth-world (<s>Bhūloka</s>), considered the lowest of all worlds;

children.text: tasmin hi bhārate varṣe barhiṣmattākhyapattane // PS_2,6.2 //
children.translated_text: in that land of <s>Bhārata</s>, in the city called <s>Barhiṣmatī</s> — (PS 2.6.2)
<s>Manu Svāyambhuva</s>, the husband of <s>Śatarūpā</s>, formerly existed;
his lotus-feet attended by many <s>koṭis</s> of divine servants — (PS 2.6.3)
he always ruled this earth, an ocean of offspring;
<s>Devahūti</s>, his daughter, once went to the upper story [of the palace]. (PS 2.6.4)
Seeing her, the chief of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, overcome with desire, fell to the earth;
placing her, endowed with beauty and youth, on his own chariot — (PS 2.6.5)

children.text: bhāryayā saha tatrāgāt sarasvatyāṃ taṭaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: together with his wife, he went there, to the bank of the <s>Sarasvatī</s> river;
there, on the bank of <s>Bindusaras</s> (Lake Bindu), [he gave her] to <s>Kardama</s>, who was performing austerity. (PS 2.6.6)

children.text: puṇyāśramaṃ pradatvāttu manuḥ kṛchrāt svakaṃ puram /
children.translated_text: <s>Manu</s>, having given [her to] his holy hermitage, with difficulty [returned to] his own city;

children.text: gate rājani sā devī vastrābharaṇasañcayam // PS_2,6.7 //
children.translated_text: when the king had departed, that goddess, [casting aside] the collection of garments and ornaments — (PS 2.6.7)
having thrown [them] into the river, wearing bark, braided [hair], and deer-hide garments,
emaciated from vows, she served her husband with devotion, wearing matted locks. (PS 2.6.8)
Thus, [<s>Kardama</s>], his feet served by her, addressed the king's daughter;

children.text: hitaṃ vadeti sā devī(vavre) taṃ tu yogaprabhāvataḥ // PS_2,6.9 //
children.translated_text: 'Speak what is beneficial' — that goddess chose him, through the power of <s>yoga</s>. (PS 2.6.9)
For the purpose of union, [he manifested] a radiant [palace] endowed with the splendor of rising jewels,
furnished with all amenities, filled with birds, trees, and water. (PS 2.6.10)
Golden, moving through time [i.e., flying], fragrant, supremely charming;

children.text: svayaṃ tadāhṛde snātvā babhau sarvamanoharaḥ // PS_2,6.11 //
children.translated_text: having himself bathed in the lake there, he appeared captivating to all minds. (PS 2.6.11)
She too, adorned with the beauty, garments, and ornaments of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) herself;

children.text: tuṣṭvā sa satayā sārdhaṃ remebdaśatakaṃ ṛṣiḥ // PS_2,6.12 //
children.translated_text: pleased, the sage sported with her for one hundred years. (PS 2.6.12)
Traveling in <s>Meru</s> and the like, situated in a divine aerial chariot, as if liberated,
with beautiful sounds, touches, tastes, forms, and fragrances, captivating the mind — (PS 2.6.13)
he passed the time as if [it were] a moment, with the breezes of springtime;
thus, on the bank of <s>Bindusaras</s>, these women approached him. (PS 2.6.14)

children.text: tatputrikānāṃ nāmāni śruṇu me vadataḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Hear the names of his daughters, as I always declare:

children.text: kalānasūyā śraddhā ca havirbhūśca gatiḥ kriyā // PS_2,6.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kalā</s>, <s>Anasūyā</s>, <s>Śraddhā</s>, <s>Havirbhū</s>, <s>Gati</s>, <s>Kriyā</s>, (PS 2.6.15)
<s>Arundhatī</s>, <s>Citti</s>, and <s>Khyāti</s> — the daughters of <s>Kardama</s>;
he gave <s>Kalā</s> to <s>Marīci</s>, and <s>Anasūyā</s> to <s>Atri</s>. (PS 2.6.16)
He gave <s>Śraddhā</s> to <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Havirbhū</s> to <s>Pulastya</s>;

children.text: pulahāya gatiṃ prādāt kratave sakriyāṃ sutām // PS_2,6.17 //
children.translated_text: he gave <s>Gati</s> to <s>Pulaha</s>, and his daughter <s>Kriyā</s> to <s>Kratu</s>. (PS 2.6.17)
He gave <s>Arundhatī</s> to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and offered <s>Citti</s> to <s>Bhṛgu</s>;

children.text: atharvaṇāya ca khyātiṃ datvā hṛṣṭo babhūva ha // PS_2,6.18 //
children.translated_text: having given <s>Khyāti</s> to <s>Atharvaṇa</s>, he became delighted. (PS 2.6.18)

children.text: tataḥ śatābdaṃ cikrīḍya tatosyāṃ kapilaṃ vyadhāt /
children.translated_text: Then, having sported for a hundred years, he begot <s>Kapila</s> in her;

children.text: sa kardama tapoyogāt sākṣānnārāyaṇo bhavat // PS_2,6.19 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Kardama</s>, through the power of austerity and <s>yoga</s>, became directly <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> [i.e., attained <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>]. (PS 2.6.19)

children.text: tyaktvā vimānaṃ bhāryāṃ ca kardamastapase yayau /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the aerial chariot and his wife, <s>Kardama</s> went for austerity,
a lifelong celibate (<s>autpattika brahmacārī</s>), on that bank of <s>Bindusaras</s>. (PS 2.6.20)
The sage <s>Kapila</s>, having taught the truth (<s>tattva</s>) to his own mother, gave [her] liberation.
That principle, taught by <s>Kapila</s>, cuts the knots of <s>karma</s>. // PS_2,6.21 //
From <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s> was born — here, in the <s>Vaivasvata</s> <s>Manvantara</s> (era);
of the reborn <s>Dakṣa</s>, among his thirteen daughters, // PS_2,6.22 //
those given to <s>Kaśyapa</s> — <s>Diti</s>, <s>Aditi</s>, and the others —
the previously mentioned sons were [born]; in the previous <s>Manvantaras</s>, he // PS_2,6.23 //
<s>Kaśyapa</s> by name, in different [forms], was the son of <s>Marīci</s>;
by another wife too, the sixty daughters born of <s>Dakṣa</s> — // PS_2,6.24 //
in each <s>Manvantara</s>, thirteen were given to <s>Kaśyapa</s>;
they, under different names, gave birth to gods and <s>Asuras</s>. // PS_2,6.25 //
The previously mentioned [beings], under different names, each accomplishing their respective functions;
in this [Manvantara], he bore the name <s>Kaśyapa</s> — wives, sons, and the rest are now // PS_2,6.26 //
called by the names of their previously stated functions; in the future time-period likewise.
He is the <s>tātvika</s> (genuine) sage; from <s>Puṣkara</s> and others, the hundred lesser [sages] were produced. // PS_2,6.27 //
The daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s> [born] of <s>Aja</s> (Brahmā), in the previous <s>Manvantaras</s> also,
twenty-seven in number, became the wives of the Moon. // PS_2,6.28 //
They, the stars beginning with <s>Aśvinī</s>, are the activators of the wheel of time;
due to [the Moon's] partiality toward <s>Rohiṇī</s>, he turned unfavorably toward the others; // PS_2,6.29 //
by <s>Dakṣa's</s> curse they remained childless in all <s>Manvantaras</s>;

children.text: bhūtāṅgirakṛśāśvebhyo dve dve datte ca bhānujāḥ // PS_2,6.30 //
children.translated_text: to <s>Bhūta</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and <s>Kṛśāśva</s>, two each were given — [their children were] the daughters of the Sun. // PS_2,6.30 //
Of the Suns and the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), [the list of] human [rulers] ---------

children.text: dattāścataśro dakṣāya daśadharmāya tāsu vai // PS_2,6.31 //
children.translated_text: four were given to <s>Dakṣa</s>, ten to <s>Dharma</s> — among them indeed, // PS_2,6.31 //
sons were mostly born, presiding over knowledge, devotion, and the like.
<s>Candra</s> (Moon), born from <s>Atri's</s> eye, in all <s>Manvantaras</s>, // PS_2,6.32 //
is the lord of trees, herbs, and <s>nakṣatras</s>;
the maker of night, the cool-rayed one, the remover of heat, always the giver of happiness. // PS_2,6.33 //
The one of immortal rays, the lord of the seat of food, born of the ocean, brother of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī),
the lord of the waxing digits, <s>Śaśāṅka</s> (Hare-marked), the kinsman of the world. // PS_2,6.34 //
In the sons of <s>Anasūyā</s> and <s>Atri</s> — <s>Datta</s> and <s>Durvāsas</s> — both [were born];
the activator of <s>yoga</s>, through <s>yoga</s>, devoted to <s>Brahman</s>, celibates. // PS_2,6.35 //
<s>Datta</s> is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> himself; <s>Durvāsas</s> is a portion of <s>Śaṅkara</s>;
of extremely fierce anger, worshipped by <s>Pṛthā</s> (<s>Kuntī</s>), he instructed <s>Manu</s>. // PS_2,6.36 //
By him indeed, being greatly worshipped, [<s>Kuntī</s>] bore three [sons]: <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Dharma</s>[-rāja], and the others;
from <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, on the <s>dvādaśī</s> (twelfth day [of the fortnight]) with little [food] remaining, [<s>Durvāsas</s>] was requested to eat. // PS_2,6.37 //

children.text: omityuktvā tu kālindyāṃ magno nāgācciraṃ nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having said 'Om' and plunging into the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā), the king did not come for a long time;
by the instruction of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, with water he performed the <s>pāraṇa</s> (breaking of the fast), desiring [to complete] the observance. // PS_2,6.38 //
Knowing that, [<s>Durvāsas</s>] directed a <s>kṛtyā</s> (magical creature) at the king; but [the king] remembered <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: pūrvamāptaṃ hareścakraṃ kṛtyāṃ hatvā vibhīṣayat // PS_2,6.39 //
children.translated_text: the disc of <s>Hari</s>, previously obtained, having killed the <s>kṛtyā</s>, terrified [<s>Durvāsas</s>]. // PS_2,6.39 //

children.text: sa ṛṣiḥ sarvalokeśaiḥ viṣṇunā ca nirākṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: That sage was rejected by all the lords of the worlds and by <s>Viṣṇu</s>;

children.text: ambarīśaṃ prāpya tena mocito bhojitobhyagāt // PS_2,6.40 //
children.translated_text: reaching <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, he was released by him, fed, and went his way. // PS_2,6.40 //
That <s>Durvāsas</s>, having reached <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, begged <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>):

children.text: sadyonnaṃ dīyatāmahyam iti taistuṣṭa āvrajat // PS_2,6.41 //
children.translated_text: 'Give me food at once!' — and they, pleased, gave; and he departed. // PS_2,6.41 //
<s>Aṅgiras</s>, with faith, obtained [as] teacher <s>Agni</s>, named <s>Ucathya</s>;
the sons of <s>Saṃvartaka</s>-fire and the previously mentioned [sages] were of the teacher's [lineage]. // PS_2,6.42 //
On earth, desiring to sport with the wife of <s>Ucathya</s>,
of [the sage] performing long austerity in the womb — from his foot, on the ground which was covered, // PS_2,6.43 //
from the semen that fell, was born a sage, supremely righteous —

children.text: bharadvājo marudbhiḥ sa pālitobhūt purā kila // PS_2,6.44 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bharadvāja</s>; he was nurtured by the <s>Maruts</s> (Wind-gods) in ancient times. // PS_2,6.44 //
In the <s>Vaivasvata Manvantara</s>, in the lunar dynasty, when the one named <s>Bharata</s>

children.text: niḥsantāne sati tadā marutastasya taṃ daduḥ // PS_2,6.45 //
children.translated_text: was without offspring, then the <s>Maruts</s> gave him that [child]. // PS_2,6.45 //
He was adopted; [later] he was raised up and released.
Again he practiced austerity for a long time; then, in the lineage of <s>Bharata</s>, // PS_2,6.46 //
when <s>Śantanu</s> was practicing austerity on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
from the sight of <s>Ūrvaśī</s>, <s>Bharadvāja's</s> [semen] was spilled — // PS_2,6.47 //

children.text: reto dadhāra droṇī(ṇe) saḥ tasmādroṇo bhavadguruḥ /
children.translated_text: he held the semen in a <s>droṇī</s> (trough); from that, <s>Droṇa</s> was born, [who became] a teacher;

children.text: tasmāt kṛpī śaṅkarāṃśamaśvatthāmā samāpa hi // PS_2,6.48 //
children.translated_text: from him [and] <s>Kṛpī</s>, <s>Aśvatthāmā</s>, a portion of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, was obtained. // PS_2,6.48 //

children.text: bṛhaspatestu tārābhyāṃ kaca āsīt sutaḥ purā /
children.translated_text: From <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and <s>Tārā</s>, <s>Kaca</s> was the son in former times;
in the <s>Vaivasvata Manvantara</s>, he became the pupil of <s>Śukra</s>, a treasure of austerity. // PS_2,6.49 //

children.text: niṣiddhā tena sā vidyā nasyātta iti śāsayat /
children.translated_text: That knowledge was forbidden to him by [<s>Śukra</s>], who commanded: 'It shall perish from you!';
'May you not become a husband, being afflicted by desire!' — knowing this, the sage cursed [him]. // PS_2,6.50 //
He obtained the <s>Mṛtasañjīvinī</s> (spell of reviving the dead) — having gone from there at some point,
[<s>Kaca</s>] desired union with <s>Devayānī</s>, the daughter of his teacher, in the forest. // PS_2,6.51 //
'Being a student together, your husband shall be of a non-twice-born [caste]!' —
thus [she] said; therefore, in the disciples of the poet [<s>Śukra</s>], this [curse] became additionally [effective]. // PS_2,6.52 //
that [princess, <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>] and no other — during water-play with [<s>Devayānī</s>], // PS_2,6.53 //
<s>Devayānī</s>, placed in the heart of the king's daughter, [caused] friction with [<s>Śukra's</s>] disciple;
through wearing [<s>Devayānī's</s>] own garment, [<s>Devayānī</s>] who was thrown [into a well] became distressed;
<s>Devayānī</s>, [fallen] into the lake, [had] her garment taken by the king's daughter. // PS_2,6.54 //
When the king's daughter had gone, [<s>Yayāti</s>] came before [<s>Devayānī</s>];
<s>Yayāti</s>, born in the lunar dynasty, was roaming then for hunting. // PS_2,6.55 //

children.text: tāṃ vivastrāṃ samudhṛtya svottarīyaṃ dadau nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having lifted her up unclothed, the king gave her his upper garment;

children.text: taṃ dhṛtvā sā gṛhaṃ prāparājāgāt svapuraṃ tadā // PS_2,6.56 //
children.translated_text: having taken it, she went home; the king went to his own city then. // PS_2,6.56 //

children.text: tadarthaṃ kupitaṃ śukraṃ rājānatvā prasādya ca /
children.translated_text: For her sake, having propitiated the angered <s>Śukra</s> and [obtained his consent],
the king appointed his own daughter as a servant to the teacher's daughter. // PS_2,6.57 //

children.text: śukro yayāti nṛpateḥ kanyāṃ svāṃ pradadau mudā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śukra</s> gave his daughter to King <s>Yayāti</s> with joy,

children.text: dāsyā śarmiṣṭayā yuktāṃ dāsī rājñe bhavet satī // PS_2,6.58 //
children.translated_text: accompanied by the servant <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> — the servant-girl became [a wife] to the king too. // PS_2,6.58 //
<s>Yadu</s> was the son from <s>Devayānī</s>; his dynasty [included] the descendant of <s>Kṛtavīrya</s> —

children.text: arjuno yo daśagrīvaṃ nigṛhya punarāpa tat // PS_2,6.59 //
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s> (<s>Kārtavīrya</s>), who having captured <s>Daśagrīva</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), again obtained that [power]. // PS_2,6.59 //
He was seized by <s>Dattātreya</s> — the thousand-armed one was clearly [blessed];
in his dynasty, from an <s>Apsaras</s>-born [ancestor], from <s>Vasudeva</s>, <s>Hari</s> was born. // PS_2,6.60 //
Thus, in the <s>Prakāśasaṃhitā</s>, the sixth chapter of the second section.
